posterior transverse collateral sulcus.d: Posterior transverse branch of the collateral sulcus.

(abdominal part of pectoralis major musc.d: The lowest fibres, arising from the aponeurosis of external oblique; they form the anterior fold of the axilla.

(adductor minimus).d: The separate uppermost fibres of adductor magnus.

(anteromedial basal segmental bronchus o.tr: (anteromedial basal segmental bronchus of left lung)

(communicating branch of median nerve wi.d: Connection between the median and ulnar nerves in the palm (a Riche–Cannieu-type anastomosis).

(deep branch of transverse cervical arte.tr: Deep branch of transverse cervical artery (dorsal scapular artery)
(deep branch of transverse cervical arte.d: Supplies the rhomboids and joins the scapular anastomosis.

(iliopectineal bursa).d: Large bursa between the iliopsoas tendon and the hip capsule; it may communicate with the hip joint.

(opponens digiti minimi muscle of foot).d: Inconstant fibres of flexor digiti minimi brevis extending to the 5th metatarsal.

(superficial branch of transverse cervic.tr: Superficial branch of transverse cervical artery

(ulnar recurrent artery).d: Branch that runs back up to the anastomosis around the elbow.

????????.d: Small venous segment opening into the coronary sinus.

?x.tr: Branch of artery of pterygoid canal
?x.d: Small branch of the artery of the pterygoid canal.

abdominal aorta.d: Runs from T12 to its bifurcation at L4; gives the coeliac trunk and the mesenteric, renal and gonadal arteries. Its aneurysms are most often infrarenal.

abducens nerve (vi).d: Supplies lateral rectus; because of its long course it is the nerve most often affected by raised intracranial pressure.

abductor digiti minimi of foot.d: Muscle on the lateral border of the sole; lateral plantar nerve.

abductor digiti minimi of hand.d: Superficial muscle of the hypothenar eminence; abducts the little finger. Ulnar nerve.

abductor hallucis.d: Muscle on the medial border of the sole; abducts the big toe and supports the medial arch. Medial plantar nerve.

abductor pollicis brevis.d: Superficial muscle of the thenar eminence; moves the thumb away from the palm at a right angle. Median nerve (recurrent branch); it wastes in carpal tunnel syndrome.

abductor pollicis longus.d: Inserts into the base of the 1st metacarpal; abducts the thumb. Its tendon runs in the 1st extensor compartment (De Quervain's tenosynovitis).

accessory branch of middle meningeal art.tr: Accessory branch of middle meningeal artery
accessory branch of middle meningeal art.d: Small branch that may enter the skull through the foramen ovale.

accessory hemi-azygos vein.d: Collects the upper and middle left intercostal veins.

accessory nerve (xi).d: Supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius; being superficial in the posterior triangle, it can be injured in surgery (drooping shoulder).

accessory nucleus of oculomotor nerve.d: Parasympathetic nucleus supplying the pupillary sphincter and ciliary muscle (light and accommodation reflexes).

acetabular fossa.d: Non-articular floor of the acetabulum; contains fat and the ligament of the head of the femur.

acetabular labrum.d: Fibrocartilaginous ring around the rim of the acetabulum; it deepens the socket and holds the femoral head by suction. A tear causes groin pain.

acetabular margin.d: Rim of the acetabulum; the acetabular labrum attaches here and deepens the socket.

acetabular notch.d: Notch in the lower rim of the acetabulum; bridged by the transverse acetabular ligament, vessels pass through it.

acetabulum.d: Socket of the hip bone; formed by the union of ilium, ischium and pubis, it receives the femoral head.

acromial angle.d: Posterolateral corner of the acromion; a reference point for measuring arm length.

acromial end.d: Flattened lateral end of the clavicle; forms the acromioclavicular joint with the acromion.

acromial facet.d: Small articular facet at the lateral end; articulates with the acromion.

acromial part of deltoid muscle.d: Middle, multipennate fibres; abduct the arm from 15° up to 90°.

acromioclavicular ligament.d: Superior capsular thickening of the acromioclavicular joint; the first ligament to tear in the grading of shoulder separations.

acromion.d: Lateral end of the spine of the scapula; the highest point of the shoulder, it articulates with the clavicle.

adductor brevis.d: Muscle lying behind adductor longus; the anterior and posterior branches of the obturator nerve run in front of and behind it.

adductor longus.d: Runs from the body of the pubis to the linea aspera; forms the medial border of the femoral triangle. It is the muscle most often injured in groin strains.

adductor magnus.d: The largest adductor; its adductor part is supplied by the obturator nerve, its hamstring part by the tibial nerve. Through the adductor hiatus in its tendon the femoral vessels pass to the popliteal fossa.

adductor pollicis.d: Deep hand muscle with oblique and transverse heads; brings the thumb towards the palm. Ulnar nerve (deep branch).

adductor tubercle.d: Small prominence above the medial epicondyle; the hamstring part of adductor magnus attaches to it.

ala of ilium.d: Broad wing of the ilium; the iliac fossa lies on its inner surface and the gluteal muscles on its outer surface.

ala of sacrum.d: Lateral wing of the sacrum; the lumbosacral trunk passes in front of it.

ampulla of lacrimal canaliculus.d: Dilatation at the end of the vertical part of the canaliculus.

amygdaloid body.d: Group of nuclei in the anteromedial temporal lobe; the centre of fear and emotional memory. Bilateral damage causes Klüver–Bucy syndrome.

anatomical neck of humerus.d: Constriction just below the articular cartilage of the humeral head; the capsule attaches here.

anconeus muscle.d: Small triangular muscle from the lateral epicondyle to the olecranon; assists elbow extension. Radial nerve.

angle of rib.d: Point where the rib curves forwards at the back; the commonest site of rib fractures.

angular artery.d: Terminal branch of the facial artery at the medial angle of the eye; anastomoses with the ophthalmic artery.

angular gyrus.d: Gyrus capping the end of the superior temporal sulcus (Brodmann 39); linked to reading and writing; dominant-side damage causes Gerstmann syndrome.

angular vein.d: Connects with the superior ophthalmic vein at the medial angle of the eye.

annular epiphysis.d: Bony ring around the upper and lower surfaces of a vertebral body.

annular ligament of radius.d: Ring holding the radial head against the radial notch of the ulna; in pulled elbow in young children the head slips out of this ring.

anserine bursa.d: Beneath the sartorius, gracilis and semitendinosus tendons; its inflammation causes pain on the lower medial side of the knee.

antebrachial fascia.d: Deep fascia enclosing the forearm; it thickens towards the wrist to form the retinacula.

anterior arch of atlas.d: Short anterior arch of the atlas; on its inner surface is a facet that articulates with the dens.

anterior articular facet of dens axis.d: Front surface of the dens; articulates with the anterior arch of the atlas.

anterior basal segment of left lung (svi.tr: Anterior basal segment of left lung (sviii)

anterior basal segment of right lung (sv.tr: Anterior basal segment of right lung (sviii)

anterior basal segmental artery of left.tr: Anterior basal segmental artery of left lung
anterior basal segmental artery of left.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis sinistri
anterior basal segmental artery of left.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

anterior basal segmental artery of right.tr: Anterior basal segmental artery of right lung
anterior basal segmental artery of right.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis dextri
anterior basal segmental artery of right.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

anterior basal segmental bronchus of lef.tr: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (bviii)
anterior basal segmental bronchus of lef.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis anterior (B VIII) sinister

anterior basal segmental bronchus of rig.tr: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (bviii)
anterior basal segmental bronchus of rig.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis anterior (B VIII) dexter

anterior belly of digastric muscle.d: Runs from the digastric fossa of the mandible to the intermediate tendon; supplied by the nerve to mylohyoid (V3), it opens the mouth.

anterior border of fibula.d: Anterior border of the fibula; the septum separating the anterior and lateral compartments attaches to it.

anterior border of tibia.d: Sharp anterior border felt under the skin (the shin).

anterior branch of medial antebrachial c.tr: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
anterior branch of medial antebrachial c.la: Ramus anterior nervi cutanei antebrachii medialis
anterior branch of medial antebrachial c.d: Supplies the skin of the anteromedial forearm.

anterior branch of obturator nerve.d: Supplies adductor longus, adductor brevis and gracilis, and the skin of the inner thigh.

anterior branch of renal artery.d: Branch to four segments of the kidney; the segmental arteries are end arteries.

anterior cells of ethmoid bone.d: Anterior air cells of the ethmoidal labyrinth; they open into the middle meatus.

anterior cerebral artery.d: Supplies the medial surface of the hemisphere; its occlusion causes marked weakness and sensory loss in the opposite leg.

anterior chamber of eyeball.d: Space between the cornea and the iris filled with aqueous humour; fluid drains at its angle (Schlemm's canal), and closure of the angle is acute glaucoma.

anterior circumflex humeral artery.d: Winds round the front of the surgical neck of the humerus.

anterior circumflex humeral vein.d: Accompanies the artery of the same name.

anterior clinoid process.d: Backward-projecting tip of the lesser wing; the tentorium cerebelli attaches to it and it lies beside the internal carotid artery.

anterior cochlear nucleus.d: One of the first brainstem relay nuclei of the auditory fibres.

anterior commissure.d: Fibre bundle joining the temporal lobes and olfactory structures; it lies in the lamina terminalis.

anterior communicating artery.d: Joins the two anterior cerebral arteries; the commonest site of aneurysms (can cause a bitemporal visual field defect).

anterior corticospinal tract.d: Uncrossed corticospinal fibres; they cross at segmental level and go to the trunk muscles.

anterior cruciate ligament.d: Runs from the anterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the inner surface of the lateral femoral condyle; prevents forward sliding of the tibia. Often torn in sports injuries (anterior drawer, Lachman test).

anterior cutaneous branches of femoral n.tr: Anterior cutaneous branches of femoral nerve
anterior cutaneous branches of femoral n.d: Sensation from the skin of the front and inner thigh.

anterior division of inferior trunk of b.d: Division that forms the medial cord.

anterior division of internal iliac arte.tr: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
anterior division of internal iliac arte.d: Gives the visceral branches (umbilical, vesical, uterine/rectal) and the obturator, internal pudendal and inferior gluteal arteries.

anterior division of mandibular nerve.d: Mostly motor division; gives branches to the muscles of mastication and the buccal nerve.

anterior division of middle trunk of bra.d: Division that joins the lateral cord.

anterior division of superior trunk of b.d: Anterior division that joins the lateral cord.

anterior ethmoidal artery.d: Supplies the anterior ethmoidal cells and the front of the nasal cavity.

anterior fasciculus proprius.d: Short fibres linking spinal cord segments (anterior funiculus).

anterior gluteal line.d: Anterior line on the outer surface of the ilium; separates the origins of gluteus medius and minimus.

anterior horn of spinal cord.d: Grey matter containing the lower motor neurons; damaged in poliomyelitis and ALS.

anterior inferior cerebellar artery.d: Lower branch of the basilar artery; gives the labyrinthine artery.

anterior inferior iliac spine.d: Projection below the ASIS; the straight head of rectus femoris and the iliofemoral ligament attach to it.

anterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal ar.d: Branch supplying the front of the head of the pancreas.

anterior intercavernous sinus.d: Joins the two cavernous sinuses in front of the pituitary.

anterior intercondylar area.d: Anterior area between the condyles; the anterior cruciate ligament and the anterior horns of the menisci attach to it.

anterior intermuscular septum of leg.d: Fascial wall separating the anterior and lateral compartments.

anterior interosseous nerve of forearm.d: Deep branch of the median nerve; supplies FPL, the radial half of FDP and pronator quadratus. After injury the 'OK' sign cannot be made.

anterior interventricular artery.d: Descends in the anterior interventricular groove to the apex; supplies the anterior 2/3 of the septum and the anterior wall of the left ventricle. The coronary artery most often occluded ('widow maker').

anterior jugular vein.d: Descends in the front of the neck close to the midline.

anterior layer of thoracolumbar fascia.d: Layer covering the front of quadratus lumborum.

anterior ligament of fibular head.d: Ligament reinforcing the superior tibiofibular joint in front.

anterior longitudinal ligament.d: Broad ligament running along the front of the vertebral bodies from the skull base to the sacrum; limits hyperextension.

anterior median fissure of medulla oblon.tr: Anterior median fissure of medulla oblongata

anterior meniscotibial ligament (lateral.d: Ligament attaching the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus to the tibia.

anterior meniscotibial ligament (medial.d: Ligament attaching the anterior horn of the medial meniscus to the tibia.

anterior obturator tubercle.d: Prominence on the anterior margin of the obturator foramen.

anterior occipital sulcus*.d: Sulcus at the boundary of the occipital and temporal lobes.

anterior papillary muscle of right ventr.tr: Anterior papillary muscle of right ventricle
anterior papillary muscle of right ventr.d: The largest papillary muscle of the right ventricle; linked to the moderator band, it holds the tricuspid cusps through the chordae tendineae.

anterior process of calcaneus.d: Front end of the calcaneus; articulates with the cuboid and can fracture in ankle sprains.

anterior process of malleus.d: Thin process projecting forwards from the neck of the malleus.

anterior quadrangular lobule.d: Hemispheric part of the anterior lobe; part of the spinocerebellum.

anterior root of posterior femoral cutan.tr: Anterior root of posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
anterior root of posterior femoral cutan.la: Radix anterior nervi cutanei femoris posterioris
anterior root of posterior femoral cutan.d: Root of the nerve coming from the anterior divisions.

anterior root of spinal nerve.d: Root carrying motor and (at T1–L2 and S2–S4) autonomic fibres.

anterior sacral foramina.d: Anterior sacral foramina; the anterior rami of the sacral nerves emerge through them.

anterior sacro-iliac ligament.d: Thin capsular thickening in front of the sacroiliac joint.

anterior segment of eyeball.d: Structures in front of the lens (cornea, anterior and posterior chambers, iris).

anterior segmental artery of left lung.tr: Anterior segmental artery of left lung
anterior segmental artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

anterior segmental artery of right lung.tr: Anterior segmental artery of right lung
anterior segmental artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

anterior segmental bronchus of left lung.tr: Anterior segmental bronchus of left lung (biii)

anterior segmental bronchus of right lun.tr: Anterior segmental bronchus of right lung (biii)

anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.tr: Anterior semilunar cusp of pulmonary valve
anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.la: Valvula semilunaris anterior valvae trunci pulmonalis
anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.d: The anterior semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve.

anterior septal branches of anterior eth.tr: Anterior septal branches of anterior ethmoidal artery
anterior septal branches of anterior eth.d: Supply the anterosuperior part of the nasal septum.

anterior spinal artery.d: Formed by branches of both vertebral arteries; supplies the anterior 2/3 of the spinal cord. When it is occluded, dorsal column sensation is spared.

anterior spinocerebellar tract.d: Carries unconscious proprioception from the lower limb to the cerebellum through the superior cerebellar peduncle.

anterior sternoclavicular ligament.d: Anterior capsular thickening of the joint.

anterior superior iliac spine.d: Front end of the iliac crest; the inguinal ligament, sartorius and TFL attach to it and it is easily felt.

anterior surface of petrous part.d: Surface of the petrous part facing the middle cranial fossa; bears the trigeminal impression and the arcuate eminence.

anterior surface of radius.d: Anterior surface of the radius; FPL and pronator quadratus arise here.

anterior talocalcaneal ligament.d: Ligament in front of the subtalar joint.

anterior talofibular ligament.d: Runs from the lateral malleolus to the neck of the talus; the first and most often torn ligament in inversion sprains.

anterior temporal branch.d: Supplies the front of the temporal lobe.

anterior tibial artery.d: Passes over the interosseous membrane into the anterior compartment; becomes the dorsalis pedis at the ankle.

anterior tibial veins.d: Accompanies the artery of the same name.

anterior tibiofibular ligament.d: Ligament holding the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis in front; it tears in 'high ankle sprains'.

anterior tubercle of atlas.d: Prominence on the front of the anterior arch; longus colli and the anterior longitudinal ligament attach to it.

anterior tubercle of transverse process.d: Anterior prominence of a cervical transverse process; at C6 the carotid tubercle (Chassaignac) can be felt.

anterior vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

anterior vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

anterolateral surface of arytenoid carti.d: Anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; the vestibular ligament and thyroarytenoid attach here.

anterolateral surface of humerus.d: Anterolateral surface of the humerus; the deltoid tuberosity lies here.

anteromedial surface of fibula.d: Anteromedial surface of the fibula; the anterior compartment muscles arise here.

anteromedial surface of humerus.d: Anteromedial surface of the humerus; coracobrachialis and brachialis attach here.

aortic arch.d: Curves backwards over the left bronchus at T4; gives the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries.

apex of arytenoid cartilage.d: Tip of the arytenoid; the corniculate cartilage sits on it and it contributes to the aryepiglottic fold.

apex of coccyx.d: Tip of the coccyx; the external anal sphincter and anococcygeal ligament attach to it.

apex of dens axis.d: Tip of the dens; the apical ligament runs from here to the anterior margin of the foramen magnum.

apex of head of fibula.d: Tip of the fibular head; the lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris tendon attach near it.

apex of petrous part.d: Medial tip of the petrous part; bounds the foramen lacerum and lies near the trigeminal ganglion.

apex of sacrum.d: Lower end of the sacrum; articulates with the coccyx.

apical segmental artery of left lung.tr: Apical segmental artery of left lung
apical segmental artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

apical segmental artery of right lung.tr: Apical segmental artery of right lung
apical segmental artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

apical segmental bronchus of right lung.tr: Apical segmental bronchus of right lung (bi)

apical vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

apicoposterior segmental bronchus of lef.tr: Apicoposterior segmental bronchus of left lung (bi+bii)

apicoposterior vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

appendicular artery.d: End artery running along the edge of the mesoappendix; ligated in appendicectomy.

aqueduct of midbrain.d: Narrow canal joining the third and fourth ventricles; its obstruction causes obstructive hydrocephalus.

arch of cricoid cartilage.d: Narrow anterior arch of the cricoid; felt in the neck below the thyroid cartilage.

arcuate artery.d: Branch forming an arch over the bases of the metatarsals on the dorsum of the foot.

arcuate crest.d: Curved ridge on the anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; separates the upper and lower pits.

arcuate eminence.d: Bulge produced by the anterior semicircular canal.

arcuate line of ilium.d: Curved line on the inner surface of the ilium; part of the boundary of the pelvic inlet.

arcuate popliteal ligament.d: Ligament arching from the fibular head over the posterolateral capsule; the popliteus tendon passes beneath it.

artery of central sulcus.d: Supplies the face and arm areas of the motor and sensory cortex.

artery of pterygoid canal.d: Thin branch passing through the pterygoid canal.

articular capsule of acromioclavicular j.d: Capsule of the plane joint between the lateral end of the clavicle and the acromion.

articular capsule of elbow joint.d: Capsule enclosing the humero-ulnar, humeroradial and proximal radio-ulnar joints together.

articular capsule of glenohumeral joint.d: Loose capsule from the glenoid rim to the anatomical neck of the humerus; it is weakest inferiorly, so most dislocations are anteroinferior.

articular capsule of hip joint.d: Strong capsule from the acetabulum to the femoral neck; it attaches to the intertrochanteric line in front and to the middle of the neck behind.

articular capsule of interphalangeal joi.tr: Capsule of interphalangeal joint of big toe
articular capsule of interphalangeal joi.d: Capsule of the single interphalangeal joint of the big toe.

articular capsule of knee joint.d: Capsule enclosing the largest synovial cavity in the body; it is completed in front by the patella and patellar ligament and extends upwards as the suprapatellar recess.

articular capsule of radiocarpal joint.d: Capsule of the ellipsoid joint between the radius and TFCC and the proximal row of carpals.

articular capsule of sternoclavicular jo.d: Capsule of the only true joint between the upper limb and the trunk.

articular capsule of superior tibiofibul.d: Capsule of the plane joint between the fibular head and the lateral condyle of the tibia.

articular capsule of temporomandibular j.d: Loose capsule enclosing the articular tubercle and fossa of the temporal bone and the mandibular condyle.

articular capsules of distal interphalan.tr: Capsules of distal interphalangeal joints of hand
articular capsules of distal interphalan.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum distalium manus
articular capsules of distal interphalan.d: Capsules of the joints between the middle and distal phalanges; Heberden's nodes appear here in osteoarthritis.

articular capsules of distal interphalan.tr: Capsules of distal interphalangeal joints of foot
articular capsules of distal interphalan.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum distalium pedis
articular capsules of distal interphalan.d: Capsules of the joints between the middle and distal phalanges of the toes.

articular capsules of metacarpophalangea.d: Capsules of the ellipsoid joints at the bases of the fingers; ulnar deviation develops at these joints in rheumatoid arthritis.

articular capsules of metatarsophalangea.d: Capsules of the ellipsoid joints between the metatarsal heads and proximal phalanges; the 1st joint is deformed in hallux valgus.

articular capsules of proximal interphal.tr: Capsules of proximal interphalangeal joints of hand
articular capsules of proximal interphal.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum proximalium manus
articular capsules of proximal interphal.d: Capsules of the hinge joints between the proximal and middle phalanges; swan-neck and boutonnière deformities involve this joint.

articular capsules of proximal interphal.tr: Capsules of proximal interphalangeal joints of foot
articular capsules of proximal interphal.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum proximalium pedis
articular capsules of proximal interphal.d: Capsules of the hinge joints between the proximal and middle phalanges of the toes; a flexion contracture develops in hammer toe.

articular circumference of head of radiu.d: Rim of the radial head; it rotates within the radial notch of the ulna and the annular ligament.

articular circumference of head of ulna.d: Surface of the ulnar head that articulates with the ulnar notch of the radius.

articular disc of acromioclavicular join.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc that may be present in the joint; often incomplete and degenerates with age.

articular disc of distal radio-ulnar joi.tr: Articular disc of distal radio-ulnar joint (TFCC)
articular disc of distal radio-ulnar joi.d: Triangular fibrocartilage separating the ulnar head from the wrist joint; it is the centre of the TFCC, and a tear causes ulnar-sided wrist pain.

articular disc of sternoclavicular joint.d: Disc dividing the joint into two cavities; prevents the clavicle from sliding medially.

articular disc of temporomandibular join.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc dividing the joint into upper (gliding) and lower (hinge) cavities; the upper head of lateral pterygoid attaches to it. Anterior displacement causes a 'click'.

articular facet for malleus.d: Surface of the body of the incus that articulates with the head of the malleus.

articular facet for stapes.d: Surface of the lenticular process of the incus that articulates with the head of the stapes.

articular facet of head of fibula.d: Articular surface of the fibular head; forms the proximal tibiofibular joint with the tibia.

articular facet of head of malleus.tr: Articular facet of head of malleus
articular facet of head of malleus.d: Surface of the head of the malleus that articulates with the incus.

articular facet of head of radius.d: Upper concavity of the radial head; articulates with the capitulum of the humerus.

articular facet of head of stapes.tr: Articular facet of head of stapes
articular facet of head of stapes.d: Surface of the head of the stapes that articulates with the incus; stapedius attaches close by.

articular facet of lateral malleolus.d: Inner surface of the lateral malleolus; takes part in the ankle joint with the talus.

articular facet of medial malleolus.d: Surface of the medial malleolus that articulates with the talus.

articular facet of tubercle of rib.tr: Articular facet of tubercle of rib
articular facet of tubercle of rib.d: Surface of the tubercle that articulates with the transverse process.

articular facets of head of rib.tr: Articular facets of head of rib
articular facets of head of rib.d: Surfaces of the rib head that articulate with two adjacent vertebral bodies.

articular surface for cuboid.d: Saddle-shaped articular surface at the front of the calcaneus; forms the calcaneocuboid joint.

articular surface of arytenoid cartilage.d: Base surface forming the cricoarytenoid joint with the cricoid lamina; opening and closing of the vocal folds takes place at this joint.

articular surface of medial condyle.d: Oval surface of the medial condyle that articulates with the femur.

articularis genus muscle.d: Deep fibres of vastus intermedius; during knee extension they pull the suprapatellar bursa upwards so it is not trapped.

ary-epiglottic part of oblique arytenoid.d: Fibres running in the aryepiglottic fold; they narrow the laryngeal inlet during swallowing.

arytenoid articular surface.d: Articular surface on the upper border of the cricoid lamina; articulates with the arytenoids.

arytenoid cartilage.d: Paired pyramid-shaped cartilage on the cricoid lamina; the vocal ligament attaches to its vocal process, and its rotation and gliding open and close the glottis.

ascending aorta.d: The part that rises from the left ventricle inside the pericardium; its only branches are the coronary arteries. Type A dissection starts here.

ascending branch of left colic artery.tr: Ascending branch of left colic artery
ascending branch of left colic artery.d: Anastomoses with the middle colic artery towards the splenic flexure.

ascending part of trapezius muscle.d: Lower fibres from the lower thoracic spines to the spine of the scapula; depress and upwardly rotate the scapula.

ascending pharyngeal artery.d: Thin branch supplying the pharyngeal wall.

atlas (c1).d: Ring-shaped first cervical vertebra that carries the skull; it has no body and no spinous process. Its superior articular facets form with the occipital condyles the atlanto-occipital joint, which produces the 'yes' movement.

auditory tube.d: Connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx and equalises pressure; short and horizontal in children, so otitis media is common.

auricular surface of ilium.d: Ear-shaped articular surface; forms the sacroiliac joint with the sacrum.

auricular surface of sacrum.d: Ear-shaped surface forming the sacroiliac joint with the ilium.

axillary artery.d: Runs from the outer border of the 1st rib to the lower border of teres major; divided into three parts by pectoralis minor.

axillary nerve.d: Arises from the posterior cord, passes through the quadrangular space and winds around the surgical neck of the humerus; supplies deltoid and teres minor. Can be injured in shoulder dislocation and neck fracture (sensory loss over the 'badge' area).

axillary vein.d: Formed by the union of the basilic and brachial veins.

axis (c2).d: The atlas rotates around the dens (odontoid process) projecting up from its body; half of the 'no' movement takes place at the atlanto-axial joint. Dens fractures and the hangman's fracture are typical.

azygos vein.d: Rises on the right of the spine in the posterior mediastinum and arches at T4 into the superior vena cava; a collateral route when the IVC is blocked.

base of arytenoid cartilage.d: Broad base of the arytenoid; the vocal process projects forwards and the muscular process laterally.

base of coccyx.d: Upper surface of the coccyx; articulates with the apex of the sacrum.

base of mandible.d: Lower border of the body of the mandible; the facial artery pulse can be felt here.

base of metatarsal bone.d: Proximal end of a metatarsal; articulates with the tarsal bones and neighbouring metatarsals.

base of peduncle.d: Anterior part of the midbrain carrying corticospinal and corticobulbar fibres; its damage causes contralateral hemiplegia in Weber syndrome.

base of phalanx of foot.d: Proximal end of a toe phalanx; articulates with the bone before it.

base of phalanx of hand.d: Proximal end of a finger phalanx; articulates with the metacarpal head or the preceding phalanx.

base of sacrum.d: Upper surface of the sacrum; articulates with L5 and bears the promontory at its front.

base of stapes.d: Base of the stapes; it sits in the oval window and transmits vibration to the inner ear.

basilar artery.d: Artery in the groove on the front of the pons; supplies the brainstem and cerebellum and divides at its top into the posterior cerebral arteries. Its occlusion can cause locked-in syndrome.

basilar part of occipital bone.d: Thick part in front of the foramen magnum (clivus); the brainstem rests on it.

basilic vein.d: Rises on the inner side of the arm; preferred for PICC lines.

biceps brachii muscle.d: Inserts into the radial tuberosity and, through the bicipital aponeurosis, into the forearm fascia; a powerful supinator and elbow flexor. Musculocutaneous nerve; biceps reflex C5–C6.

biceps femoris muscle.d: Lateral hamstring whose long and short heads insert into the fibular head; flexes the knee and rotates the leg laterally when the knee is bent.

bicipitoradial bursa.d: Between the biceps tendon and the radial tuberosity; reduces friction of the tendon during pronation.

bifurcation of pulmonary trunk.d: Where the trunk divides into right and left branches; joined to the aortic arch by the ligamentum arteriosum. A massive pulmonary embolus can form a 'saddle thrombus' here.

biventral lobule.d: Two-bellied lobule of the inferior hemisphere.

body of clavicle.d: Body of the clavicle; S-shaped, it most often fractures in its middle third.

body of femur.d: Shaft of the femur; the linea aspera runs on its posterior surface, and fractures can cause major blood loss.

body of fibula.d: Thin shaft of the fibula; it does not bear weight but provides attachment for muscles.

body of humerus.d: Shaft of the humerus; the radial nerve runs in the groove on its posterior surface.

body of hyoid bone.d: Central body of the hyoid; the suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles attach to it.

body of ilium.d: Body of the ilium contributing to the acetabulum.

body of incus.d: Body of the incus; articulates with the head of the malleus.

body of ischium.d: Body of the ischium contributing to the acetabulum.

body of mandible.d: Horseshoe-shaped body of the mandible; carries the lower teeth.

body of metatarsal bone.d: Shaft of a metatarsal; stress fractures from walking are most common here.

body of phalanx of hand.d: Shaft of a finger phalanx; its front surface carries the sheath of the flexor tendons.

body of pubis.d: Midline body of the pubis; forms the symphysis with the opposite side.

body of radius.d: Shaft of the radius; it curves slightly outwards, which aids supination.

body of rib.d: Thin, curved shaft of the rib.

body of sphenoid bone.d: Cube-shaped body of the sphenoid; it contains the sphenoidal sinus and bears the sella turcica above.

body of sternum.d: Longest part of the sternum; articulates with the 2nd–7th costal cartilages. Its junction with the manubrium (sternal angle) marks the 2nd rib and the T4–T5 level.

body of talus.d: Main mass of the talus; the trochlea lies on top of it.

body of tibia.d: Shaft of the tibia; triangular in cross-section, its anteromedial surface lies just under the skin.

body of ulna.d: Shaft of the ulna; its posterior border can be felt under the skin.

bones of hand.d: The 27 bones of the hand: 8 carpal bones, 5 metacarpals and 14 phalanges.

brachial artery.d: Runs in the medial bicipital groove of the arm; heard when measuring blood pressure and divides at the elbow into the radial and ulnar arteries. Can be injured in supracondylar fractures (Volkmann's contracture).

brachial fascia.d: Deep fascia enclosing the arm; with the intermuscular septa it forms the anterior and posterior compartments.

brachial veins.d: Paired veins accompanying the brachial artery.

brachialis muscle.d: Main flexor of the elbow, running from the lower anterior half of the humerus to the ulnar tuberosity. Musculocutaneous nerve (and partly the radial nerve).

brachiocephalic trunk.d: First branch of the aortic arch; divides behind the right sternoclavicular joint into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.

brachioradialis muscle.d: Runs from the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus to the radial styloid process; flexes the half-pronated forearm. Although supplied by the radial nerve, it is a flexor.

branch to angular gyrus.d: Terminal branch supplying the angular gyrus.

branches of anterior part of lumbar plex.tr: Branches of the anterior part of the lumbar plexus

branches of posterior part of lumbar ple.tr: Branches of the posterior part of the lumbar plexus

buccal artery.d: Supplies the buccinator and the mucosa of the cheek.

buccal nerve.d: Carries sensation from the skin and mucosa of the cheek (not to be confused with the facial nerve branch supplying buccinator).

bucinator.d: Muscle forming the wall of the cheek; keeps food between the teeth during chewing and tenses the cheeks when blowing. The parotid duct pierces it. Nerve: facial nerve (buccal branch).

bursa of piriformis muscle.d: Bursa between the piriformis tendon and the greater trochanter.

calcaneal branches of fibular artery.d: Supply the lateral part of the heel.

calcaneal branches of posterior tibial a.tr: Calcaneal branches of posterior tibial artery
calcaneal branches of posterior tibial a.d: Supply the medial part of the heel.

calcaneal sulcus.d: Groove on the upper surface of the calcaneus; with the groove on the talus it forms the sinus tarsi.

calcaneal tendon.d: Common tendon of gastrocnemius and soleus; the thickest and strongest tendon in the body, it inserts into the calcaneal tuberosity. Rupture is assessed with the Thompson test; it carries the S1 reflex.

calcaneal tubercle.d: Prominence on the lower front surface of the calcaneus; the plantar ligaments attach to it.

calcaneal tuberosity.d: Posterior projection of the heel; the Achilles tendon inserts here and it bears weight during standing.

calcaneocuboid ligament.d: Lateral limb of the bifurcate ligament; binds the calcaneus to the cuboid.

calcaneofibular ligament.d: Cord running from the tip of the lateral malleolus to the side of the calcaneus; in severe sprains it tears after the anterior talofibular ligament.

calcaneonavicular ligament.d: Medial limb of the bifurcate ligament; binds the calcaneus to the navicular.

calcaneus.d: Largest tarsal bone; it forms the heel, and the Achilles tendon inserts into its tuberosity. The flexor hallucis longus tendon passes beneath the sustentaculum tali.

calcarine sulcus.d: Sulcus on the medial surface of the occipital lobe surrounded by the primary visual cortex (Brodmann 17). Posterior cerebral artery occlusion causes hemianopia with macular sparing.

callosomarginal artery.d: Branch running in the cingulate sulcus.

canal for vertebral artery.d: Canal formed in some people by a bony bridge roofing the groove for the vertebral artery (ponticulus posticus).

capitate bone.d: Largest carpal bone; it lies in the middle of the distal row and articulates with the 3rd metacarpal. The axis of movement of the hand passes through it.

capitohamate interosseous ligament.d: Interosseous ligament between the capitate and the hamate.

capitulum of humerus.d: Rounded articular surface at the lower lateral end of the humerus; forms the humeroradial joint with the radial head.

carotid sulcus.d: Groove on the side of the body of the sphenoid; the internal carotid artery runs here within the cavernous sinus.

carpal articular surface.d: Lower articular surface of the radius; forms the wrist joint with the scaphoid and lunate.

carpal bones.d: Eight short bones arranged in two rows; they form the wrist between the forearm bones and the metacarpus.

cauda equina.d: Lumbar and sacral nerve roots descending from the conus medullaris; their compression causes incontinence and saddle anaesthesia and needs emergency surgery.

caudate nucleus.d: C-shaped basal nucleus following the lateral ventricle; it atrophies in Huntington disease.

cavernous sinus.d: Sinus beside the sella turcica; the internal carotid artery and abducens nerve pass through it, and CN III, IV, V1 and V2 in its wall. Its thrombosis causes multiple cranial nerve palsies.

central canal.d: Narrow canal in the middle of the spinal cord continuous with the fourth ventricle; its widening is syringomyelia.

central canal'.d: Lower part of the central canal of the spinal cord.

central lobule.d: Middle part of the anterior lobe of the vermis.

central retinal artery.d: End artery entering the optic nerve to supply the inner layers of the retina; its occlusion causes sudden painless loss of vision and a 'cherry-red spot'.

central structures of spinal cord.tr: Central structures of the spinal cord

central sulcus.d: Separates the frontal and parietal lobes, between the motor and sensory cortices.

cephalic vein.d: Rises on the lateral side of the arm and opens through the deltopectoral groove into the axillary vein; can be used for pacemaker leads.

cerebral fossa.d: Upper fossae in which the occipital lobes rest.

cerebral surface of greater wing.d: Surface of the greater wing facing the middle cranial fossa; the temporal lobe rests against it.

cervical vertebra.d: Neck vertebra; its transverse process has a foramen.

chiasmatic sulcus.d: Groove between the two optic canals; it lies next to the optic chiasm.

chorda tympani.d: Branch of the facial nerve crossing the middle ear; it joins the lingual nerve and carries taste from the anterior two thirds of the tongue and parasympathetic fibres to the submandibular and sublingual glands.

choroid plexus.d: Vascular structure in the ventricles producing cerebrospinal fluid (about 500 ml a day).

cingulate gyrus (posteroventral part*).d: Part of the cingulate gyrus passing behind the splenium into the parahippocampal gyrus.

cingulate gyrus and sulcus (middle anter.d: Middle anterior part of the limbic gyrus above the corpus callosum; linked to attention and error monitoring.

cingulate gyrus and sulcus (middle poste.d: Middle posterior part of the cingulate gyrus.

cingulate gyrus and sulcus (posterior do.d: Posterior dorsal part of the cingulate gyrus.

cingulate sulcus (marginal part*).d: Upturned posterior end of the cingulate sulcus; it bounds the paracentral lobule behind.

circumflex artery of heart.d: Winds round to the back of the heart in the left AV groove; supplies the left atrium and the lateral and posterior walls of the left ventricle.

circumflex scapular artery.d: Passes through the triangular space to join the scapular anastomosis.

circumflex scapular vein.d: Accompanies the artery of the same name.

clavicle.d: The only long bone lying horizontally, S-shaped; it acts as a strut between the sternum and scapula. It is one of the most commonly fractured bones, usually at the junction of the middle and lateral thirds.

clavicular facet.d: Small surface of the acromion that articulates with the clavicle.

clavicular head of pectoralis major musc.d: Upper fibres from the clavicle to the humerus; raise the arm forwards (flexion). Lateral pectoral nerve.

clavicular notch.d: Superolateral notch of the manubrium; forms the sternoclavicular joint with the clavicle.

clavicular part of deltoid muscle.d: Anterior fibres; raise the arm forwards and rotate it medially. Axillary nerve (C5–C6).

clavipectoral fascia.d: Fascia between the clavicle and pectoralis minor; pierced by the cephalic vein, thoracoacromial artery and lateral pectoral nerve.

coccygeal horn.d: Processes projecting upwards from the base of the coccyx; they articulate with the sacral cornua.

coccygeus muscle.d: Pelvic diaphragm muscle from the ischial spine to the edge of the sacrum and coccyx; fused with the sacrospinous ligament.

coccyx.d: Small bone usually formed by the fusion of four rudimentary vertebrae; it gives attachment to the pelvic floor muscles and the anococcygeal ligament.

cochlea.d: Organ of hearing coiled through 2.5 turns and containing the organ of Corti; its base detects high and its apex low frequencies.

cochlear nerve.d: Part carrying hearing information from the cochlea.

coeliac trunk.d: Main anterior branch of the aorta at T12; divides into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries to supply the foregut (stomach, liver, spleen, part of the pancreas).

colic branch of ileocolic artery.d: Supplies the beginning of the ascending colon.

collateral interphalangeal ligaments of.tr: Collateral ligaments of interphalangeal joints of foot
collateral interphalangeal ligaments of.d: Side ligaments of the toe joints.

collateral interphalangeal ligaments of.tr: Collateral ligaments of interphalangeal joints of hand
collateral interphalangeal ligaments of.d: Side ligaments of the finger joints.

collateral metacarpophalangeal ligaments.d: Side ligaments that tighten in flexion, which is why the hand is splinted with the MCP joints flexed. Injury of the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb is 'skier's thumb'.

collateral metatarsophalangeal ligaments.d: Side ligaments of the metatarsophalangeal joints.

collateral sulcus.d: Sulcus on the inferior surface of the temporal lobe bounding the parahippocampal gyrus laterally.

colliculus of arytenoid cartilage.d: Small prominence on the anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; where the vestibular ligament attaches.

commissural fibres of telencephalon.d: Fibres connecting the two cerebral hemispheres: the corpus callosum, anterior commissure and hippocampal commissure.

common extensor tendon.d: Common tendon of the superficial muscles of the posterior forearm arising from the lateral epicondyle; its degeneration is tennis elbow.

common facial vein.d: Union of the facial vein and the anterior division of the retromandibular vein.

common fibular nerve.d: Lateral branch of the sciatic nerve; runs superficially around the neck of the fibula and is compressed by plaster casts or crossed legs, causing foot drop.

common flexor tendon.d: Common tendon of the superficial muscles of the anterior forearm arising from the medial epicondyle; its degeneration is golfer's elbow.

common flexor tendon sheath.d: Sheath enclosing the superficial and deep finger flexor tendons in the carpal tunnel; it is continuous with the little finger sheath.

common hepatic artery.d: Runs to the right and divides into the gastroduodenal and proper hepatic arteries.

common iliac artery.d: Arises at the aortic bifurcation at L4; divides in front of the sacroiliac joint into the internal and external iliac arteries.

common iliac vein.d: The left common iliac vein can be compressed under the right common iliac artery (May–Thurner syndrome).

common interosseous artery.d: Short trunk that divides into the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.

common palmar digital arteries.d: Branches running from the superficial arch to the clefts between the fingers.

common palmar digital branches of median.tr: Common palmar digital nerves of median nerve
common palmar digital branches of median.la: Nervi digitales palmares communes nervi mediani
common palmar digital branches of median.d: Branches running in the palm towards the finger webs; they also supply the first two lumbricals.

common palmar digital branches of ulnar.tr: Common palmar digital nerve of ulnar nerve
common palmar digital branches of ulnar.la: Nervi digitales palmares communes nervi ulnaris
common palmar digital branches of ulnar.d: Branch running to the web between the ring and little fingers.

common plantar digital arteries.d: Branches running to the clefts between the toes.

common plantar digital branches of later.tr: Common plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve
common plantar digital branches of later.la: Nervi digitales plantares communes nervi plantaris lateralis
common plantar digital branches of later.d: Branches running to the lateral toe webs.

common plantar digital branches of media.tr: Common plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve
common plantar digital branches of media.la: Nervi digitales plantares communes nervi plantaris medialis
common plantar digital branches of media.d: Branches running to the toe webs; compression between the 3rd and 4th metatarsals is Morton's neuroma.

common tendinous ring.d: Fibrous ring around the optic canal and the medial part of the superior orbital fissure from which the four rectus muscles arise; the optic, oculomotor, nasociliary and abducens nerves pass through it.

common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle.tr: Common tendon sheath of fibular muscles
common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle.d: Sheath enclosing the two fibular tendons behind the lateral malleolus.

condylar canal.d: Canal behind the condyle; an emissary vein passes through it.

condyle of humerus.d: Lower end of the humerus; includes the trochlea, the capitulum and the fossae.

conoid ligament.d: Medial, cone-shaped part of the coracoclavicular ligament; attaches to the conoid tubercle of the clavicle.

conoid tubercle.d: Prominence on the lower surface of the lateral end; the conoid part of the coracoclavicular ligament attaches to it.

coraco-acromial ligament.d: Forms an arch above the humeral head between the coracoid process and the acromion; in subacromial impingement the rotator cuff is trapped under this arch.

coracobrachialis muscle.d: Runs from the coracoid process to the middle of the medial surface of the humerus; the musculocutaneous nerve pierces it.

coracohumeral ligament.d: Runs from the coracoid process to the greater and lesser tubercles; it reinforces the rotator interval and thickens in frozen shoulder.

coracoid process.d: Beak-like process of the scapula projecting forwards; pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis and the short head of biceps attach to it.

cornea.d: Transparent anterior dome of the eye; avascular, it provides most of the refraction and is densely supplied by V1.

corniculate cartilage.d: Small elastic cartilages sitting on the apex of the arytenoids; they support the aryepiglottic fold.

coronary sinus.d: Wide venous channel in the posterior AV groove of the heart; collects the cardiac veins and opens into the right atrium.

coronoid fossa.d: Anterior fossa above the trochlea; the coronoid process of the ulna enters it when the elbow is flexed.

coronoid process of ulna.d: Anterior projection of the trochlear notch; brachialis attaches to it and it can fracture in elbow dislocation.

corpus callosum.d: Largest commissure joining the two hemispheres; it consists of rostrum, genu, body and splenium. When it is cut, 'split-brain' signs appear.

corrugator supercilii.d: Draws the eyebrows medially and downwards, producing vertical wrinkles between them (frowning).

costal cartilage of eighth rib.d: False rib cartilage; it joins the cartilage above to form the costal arch.

costal cartilage of fifth rib.d: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.

costal cartilage of first rib.d: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.

costal cartilage of fourth rib.d: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.

costal cartilage of ninth rib.d: False rib cartilage; it joins the cartilage above to form the costal arch.

costal cartilage of second rib.d: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.

costal cartilage of seventh rib.d: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.

costal cartilage of sixth rib.d: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.

costal cartilage of tenth rib.d: False rib cartilage; it joins the cartilage above to form the costal arch.

costal cartilage of third rib.d: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.

costal groove.d: Groove on the inner surface of the lower border of the rib; the intercostal vein, artery and nerve run in it.

costal notches.d: Notches on the borders of the sternum; the costal cartilages articulate with the sternum here.

costal part of transverse process.d: Part of a lumbar transverse process that is a remnant of a rib.

costocervical trunk.d: Trunk giving the deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries.

costoclavicular ligament.d: Strong ligament binding the 1st costal cartilage to the lower surface of the clavicle; the most important stabiliser of the clavicle.

costotransverse ligament.d: Ligament binding the neck of the rib to the transverse process.

crest of greater tubercle.d: Ridge descending from the greater tubercle; pectoralis major attaches to it.

crest of head of rib.d: Ridge separating the two articular facets of the rib head; the intra-articular ligament attaches to it.

crest of lesser tubercle.d: Ridge descending from the lesser tubercle; teres major attaches to it.

crest of neck of rib.d: Upper border of the neck of the rib; the superior costotransverse ligament attaches to it.

cricoid cartilage.d: The only complete cartilaginous ring around the airway (at C6); narrow in front and broad behind. The trachea begins below it.

cricopharyngeal ligament.d: Ligament running from the apex of the arytenoid cartilages to the pharyngeal mucosa.

crown of tooth.d: Part of the tooth covered by enamel and visible in the mouth.

cruciform eminence.d: Cross-shaped elevation on the inner surface; the grooves of the dural sinuses meet here.

cruciform part of fibrous sheath of digi.tr: Cruciform part of digital fibrous sheath
cruciform part of fibrous sheath of digi.la: Pars cruciformis vaginae fibrosae digitorum manus
cruciform part of fibrous sheath of digi.d: Crossed bands holding the flexor tendon sheath over the joints (C pulleys); with the A pulleys they stop the tendon bowstringing away from the bone.

crural fascia.d: Deep fascia enclosing the leg; by forming the muscle compartments it is the anatomical basis of compartment syndrome.

cuboid bone.d: Tarsal bone of the lateral column; the fibularis longus tendon runs in the groove on its lower surface.

culmen.d: Highest vermian lobule of the anterior lobe.

cuneate fasciculus.d: Lateral dorsal column carrying the same senses from the upper trunk and arms (above T6).

cuneocuboid interosseous ligament.d: Interosseous ligament between the lateral cuneiform and the cuboid.

cuneometatarsal interosseous ligaments.d: Include the Lisfranc ligament from the medial cuneiform to the 2nd metatarsal; its injury leads to a Lisfranc fracture-dislocation.

cuneus.d: Triangular gyrus between the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci; it represents the lower visual field.

cusp of tooth.d: Cusps on the chewing surface of the premolars and molars.

declive.d: Vermian lobule behind the primary fissure.

deep artery of penis.d: Runs within the corpus cavernosum and gives the helicine arteries that produce erection.

deep brachial artery.d: Runs with the radial nerve in the spiral groove.

deep branch of radial nerve.d: Motor branch piercing supinator to reach the posterior compartment of the forearm.

deep branch of ulnar nerve.d: Supplies the hypothenar, interosseous and 3rd–4th lumbrical muscles and adductor pollicis.

deep cervical artery.d: Supplies the muscles of the back of the neck.

deep dorsal vein of penis.d: Opens into the prostatic venous plexus.

deep external pudendal artery.d: Deep branch supplying the skin of the perineum.

deep femoral artery.d: Main artery of the thigh muscles; gives the circumflex and perforating branches.

deep fibular nerve.d: Supplies the muscles of the anterior compartment and the skin between the 1st and 2nd toes.

deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.tr: Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis
deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.la: Caput profundum musculi flexoris pollicis brevis
deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.d: Arises from the trapezoid and capitate; usually supplied by the ulnar nerve.

deep head of pronator teres.d: Small head arising from the coronoid process; the muscle pronates the forearm. Median nerve.

deep infrapatellar bursa.d: Between the patellar ligament and the tibia.

deep palmar arch.d: Arch formed by the radial artery at the level of the bases of the metacarpals.

deep part of anterior compartment of for.tr: Deep layer of anterior forearm compartment

deep part of masseter.d: Deep, vertical fibres of masseter; close and retract the jaw.

deep part of posterior compartment of fo.tr: Deep layer of posterior forearm compartment

deep part of posterior compartment of le.tr: Deep layer of posterior leg compartment

deep part of tibial collateral ligament.tr: Deep part of medial collateral ligament
deep part of tibial collateral ligament.d: Deep fibres of the medial collateral ligament attached to the capsule and medial meniscus.

deep plantar artery.d: Passes through the 1st metatarsal space to the sole and completes the plantar arch.

deep transverse metacarpal ligament.d: Ligament binding the heads of the 2nd–5th metacarpals together; the lumbricals pass in front of it and the interossei behind.

deep transverse metatarsal ligament.d: Ligament binding the five metatarsal heads together; the interdigital nerves can be compressed beneath it (Morton's neuroma).

deep venous palmar arch.d: Accompanies the deep palmar arterial arch.

deltoid muscle.d: Triangular muscle covering the shoulder; its clavicular, acromial and spinal parts insert into the deltoid tuberosity of the humerus. Axillary nerve (C5–C6); it can be paralysed in fractures of the surgical neck.

deltoid tubercle.d: Prominence on the spine of the scapula; deltoid and trapezius attach to it.

deltoid tuberosity.d: Rough area on the lateral surface of the humeral shaft; deltoid inserts here.

dens axis.d: Tooth-like process projecting up from the axis; the atlas rotates around it, producing the 'no' movement of the head.

depressor anguli oris.d: Pulls the corner of the mouth down (sad expression).

depressor labii inferioris.d: Pulls the lower lip downwards and outwards.

depressor septi nasi.d: Pulls the tip of the nose and the septum downwards.

descending branch of lateral circumflex.tr: Descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery
descending branch of lateral circumflex.la: Ramus descendens arteriae circumflexae femoris lateralis
descending branch of lateral circumflex.d: Descends along vastus lateralis; the pedicle of the anterolateral thigh flap.

descending branch of left colic artery.tr: Descending branch of left colic artery

descending part of iliofemoral ligament.d: Medial limb of the inverted-Y (Bigelow) ligament; the iliofemoral ligament, the strongest ligament in the body, prevents hyperextension of the hip.

descending part of trapezius muscle.d: Upper fibres from the occiput and nuchal ligament to the lateral end of the clavicle; elevate and upwardly rotate the scapula. Nerve: accessory nerve (XI).

diaphragm.d: Dome-shaped main muscle of respiration separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities; when it contracts the dome descends and thoracic volume increases. Supplied by the phrenic nerve (C3–C5). Openings: vena cava (T8), oesophagus (T10), aorta (T12).

diaphragmatic fascia.d: Fascia covering the abdominal surface of the diaphragm.

digastric fossa.d: Fossa on the inner lower surface of the mandible; the anterior belly of digastric attaches here.

distal lateral striate branches.d: Perforating branches supplying the lateral part of the lentiform nucleus.

distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.d: Distal bone of the little toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

distal phalanx of fifth finger of hand.d: Distal bone of the little finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.

distal phalanx of first finger of foot.d: Distal bone of the big toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

distal phalanx of first finger of hand.d: Distal bone of the thumb; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.

distal phalanx of fourth finger of foot.d: Distal bone of the 4th toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

distal phalanx of fourth finger of hand.d: Distal bone of the ring finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.

distal phalanx of second finger of foot.d: Distal bone of the 2nd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

distal phalanx of second finger of hand.d: Distal bone of the index finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.

distal phalanx of third finger of foot.d: Distal bone of the 3rd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

distal phalanx of third finger of hand.d: Distal bone of the middle finger; its tip bears the tuberosity of the distal phalanx, which carries the nail bed.

distal surface of tooth.d: Surface of a tooth facing the back of the dental arch.

dorsal artery of penis.d: Runs on the dorsum of the penis on each side of the deep dorsal vein.

dorsal branch of ulnar nerve.d: Carries sensation from the medial part of the back of the hand; it leaves before Guyon's canal, so it is spared in canal lesions.

dorsal calcaneocuboid ligament.d: Thin ligament on the upper surface of the calcaneocuboid joint.

dorsal carpal anastomosis.d: Arterial network on the back of the wrist.

dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery.tr: Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery
dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery.d: Joins the network on the back of the wrist.

dorsal carpometacarpal ligaments.d: Bind the distal carpal row to the metacarpal bases from behind.

dorsal cuboideonavicular ligament.d: Binds the cuboid and navicular from above.

dorsal cuneocuboid ligament.d: Binds the lateral cuneiform to the cuboid from above.

dorsal cuneonavicular ligaments.d: Ligaments binding the navicular to the three cuneiforms from above.

dorsal digital arteries of foot.d: Supply the dorsal surface of the toes.

dorsal digital arteries of hand.d: Supply the dorsal surface of the fingers.

dorsal digital branches of deep fibular.tr: Dorsal digital nerves of deep fibular nerve
dorsal digital branches of deep fibular.la: Nervi digitales dorsales nervi fibularis profundi

dorsal digital branches of radial nerve.tr: Dorsal digital nerves of radial nerve
dorsal digital branches of radial nerve.d: Sensation from the back of the lateral three and a half fingers (except the nail beds).

dorsal digital branches of superficial f.tr: Dorsal digital nerves of superficial fibular nerve
dorsal digital branches of superficial f.la: Nervi digitales dorsales nervi fibularis superficialis
dorsal digital branches of superficial f.d: Sensation from the dorsal surface of the toes.

dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve.tr: Dorsal digital nerves of ulnar nerve
dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve.d: Sensation from the back of the medial fingers.

dorsal digital veins of foot.d: Drain the backs of the toes.

dorsal digital veins of hand.d: Drain the backs of the fingers.

dorsal fascia of hand.d: Fascia covering the extensor tendons on the back of the hand.

dorsal intercarpal ligaments.d: Ligaments binding the carpal bones to each other from behind.

dorsal intercuneiform ligaments.d: Bind the cuneiforms to each other from above.

dorsal interossei muscles of foot.d: Four muscles that move the toes away from the axis of the 2nd toe.

dorsal interossei muscles of hand.d: Four two-headed muscles between the metacarpals; they move the fingers away from the axis of the middle finger ('DAB'). Ulnar nerve.

dorsal metacarpal arteries.d: Arteries between the metacarpals on the back of the hand.

dorsal metacarpal ligaments.d: Bind the metacarpal bases to each other from behind.

dorsal metatarsal arteries.d: Branches from the arcuate artery to the clefts between the toes.

dorsal metatarsal ligaments.d: Bind the metatarsal bases to each other from above.

dorsal metatarsal veins.d: Open into the dorsal venous arch of the foot.

dorsal parts of lateral intertransversar.tr: Dorsal parts of lateral lumbar intertransversarii
dorsal parts of lateral intertransversar.la: Partes dorsales musculorum intertransversariorum lateralium lumborum
dorsal parts of lateral intertransversar.d: Posterior fibres of the small muscles between the lumbar transverse processes; they bend the trunk sideways.

dorsal radial tubercle.d: Lister's tubercle; the EPL tendon turns around it on its way to the thumb.

dorsal radio-ulnar ligament.d: Ligament holding the distal radio-ulnar joint from behind; part of the TFCC.

dorsal radiocarpal ligament.d: Ligament running from the radius to the proximal carpal bones at the back.

dorsal scaphotriquetral ligament.d: Dorsal intercarpal ligament running from the scaphoid to the triquetrum at the back.

dorsal scapular nerve.d: Arises from C5 and supplies the rhomboids and levator scapulae.

dorsal surface of sacrum.d: Convex posterior surface of the sacrum; the deep back muscles attach to it.

dorsal surfaces of digits of foot.tr: Dorsal surfaces of digits of foot

dorsal surfaces of digits of hand.tr: Dorsal surfaces of digits of hand

dorsal tarsometatarsal ligaments.d: Ligaments reinforcing the Lisfranc joint from above.

dorsal ulnocarpal ligament.d: Ligament running from the ulnar side to the carpal bones at the back.

dorsal venous arch of foot.d: Arch from which the great and small saphenous veins begin.

dorsal venous network of hand.d: Superficial network often used for venous cannulation.

dorsalis pedis artery.d: Its pulse is felt on the dorsum of the foot lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon.

dorsum sellae.d: Posterior wall of the sella turcica.

eighth rib.d: 8th rib: a false (vertebrochondral) rib; its cartilage joins the costal cartilage above.

eleventh rib.d: 11th rib: a floating rib; its front end is free and ends among the muscles of the abdominal wall.

epicranial aponeurosis.d: Tough tendinous layer of the scalp joining the frontal and occipital bellies; bleeding can spread in the loose layer beneath it.

erector spinae.d: Deep back muscle made up of the iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis columns; it holds the spine erect and extends it. Posterior rami of the spinal nerves.

ethmoid bone.d: Light bone forming the roof of the nasal cavity and the medial walls of the orbits; the olfactory nerves pass through the holes of the cribriform plate, and its labyrinth contains the ethmoidal cells.

ethmoidal notch.d: Gap between the orbital plates of the frontal bone; the cribriform plate of the ethmoid fits into it.

extensor carpi radialis brevis.d: Runs from the lateral epicondyle to the base of the 3rd metacarpal; degeneration of its origin tendon is tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis).

extensor carpi radialis longus.d: Inserts into the base of the 2nd metacarpal; extends the hand and deviates it radially. Radial nerve.

extensor carpi ulnaris.d: Inserts into the base of the 5th metacarpal; extends the hand and deviates it ulnarly. Posterior interosseous nerve.

extensor digiti minimi.d: Thin muscle that extends the little finger; it passes through the 5th extensor compartment.

extensor digitorum.d: Runs from the lateral epicondyle to the extensor hoods of the 2nd–5th fingers; extends the fingers. Posterior interosseous nerve.

extensor digitorum brevis.d: The only muscle group on the dorsum of the foot; extends the 2nd–4th toes. Deep fibular nerve.

extensor digitorum longus.d: Extends the 2nd–5th toes and dorsiflexes the foot. Deep fibular nerve.

extensor hallucis brevis.d: Part of extensor digitorum brevis going to the big toe.

extensor hallucis longus.d: Extends the big toe; the dorsalis pedis pulse is felt just lateral to its tendon. It is the test muscle for the L5 root.

extensor indicis.d: Muscle that extends the index finger independently; often used in tendon transfers.

extensor pollicis brevis.d: Extends the proximal phalanx of the thumb; forms the lateral border of the anatomical snuffbox.

extensor pollicis longus.d: Turns around Lister's tubercle to reach the distal phalanx of the thumb; the medial border of the snuffbox. It can rupture after a distal radius fracture.

extensor retinaculum of wrist.d: Band at the back of the wrist dividing the extensor tendons into six compartments.

external abdominal oblique muscle.d: The most superficial flat muscle of the lateral abdominal wall; its fibres run down and forwards and its lower border forms the inguinal ligament. Nerves: intercostal nerves T7–T11, subcostal nerve. It flexes the trunk and rotates it to the opposite side.

external anal sphincter.d: Voluntary ring of striated muscle around the anal canal; supplied by the pudendal nerve (inferior rectal nerve).

external carotid artery.d: Supplies most of the neck and face; it has eight branches (superior thyroid, lingual, facial, ascending pharyngeal, occipital, posterior auricular, maxillary, superficial temporal).

external iliac artery.d: Becomes the femoral artery after passing under the inguinal ligament; gives the inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac branches.

external iliac vein.d: Continuation of the femoral vein in the pelvis.

external intercostal membrane.d: Membranous continuation of the external intercostal muscle between the costal cartilages.

external intercostal muscles.d: Muscles between the ribs whose fibres run down and forwards ('hands in pockets' direction); they raise the ribs during inspiration. Intercostal nerves.

external jugular vein.d: Descends obliquely over sternocleidomastoid; becomes distended in right heart failure.

external occipital crest.d: Midline ridge running from the external occipital protuberance to the foramen magnum; the nuchal ligament attaches to it.

external occipital protuberance.d: Prominence felt in the middle of the back of the head (inion); trapezius and the nuchal ligament attach to it.

external part of thyro-arytenoid muscle.d: Muscle fibres that relax and shorten the vocal fold; the internal part is vocalis.

external pudendal veins.d: Open into the great saphenous vein.

external surface of parietal bone.d: Outer surface of the parietal bone; the temporal lines lie on it.

external surface of squamous part of fro.d: Bony surface of the forehead; the frontal sinus lies beneath it.

eyeball.d: The eyeball; formed by the sclera and cornea outside, the uvea in the middle and the retina inside.

facet for calcaneonavicular part of bifu.tr: Facet for calcaneonavicular part of bifurcate ligament
facet for calcaneonavicular part of bifu.la: Facies articularis partis calcaneonavicularis ligamenti bifurcati
facet for calcaneonavicular part of bifu.d: Articular surface on the head of the talus that the bifurcate ligament touches.

facet for dens.d: Articular surface on the back of the anterior arch of the atlas; forms the median atlanto-axial joint with the dens.

facet for plantar calcaneonavicular liga.d: Articular surface of the head of the talus that rests on the spring (plantar calcaneonavicular) ligament.

facial artery.d: Its pulse is felt at the edge of the mandible in front of masseter; it supplies the face by a tortuous course.

facial nerve (vii).d: Supplies the muscles of facial expression, taste from the anterior two thirds of the tongue, the lacrimal and salivary glands and stapedius. It leaves through the stylomastoid foramen; a peripheral palsy affects the whole half of the face (Bell's palsy).

facial vein.d: Having no valves, it lets infections of the 'danger triangle' of the face spread through the ophthalmic veins to the cavernous sinus.

falx cerebri.d: Sickle-shaped fold of dura descending between the hemispheres; it carries the superior and inferior sagittal sinuses.

fascia lata.d: Strong deep fascia that wraps the thigh like a stocking; laterally it forms the iliotibial band, and the great saphenous vein passes through its saphenous opening.

femoral artery.d: Its pulse is felt at the middle of the inguinal ligament; it passes from the femoral triangle into the adductor canal. A common access site for cardiac catheterisation.

femoral branch of genitofemoral nerve.d: Carries sensation from the skin over the femoral triangle (the afferent limb of the cremasteric reflex).

femoral nerve.d: Largest branch of the lumbar plexus, from L2–L4; supplies quadriceps, sartorius and iliacus and carries the patellar reflex. In the femoral triangle it lies lateral to the artery.

femoral vein.d: Runs medial to the artery in the femoral triangle; a common site of deep vein thrombosis.

femur.d: The longest and strongest bone in the body; its head forms the hip joint with the acetabulum and its condyles the knee joint with the tibia. If the medial circumflex femoral artery is damaged in a femoral neck fracture, avascular necrosis of the head can follow.

fibrous joints of free lower limb.tr: Fibrous joints of free lower limb

fibrous joints of free upper limb.tr: Fibrous joints of free upper limb

fibula.d: Thin lateral bone of the leg; it does not bear weight but gives attachment to muscles and, through the lateral malleolus, stabilises the ankle joint. The common fibular nerve winds around its neck.

fibular artery.d: Arises from the posterior tibial artery and descends along the fibula; the pedicle of the free fibula flap.

fibular articular facet.d: Surface of the lateral condyle that articulates with the head of the fibula.

fibular collateral ligament.d: Round cord from the lateral epicondyle of the femur to the fibular head; separate from the capsule and meniscus, it resists varus stress.

fibular notch.d: Notch at the lower end of the tibia; forms a syndesmosis with the fibula.

fibularis brevis muscle.d: Inserts into the tuberosity of the 5th metatarsal; it everts the foot. In inversion injuries it can avulse the bone fragment it attaches to.

fibularis longus muscle.d: Arises from the lateral surface of the fibula and crosses the sole through the groove of the cuboid to insert into the 1st metatarsal; it everts and plantarflexes the foot. Superficial fibular nerve.

fibularis tertius muscle.d: Separate part of extensor digitorum longus going to the 5th metatarsal; dorsiflexes and everts the foot.

fifth metacarpal bone.d: The 5th of the five long bones of the metacarpus; its base articulates with the carpal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.

fifth metatarsal bone.d: Metatarsal on the lateral border; fibularis brevis attaches to the tuberosity at its base, and it fractures often.

fifth rib.d: 5th rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.

first metacarpal bone.d: Metacarpal of the thumb; the shortest and thickest metacarpal, it forms a saddle joint with the trapezium.

first metatarsal bone.d: Thick, short metatarsal of the big toe; with the two sesamoids beneath it, it carries most of the load during walking.

first posterior intercostal artery.d: Arises from the supreme intercostal artery.

first rib.d: 1st rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly. The shortest, broadest and most curved rib; its upper surface bears the grooves for the subclavian artery and vein and the tubercle for scalenus anterior.

flexor carpi radialis.d: Runs from the medial epicondyle to the base of the 2nd metacarpal; flexes the hand and deviates it radially. Its tendon lies just medial to the radial pulse. Median nerve.

flexor carpi ulnaris.d: Inserts into the pisiform (and through the pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments into the hamate and 5th metacarpal); flexes the hand and deviates it ulnarly. Ulnar nerve.

flexor digiti minimi of foot.tr: Flexor digiti minimi brevis of foot
flexor digiti minimi of foot.la: Musculus flexor digiti minimi brevis pedis
flexor digiti minimi of foot.d: Runs from the base of the 5th metatarsal to the proximal phalanx of the little toe.

flexor digiti minimi of hand.tr: Flexor digiti minimi brevis of hand
flexor digiti minimi of hand.la: Musculus flexor digiti minimi brevis manus
flexor digiti minimi of hand.d: Hypothenar muscle running from the hook of the hamate to the little finger.

flexor digitorum brevis.d: Central superficial muscle of the sole; flexes the middle phalanges of the 2nd–5th toes.

flexor digitorum longus.d: Flexes the distal phalanges of the 2nd–5th toes; its tendon passes behind the medial malleolus.

flexor digitorum profundus.d: Runs from the ulna and interosseous membrane to the distal phalanges; the only muscle that flexes the DIP joints. Its radial half is supplied by the anterior interosseous nerve (median), its ulnar half by the ulnar nerve.

flexor digitorum superficialis.d: Muscle whose four tendons insert into the middle phalanges; flexes the PIP joints. Median nerve.

flexor hallucis longus.d: Flexes the big toe and provides power during push-off; its tendon passes beneath the sustentaculum tali.

flexor pollicis longus.d: Runs from the front of the radius to the distal phalanx of the thumb; flexes the tip of the thumb. With anterior interosseous nerve damage the 'OK' sign cannot be made.

flexor retinaculum of ankle.d: Band between the medial malleolus and the calcaneus roofing the tarsal tunnel; the tibial nerve and posterior tibial artery pass beneath it (tarsal tunnel syndrome).

flexor retinaculum of wrist.tr: Flexor retinaculum of wrist (transverse carpal ligament)
flexor retinaculum of wrist.d: Strong band forming the roof of the carpal tunnel; the median nerve and nine flexor tendons pass beneath it. It is divided in carpal tunnel surgery.

flocculus.d: Small lobule beside the middle cerebellar peduncle; with the nodule it forms the vestibulocerebellum and regulates eye movements.

folium of vermis.d: Thin lobule in the posterior superior vermis.

foramen caecum of frontal bone.d: Small hole in front of the frontal crest; an emissary vein from the nose to the superior sagittal sinus may pass through it.

foramen magnum.d: Large opening in the skull base; the medulla, the vertebral arteries and the spinal roots of the accessory nerve (XI) pass through it.

foramen ovale.d: Oval hole in the greater wing; the mandibular nerve (V3) passes through it.

foramen rotundum.d: Round hole in the greater wing; the maxillary nerve (V2) passes through it.

foramen spinosum.d: Small hole in the greater wing; the middle meningeal artery passes through it.

foramen transversarium.d: Hole in the cervical transverse processes; the vertebral artery passes through it from C6 to C1.

fornix.d: Arched fibre bundle from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies; the main output pathway of the Papez circuit.

fossa for lacrimal gland.d: Fossa in the anterolateral part of the orbital roof; the orbital part of the lacrimal gland lies in it.

fourth metacarpal bone.d: The 4th of the five long bones of the metacarpus; its base articulates with the carpal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.

fourth metatarsal bone.d: The 4th of the five long bones of the metatarsus; its base articulates with the tarsal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.

fourth rib.d: 4th rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.

fourth ventricle.d: Tent-shaped cavity between the pons and medulla and the cerebellum; it opens into the subarachnoid space through the foramina of Magendie and Luschka.
