fovea for ligament of head of femur.d: Pit on the femoral head; the ligament of the head of the femur and the small artery within it enter here.

frenula capsulae.d: Synovial folds of the capsule reflected onto the femoral neck; they carry the retinacular vessels that supply the femoral head.

frontal bone.d: Bone forming the forehead, the roofs of the orbits and most of the anterior cranial fossa; it contains the frontal sinus. It joins the parietal bones at the coronal suture.

frontal border of parietal bone.d: Border forming the coronal suture with the frontal bone.

frontal branch of superficial temporal a.tr: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery
frontal branch of superficial temporal a.d: Supplies the skin of the forehead.

frontal branches of callosomarginal arte.d: Supply the medial surface of the frontal lobe.

frontal crest.d: Midline ridge on the inner surface of the frontal bone; the falx cerebri attaches to it.

frontal eminence.d: Prominence on each side of the forehead; the site of the ossification centre at birth.

frontal margin of greater wing.d: Margin that articulates with the frontal bone.

frontal part of orbital margin.d: Part of the frontal bone forming the upper margin of the orbit.

frontalis muscle.d: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead; temporal branch of the facial nerve. In central facial palsy the forehead is spared, in peripheral palsy it is involved.

ganglia of sympathetic trunk.d: Paravertebral ganglia containing the cell bodies of sympathetic postganglionic neurons; the stellate ganglion lies at C7–T1.

gastroduodenal artery.d: Descends behind the 1st part of the duodenum; a posterior duodenal ulcer can erode it and cause severe bleeding.

genioglossus muscle.d: Fan-shaped muscle forming the main mass of the tongue; supplied by the hypoglossal nerve, it protrudes the tongue. In unilateral paralysis the tongue deviates to the paralysed side.

geniohyoid muscle.d: Suprahyoid muscle from the mental spines on the inner surface of the mandible to the hyoid; supplied by C1, it pulls the hyoid forwards and upwards.

genion.d: Tip of the mental spines; an anthropometric landmark.

genital branch of genitofemoral nerve.d: Passes through the inguinal canal; supplies cremaster and the skin of the scrotum or labium majus.

genitofemoral nerve.d: Arises from L1–L2 and descends on the front of psoas; the efferent limb of the cremasteric reflex.

glabella.d: Smooth area between the eyebrows; a reference point in anthropometric measurement.

glenoid fossa.d: Shallow fossa forming the shoulder joint with the humeral head; deepened by the labrum.

glenoid labrum.d: Fibrocartilaginous ring on the rim of the glenoid cavity; deepens the socket. An anteroinferior tear is a Bankart lesion, a superior tear a SLAP lesion.

glenoid process of scapula.d: Lateral angle carrying the glenoid cavity.

globus pallidus.d: Inner part of the lentiform nucleus; the main output station of the basal ganglia.

glossopharyngeal nerve (ix).d: Carries taste and sensation from the posterior third of the tongue, pharyngeal sensation, the carotid sinus and body, parotid parasympathetic fibres, and supplies stylopharyngeus; the afferent limb of the gag reflex.

gluteal surface of ilium.d: Outer surface of the ilium; the gluteal muscles arise here.

gluteal tuberosity.d: Rough area on the upper posterior surface of the femur; the deep fibres of gluteus maximus attach here.

gluteus maximus muscle.d: The largest muscle in the body; extends and laterally rotates the hip, and is active in climbing stairs and rising from sitting. Inferior gluteal nerve.

gluteus medius muscle.d: Runs from the outer surface of the ilium to the greater trochanter; abducts the hip and stabilises the pelvis during walking. With superior gluteal nerve damage a Trendelenburg sign appears.

gluteus minimus muscle.d: Fan-shaped muscle beneath gluteus medius; abducts and medially rotates the hip. Superior gluteal nerve.

gnathion.d: Lowest anterior point of the chin; an anthropometric landmark.

gracile fasciculus.d: Medial dorsal column carrying fine touch, vibration and position sense from the lower trunk and legs.

gracile lobule.d: Slender lobule of the inferior hemisphere.

gracilis muscle.d: Long thin adductor running from the pubis to the pes anserinus; it also flexes the knee. Obturator nerve; used in flap and graft surgery.

great cardiac vein.d: Vein that accompanies the LAD and opens into the coronary sinus.

great saphenous vein.d: The longest vein of the body; begins in front of the medial malleolus and opens into the femoral vein at the saphenous opening. Used as a coronary bypass graft; the commonest site of varicose veins.

greater horn of hyoid bone.d: Large horn projecting backwards from the body; felt on both sides when examining the throat.

greater palatine artery.d: Supplies the hard palate; passes through the incisive canal to the nose and contributes to septal bleeding.

greater sciatic foramen.d: Greater sciatic foramen; piriformis, the sciatic nerve and the gluteal vessels and nerves pass through it.

greater sciatic notch.d: Large notch on the posterior border of the ilium; ligaments convert it into the greater sciatic foramen.

greater trochanter.d: Large projection at the upper lateral end of the femoral neck; gluteus medius, minimus and piriformis attach to it, and it is felt on the side of the hip.

greater tubercle.d: Large prominence on the lateral side of the humeral head; supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor attach to it.

greater wing.d: Large wing of the sphenoid extending laterally; forms part of the middle cranial fossa and the lateral wall of the orbit.

grey matter of medulla oblongata..d: Grey matter of the medulla made up of cranial nerve nuclei and relay nuclei.

grey matter of pontine tegmentum.d: Grey matter in the posterior part of the pons; contains the nuclei of V, VI and VII and the reticular formation.

groove for marginal sinus.d: Groove for the marginal sinus around the foramen magnum.

groove for middle meningeal artery.d: Branching groove on the inner surface; the middle meningeal artery runs in it, and fractures here cause an extradural haematoma.

groove for occipital sinus.d: Groove for the occipital sinus along the internal occipital crest.

groove for popliteus muscle.d: Groove on the outer surface of the lateral condyle; the popliteus tendon lies here.

groove for spinal nerve.d: Groove on the upper surface of a cervical transverse process; the spinal nerve runs in it.

groove for subclavius muscle.d: Groove on the lower surface of the shaft; subclavius attaches here.

groove for tendon of flexor hallucis lon.tr: Groove for flexor hallucis longus tendon (calcaneus)
groove for tendon of flexor hallucis lon.d: Groove beneath the sustentaculum tali; the flexor hallucis longus tendon passes here.

groove for transverse sinus.d: Horizontal groove on the inner surface; the transverse sinus runs in it and the tentorium cerebelli attaches to it.

groove for ulnar nerve.d: Groove behind the medial epicondyle; the ulnar nerve runs superficially here ('funny bone').

groove for vertebral artery.d: Groove on the upper surface of the posterior arch; the vertebral artery and the suboccipital nerve (C1) run here.

groove of pterygoid hamulus.d: Groove of the pterygoid hamulus; the tensor veli palatini tendon turns around it.

grooves for extensor tendons.d: Grooves on the lower posterior surface of the radius; the extensor tendons pass through them.

habenula.d: Part of the epithalamus; links the limbic system with the brainstem.

hamate bone.d: Medial bone of the distal row; the hook on its palmar surface forms the lateral wall of Guyon's canal and the medial boundary of the carpal tunnel.

handle of malleus.d: Handle of the malleus; embedded in the eardrum, its tip forms the umbo. Tensor tympani attaches here.

head of femur.d: Rounded articular head of the femur; forms the hip joint with the acetabulum, and its blood supply comes from the medial circumflex femoral artery.

head of fibula.d: Upper end of the fibula; the common fibular nerve winds around it behind and laterally.

head of humerus.d: Hemispherical articular head; forms the shoulder joint with the glenoid cavity.

head of malleus.d: Head of the malleus in the upper middle ear; articulates with the incus.

head of metatarsal bone.d: Distal head of a metatarsal; bears weight in the sole and articulates with the proximal phalanx.

head of radius.d: Disc-shaped upper end of the radius; it rotates at the elbow and in children can slip out of the annular ligament.

head of rib.d: Head of the rib that articulates with the vertebral column.

head of talus.d: Head articulating with the navicular; the keystone of the medial arch.

head of ulna.d: Head at the lower end of the ulna; felt on the posteromedial side of the wrist.

hemi-azygos vein.d: Collects the lower left intercostal veins and crosses to the azygos vein at T8–T9.

hepatic portal vein.d: Formed behind the neck of the pancreas by the splenic and superior mesenteric veins; brings 75% of the liver's blood. Oesophageal varices develop in portal hypertension.

hepatic veins.d: The three large veins of the liver; they open directly into the inferior vena cava, and their occlusion is the Budd–Chiari syndrome.

hip bone.d: Large irregular bone formed by the fusion of ilium, ischium and pubis at the acetabulum; with the sacrum it forms the pelvic ring and with the femoral head the hip joint.

hippocampal commissure.d: Fibres joining the crura of the two fornices.

hippocampus.d: Fold in the floor of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle; it transfers new information into long-term memory and is among the first regions affected in Alzheimer disease.

hook of hamate bone.d: Hook of the hamate projecting towards the palm; forms the lateral wall of Guyon's canal and can fracture in golfers.

humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris.tr: Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris
humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris.la: Caput humerale musculi extensoris carpi ulnaris
humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris.d: Head arising from the lateral epicondyle.

humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.tr: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris
humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.la: Caput humerale musculi flexoris carpi ulnaris
humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.d: Arises from the medial epicondyle; the ulnar nerve enters the forearm through the arch between the two heads (cubital tunnel).

humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.tr: Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum superficialis
humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.la: Caput humeroulnare musculi flexoris digitorum superficialis
humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.d: Arises from the medial epicondyle and the coronoid process.

humerus.d: The single long bone of the arm; its head forms the shoulder joint with the glenoid cavity of the scapula. The surgical neck (axillary nerve), radial groove (radial nerve) and medial epicondyle (ulnar nerve) matter in fractures because of nerve injury.

hyoglossus muscle.d: Quadrilateral muscle from the hyoid to the side of the tongue; depresses the tongue. The hypoglossal and lingual nerves run on its surface and the lingual artery deep to it.

hyoid bone.d: U-shaped bone in the neck at the level of C3 that articulates with no other bone; it gives attachment to the muscles of the tongue and larynx. Its fracture is of forensic importance in strangulation.

hypoglossal canal.d: Canal above the condyle; the hypoglossal nerve leaves the skull through it.

hypoglossal nerve (xii).d: Supplies the tongue muscles; in a peripheral palsy the protruded tongue deviates to the paralysed side.

hypophysial fossa.d: Fossa in the sella turcica; the pituitary gland lies in it.

hypothalamus.d: Floor and lower walls of the third ventricle; regulates body temperature, hunger and thirst, circadian rhythm and pituitary secretion.

ileocolic artery.d: Last branch, supplying the terminal ileum, caecum and appendix.

iliac crest.d: Upper border of the ilium; the abdominal and back muscles attach to it, and bone marrow aspiration can be performed here.

iliac fossa.d: Broad fossa on the inner surface of the ilium; iliacus arises here.

iliac tubercle.d: Prominence on the outer lip of the iliac crest, about 5 cm behind the ASIS.

iliac tuberosity.d: Rough area above the auricular surface; the strong sacroiliac ligaments attach to it.

iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery.d: Supplies the iliacus muscle and the ilium.

iliacus muscle.d: Muscle filling the iliac fossa; it joins psoas to insert into the lesser trochanter. Femoral nerve.

ilio-inguinal nerve.d: Arises from L1 and passes through the inguinal canal; supplies the skin of the upper inner thigh and external genitalia and can be injured in hernia repair.

iliococcygeus muscle.d: Thin posterior part of levator ani running from the tendinous arch to the coccyx.

iliocostalis colli muscle.d: Part of the iliocostalis column running from the upper ribs to the lower cervical vertebrae.

iliocostalis lumborum muscle.d: Lumbar part of the most lateral column of erector spinae; extends the spine and bends it sideways. Posterior rami of the spinal nerves.

iliocostalis thoracis muscle.d: Part of the iliocostalis column running from the lower ribs to the upper ribs.

iliohypogastric nerve.d: Arises from L1; gives branches to the abdominal wall muscles and the suprapubic skin.

iliolumbar artery.d: Supplies the iliacus and the muscles of the lower back.

iliolumbar ligament.d: Strong ligament binding the transverse process of L5 to the iliac crest; stabilises the lumbosacral junction.

iliolumbar vein.d: Accompanies the artery of the same name.

iliopectineal arch.d: Fascial thickening dividing the space between the inguinal ligament and the pubis into muscular (lacuna musculorum) and vascular (lacuna vasorum) compartments.

iliopsoas fascia.d: Fascia enclosing the iliacus and psoas muscles; a psoas abscess tracks down to the groin within this sheath.

iliopsoas muscle.d: Psoas major and iliacus joined by a common insertion into the lesser trochanter; the most powerful flexor of the hip.

iliopubic eminence.d: Prominence where the ilium and pubis meet.

iliotibial tract.d: Lateral thickening of the fascia lata running from the iliac crest to Gerdy's tubercle of the tibia. In runners it causes a friction syndrome over the lateral femoral condyle.

ilium.d: The largest, upper part of the hip bone.

impression for costoclavicular ligament.d: Rough area on the lower surface of the medial end; the costoclavicular ligament to the 1st rib attaches here.

incus.d: The middle of the three ossicles of the middle ear; it transmits vibration between the malleus and the stapes.

inferior alveolar artery.d: Supplies the lower teeth in the mandibular canal.

inferior alveolar nerve.d: Branch running in the mandibular canal and supplying the lower teeth; blocked in dentistry.

inferior angle of scapula.d: Lower tip of the scapula; at the level of T7.

inferior articular facet of vertebra.d: Surface of the inferior articular process that forms a facet joint with the vertebra below.

inferior articular surface of atlas.d: Lower surface of the lateral mass; forms the lateral atlanto-axial joint with the axis.

inferior articular surface of tibia.d: Lower surface forming the ankle joint with the talus.

inferior basal vein of left lung.tr: Inferior basal vein of left lung
inferior basal vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

inferior basal vein of right lung.tr: Inferior basal vein of right lung
inferior basal vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

inferior colliculus.d: Midbrain relay centre of the auditory pathway.

inferior costal facet.d: Half facet on the lower border of a thoracic vertebral body; articulates with the head of the rib below.

inferior deep lateral cervical nodes.la: Nodi lymphoidei cervicales laterales profundi inferiores

inferior epigastric artery.d: Arises from the external iliac artery and enters the rectus sheath; the landmark separating direct from indirect inguinal hernias (an indirect hernia emerges lateral to it).

inferior extensor retinaculum of ankle.d: Y-shaped band on the dorsum of the foot; the deep fibular nerve can be compressed beneath it (anterior tarsal tunnel).

inferior fibular retinaculum.d: Band holding the fibular tendons on the lateral surface of the calcaneus.

inferior frontal sulcus.d: Separates the middle and inferior frontal gyri.

inferior gemellus muscle.d: Runs from the ischial tuberosity to join the obturator internus tendon; a lateral rotator.

inferior glenohumeral ligament.d: The most important static stabiliser of the shoulder; prevents anterior dislocation when the arm is abducted and externally rotated.

inferior gluteal artery.d: Emerges below piriformis; supplies gluteus maximus.

inferior gluteal line.d: Lower line on the outer surface of the ilium; bounds the origin of gluteus minimus.

inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscl.d: Runs from the lateral plate to the neck of the condyle; the only muscle of mastication that starts mouth opening and protrudes the jaw.

inferior horn of thyroid cartilage.d: Lower extension of the thyroid cartilage; it articulates with the cricoid and allows the tilting that adjusts the pitch of the voice.

inferior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv.tr: Inferior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm
inferior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv.d: Sensation from the skin of the lower lateral arm.

inferior lateral genicular artery.d: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.

inferior leaflet of right atrioventricul.d: The posteroinferior cusp of the tricuspid valve.

inferior lingular artery of left lung.tr: Inferior lingular segmental artery of left lung
inferior lingular artery of left lung.la: Arteria segmentalis lingularis inferior pulmonis sinistri
inferior lingular artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

inferior lingular artery of right lung.tr: Inferior lingular artery of right lung
inferior lingular artery of right lung.la: Arteria segmentalis lingularis inferior pulmonis dextri

inferior lingular segment of left lung (.tr: Inferior lingular segment of left lung (sv)

inferior lingular segmental bronchus of.tr: Inferior lingular segmental bronchus of left lung (bv)

inferior lingular vein of left lung.tr: Inferior lingular vein of left lung
inferior lingular vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

inferior lingular vein of right lung.tr: Inferior lingular vein of right lung

inferior lobar artery of left lung.tr: Inferior lobar artery of left lung
inferior lobar artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to the lower lobe of the left lung.

inferior lobar artery of right lung.tr: Inferior lobar artery of right lung
inferior lobar artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to the lower lobe of the right lung.

inferior medial genicular artery.d: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.

inferior mental spine.d: Lower spine on the inner surface; geniohyoid attaches to it.

inferior mesenteric artery.d: Arises from the aorta at L3; supplies the hindgut (distal 1/3 of the transverse colon, descending and sigmoid colon, upper rectum).

inferior mesenteric vein.d: Drains the left colon and upper rectum and opens into the splenic vein.

inferior nasal concha bone.d: Independent thin bone attached to the lateral wall of the nasal cavity; the nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus beneath it.

inferior nuchal line.d: Lower line where neck muscles attach; the suboccipital muscles attach to it.

inferior oblique muscle.d: The only eye muscle arising from the front of the orbital floor; turns the eye up and out and rotates it outwards. Oculomotor nerve.

inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus*.d: Lower gyrus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe.

inferior ophthalmic vein.d: Drains the floor of the orbit; connected with the pterygoid plexus.

inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.d: First branch of the superior mesenteric artery; anastomoses with the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

inferior papillary muscle of left ventri.tr: Posterior papillary muscle of left ventricle
inferior papillary muscle of left ventri.d: Holds the mitral valve; because it has a single blood supply (usually the right coronary), it tends to rupture after infarction.

inferior papillary muscle of right ventr.tr: Posterior papillary muscle of right ventricle
inferior papillary muscle of right ventr.d: Papillary muscle holding the posterior and septal cusps of the tricuspid valve.

inferior petrosal sinus.d: Connects the cavernous sinus with the internal jugular vein; sampled in the diagnosis of Cushing's disease.

inferior pharyngeal constrictor.d: Arises from the thyroid and cricoid cartilages; its cricopharyngeal part is the upper oesophageal sphincter. A Zenker's diverticulum develops in the weak area between its two parts.

inferior phrenic artery.d: First branch of the abdominal aorta; supplies the diaphragm and gives the superior suprarenal artery.

inferior pubic ligament.d: Thick ligament arching beneath the symphysis (arcuate pubic ligament); it rounds off the pubic arch.

inferior pubic ramus.d: Lower ramus of the pubis; it joins the ischial ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus.

inferior rectus muscle.d: Turns the eye down (depression) and in, and rotates it outwards; oculomotor nerve. It can be trapped in orbital floor fractures.

inferior sagittal sinus.d: Lies in the free lower edge of the falx cerebri.

inferior salivatory nucleus.d: Nucleus of the parasympathetic fibres (IX) to the parotid gland.

inferior subscapular nerve.d: Supplies the lower part of subscapularis and teres major.

inferior subtendinous bursa of biceps fe.tr: Inferior subtendinous bursa of biceps femoris
inferior subtendinous bursa of biceps fe.la: Bursa subtendinea musculi bicipitis femoris inferior
inferior subtendinous bursa of biceps fe.d: Between the biceps femoris tendon and the fibular collateral ligament.

inferior suprarenal artery.d: Branch of the renal artery to the lower part of the adrenal gland.

inferior tarsus.d: Connective tissue plate forming the skeleton of the lower eyelid; narrower than the upper one.

inferior temporal gyrus.d: Gyrus at the lower border of the temporal lobe; takes part in object recognition.

inferior temporal sulcus.d: Separates the middle and inferior temporal gyri.

inferior thyroid artery.d: Supplies the thyroid and parathyroids; closely related to the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

inferior thyroid notch.d: Shallow notch in the middle of the lower border of the thyroid cartilage.

inferior thyroid tubercle.d: Prominence at the lower end of the oblique line; the infrahyoid muscles attach to it.

inferior transverse scapular ligament.d: Ligament bridging the spinoglenoid notch; the suprascapular nerve passes beneath it into the infraspinous fossa.

inferior trunk of brachial plexus.d: Formed by the C8–T1 roots; its damage causes Klumpke palsy (claw hand) and it is compressed by a cervical rib or a Pancoast tumour.

inferior ulnar collateral artery.d: Joins the anastomosis above the elbow.

inferior vein of left ventricle.d: Drains the posterior surface of the left ventricle.

inferior vein of left ventricle (//poste.tr: Posterior vein of left ventricle (accessory branch)
inferior vein of left ventricle (//poste.d: Additional drainage branch of the posterior surface of the left ventricle.

inferior vena cava (abdominal part).d: Formed at L5 by the union of the common iliac veins; rises to the right of the aorta.

inferior vena cava (thoracic part).d: Short part that passes through the diaphragm at T8 and opens into the right atrium.

inferior vertebral notch.d: Notch below the pedicle; forms the upper half of the intervertebral foramen.

infra-orbital artery.d: Runs through the floor of the orbit and emerges on the face at the infraorbital foramen.

infraglenoid tubercle.d: Prominence below the glenoid; the long head of triceps arises here.

infrapatellar branch of saphenous nerve.d: Sensation from the skin in front of the knee; it can be cut in knee surgery.

infrapatellar fat pad.d: Fat pad behind the patellar ligament, between the capsule and the synovium; it fills the joint space during knee movements.

infraspinatus muscle.d: Rotator cuff muscle from the infraspinous fossa to the greater tubercle; rotates the arm laterally. Suprascapular nerve.

infraspinous fossa.d: Fossa below the spine; infraspinatus arises here.

infratemporal surface of greater wing.d: Surface of the greater wing facing the infratemporal fossa; the upper head of lateral pterygoid arises here.

inguinal ligament.d: The folded lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis, running from the ASIS to the pubic tubercle; the femoral neurovascular bundle and iliopsoas pass beneath it.

inner lip of iliac crest.d: Inner lip of the iliac crest; transversus abdominis and quadratus lumborum attach to it.

innermost intercostal muscles.d: Deep layer of the internal intercostals; the intercostal neurovascular bundle runs between this muscle and the internal intercostal.

insula (subcentral gyrus and ant. and po.d: Cortex deep in the lateral fissure covered by the opercula; linked to taste, visceral sensation and emotional awareness.

insular branches of middle cerebral arte.d: The M2 segment branching over the surface of the insula.

insular branches of middle cerebral arte.tr: Insular branches of middle cerebral artery (M2)
insular branches of middle cerebral arte.d: The M2 segment running over the insula.

intercapitular veins of foot.d: Connect the plantar and dorsal veins at the bases of the toes.

interclavicular ligament.d: Joins the medial ends of the two clavicles across the jugular notch.

intercondylar area.d: Area between the two condyles on the tibial plateau.

intercondylar eminence.d: Prominence between the condyles; the cruciate ligaments attach around it.

intercondylar fossa.d: Deep notch between the two condyles; the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments attach here.

intercondylar line.d: Line separating the intercondylar fossa from the popliteal surface; the joint capsule attaches to it.

intercornual ligament.d: Small ligament joining the sacral and coccygeal cornua.

intercostal nerves.d: Anterior rami of the T1–T11 spinal nerves; they run in the subcostal groove in the order vein–artery–nerve (VAN), so intercostal block is done at the lower border of the rib.

intercuneiform interosseous ligaments.d: Strong ligaments between the facing surfaces of the cuneiforms.

intermediate cuneiform bone.d: The smallest cuneiform; the base of the 2nd metatarsal locks into it, giving the Lisfranc joint its stability.

intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of f.tr: Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot
intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of f.d: Branch of the superficial fibular nerve to the middle and lateral part of the dorsum of the foot.

intermediate sacral crest.d: Ridge formed by the fused articular processes.

intermediate tendon of digastric muscle.d: Tendon joining the two bellies; a fibrous loop binds it to the body of the hyoid.

intermediate zone.d: Line between the inner and outer lips of the iliac crest; internal oblique attaches to it.

intermediolateral nucleus.d: Sympathetic preganglionic neurons in the lateral horn of T1–L2.

intermediomedial nucleus.d: Visceral sensory nucleus of the intermediate zone.

intermuscular gluteal bursae.d: Bursae between gluteus maximus and vastus lateralis.

internal abdominal oblique muscle.d: Middle-layer muscle beneath the external oblique, with fibres running up and forwards; in males its lower fibres give rise to cremaster. Nerves: T7–L1. It flexes the trunk and rotates it to the same side.

internal carotid artery.d: Gives no branches in the neck; passes through the carotid canal and cavernous sinus to supply the anterior circulation of the brain and the eye.

internal iliac artery.d: Supplies the pelvic organs, buttock and perineum; may be ligated in postpartum haemorrhage.

internal intercostal membrane.d: Membranous continuation of the internal intercostal muscle posteriorly towards the spine.

internal intercostal muscles.d: Muscles whose fibres run at right angles to the external intercostals; they depress the ribs in forced expiration.

internal jugular vein.d: Continuation of the sigmoid sinus; runs in the carotid sheath and is often used for central venous catheters.

internal occipital crest.d: Midline ridge on the inner surface of the occipital bone; the falx cerebelli attaches to it.

internal pudendal artery.d: Runs with the pudendal nerve in Alcock's canal; supplies the perineum and external genitalia.

internal surface of squamous part of fro.d: Surface of the frontal bone facing the brain; it carries the frontal lobe.

internal thoracic artery.d: Descends 1 cm lateral to the sternal border; the graft most used in coronary bypass (LIMA).

internal thoracic veins.d: Veins accompanying the internal thoracic artery.

interosseous border of radius.d: Sharp border facing the ulna; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.

interosseous border of tibia.d: Border facing the fibula; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.

interosseous border of ulna.d: Sharp border facing the radius; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.

interosseous crest of fibula.d: Border of the fibula facing the tibia; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.

interosseous membrane of forearm.d: Fibrous membrane joining the radius and ulna; its fibres run down and medially from the radius, transferring load from the hand to the ulna.

interosseous membrane of leg.d: Fibrous membrane joining the tibia and fibula; it separates the anterior and posterior muscle compartments of the leg and gives attachment to muscles.

interosseous metacarpal ligaments.d: Interosseous ligaments between the metacarpal bases.

interosseous sacro-iliac ligament.d: One of the strongest ligaments in the body, between the tuberosities of the sacrum and ilium; it locks the sacroiliac joint.

interpeduncular fossa.d: Depression between the two cerebral peduncles; the oculomotor nerve emerges here.

interpubic disc.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc of the pubic symphysis; it usually contains a small cavity.

intersesamoid ligament.d: Joins the two sesamoid bones under the big toe.

interspinales colli muscles.d: Short muscles between adjacent cervical spinous processes.

interspinales lumborum muscles.d: Short muscles between the lumbar spinous processes.

interspinales thoracis muscles.d: Interspinous muscles of the thoracic region; often present only at the upper and lower ends.

interspinous ligaments.d: Thin ligaments between adjacent spinous processes; they limit flexion.

intertransverse ligaments.d: Thin ligaments joining adjacent transverse processes; they limit lateral flexion.

intertrochanteric crest.d: Ridge joining the trochanters behind; the quadrate tubercle lies on it.

intertrochanteric line.d: Line joining the trochanters in front; the hip joint capsule and iliofemoral ligament attach to it.

intertubercular sulcus.d: Groove between the two tubercles; the tendon of the long head of biceps runs in it.

intertubercular tendon sheath.d: Sheath around the tendon of the long head of biceps in its groove; continuous with the joint cavity.

intervertebral disc c2-c3.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C2-C3 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc c3-c4.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C3-C4 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc c4-c5.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C4-C5 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc c5-c6.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C5-C6 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. The commonest level of cervical disc herniation; the C6 root is affected.

intervertebral disc c6-c7.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C6-C7 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. A frequent level of cervical herniation; the C7 root is affected (reduced triceps reflex).

intervertebral disc c7-t1.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C7-T1 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc l1-l2.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L1-L2 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc l2-l3.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L2-L3 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc l3-l4.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L3-L4 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc l4-l5.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L4-L5 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. One of the two commonest levels of disc herniation; a posterolateral herniation usually compresses the L5 root.

intervertebral disc l5-s1.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L5-S1 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. The commonest level of herniation; a posterolateral herniation compresses the S1 root (reduced Achilles reflex).

intervertebral disc t1-t2.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T1-T2 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t10-t11.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T10-T11 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t11-t12.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T11-T12 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t12-l1.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T12-L1 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t2-t3.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T2-T3 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t3-t4.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T3-T4 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t4-t5.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T4-T5 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t5-t6.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T5-T6 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t6-t7.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T6-T7 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t7-t8.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T7-T8 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t8-t9.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T8-T9 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral disc t9-t10.d: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T9-T10 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.

intervertebral foramen.d: Opening between two vertebrae; it contains the spinal nerve and the dorsal root ganglion.

intervertebral foramina.d: Openings connecting the sacral canal to the anterior and posterior sacral foramina.

intervertebral surface.d: Surface of the vertebral body in contact with the disc.

intra-articular ligament of head of rib.tr: Intra-articular ligament of head of rib
intra-articular ligament of head of rib.d: Joins the crest of the rib head to the intervertebral disc, dividing the joint into two cavities.

intrajugular process of occipital bone.d: Small process that partly divides the jugular foramen.

intraparietal sulcus.d: Separates the superior and inferior parietal lobules.

intrarenal arteries of left kidney.d: Segmental, interlobar, arcuate and interlobular arteries.

intrarenal arteries of right kidney.d: Segmental, interlobar, arcuate and interlobular arteries.

intrarenal veins of left kidney.d: The venous network inside the kidney.

intrarenal veins of right kidney.d: The venous network inside the kidney.

investing abdominal fascia.d: Deep fascia enclosing each of the abdominal wall muscles.

iris.d: Muscular diaphragm giving the eye its colour, with the pupil in its centre; it has sphincter (parasympathetic) and dilator (sympathetic) muscles.

ischial spine.d: Spine on the posterior border of the ischium; the sacrospinous ligament attaches to it, and it guides pudendal nerve block.

ischial tuberosity.d: Tuberosity that bears weight when sitting; the hamstrings and the sacrotuberous ligament attach to it.

ischiofemoral ligament.d: Posterior ligament of the capsule; limits internal rotation and, with its spiral course, tightens in extension.

ischiopubic ramus.d: Union of the ischial and pubic rami; bounds the obturator foramen below, and the crura of the penis/clitoris attach to it.

ischium.d: Posteroinferior part of the hip bone (the sitting bone).

jugular notch of occipital bone.d: Notch that forms the jugular foramen together with the temporal bone.

jugular process.d: Process behind the jugular notch; rectus capitis lateralis attaches to it.

lacrimal artery.d: Supplies the lacrimal gland and the eyelids.

lacrimal bone.d: The smallest facial bone, in the medial wall of the orbit; the lacrimal sac lies in its fossa for the lacrimal sac.

lacrimal canaliculus.d: Thin canal from the punctum on the eyelid margin to the lacrimal sac.

lacrimal gland.d: Tear-secreting gland in the upper outer corner of the orbit; its parasympathetic fibres come from the facial nerve (pterygopalatine ganglion).

lacrimal sac.d: Sac in the fossa on the medial wall of the orbit; its inflammation is dacryocystitis.

lamina of cricoid cartilage.d: Broad posterior plate of the cricoid; the posterior cricoarytenoid muscles arise from it.

lamina of thyroid cartilage.d: One of the two plates forming the thyroid cartilage; they join in front to form the Adam's apple.

lamina of vertebral arch.d: Posterior part of the arch; it is removed in laminectomy, and the ligamentum flavum spans between laminae.

laryngeal prominence.d: Projection where the two laminae meet in front (Adam's apple); more prominent in males.

lat_fis-ant-horizont.tr: Anterior horizontal ramus of lateral sulcus
lat_fis-ant-horizont.d: Horizontal limb of the Sylvian fissure entering the inferior frontal gyrus; it separates the orbital and triangular parts.

lat_fis-ant-vertical.d: Ascending limb of the Sylvian fissure; it separates the triangular and opercular parts.

lat_fis-post.d: Long posterior limb of the Sylvian fissure separating the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes.

lateral angle of scapula.d: Lateral angle of the scapula carrying the glenoid.

lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve.d: Sensory terminal branch of the musculocutaneous nerve; supplies the skin of the lateral forearm.

lateral basal segment of left lung (six).tr: Lateral basal segment of left lung (six)

lateral basal segment of right lung (six.tr: Lateral basal segment of right lung (six)

lateral basal segmental artery of left l.tr: Lateral basal segmental artery of left lung
lateral basal segmental artery of left l.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis sinistri
lateral basal segmental artery of left l.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

lateral basal segmental artery of right.tr: Lateral basal segmental artery of right lung
lateral basal segmental artery of right.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis dextri
lateral basal segmental artery of right.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

lateral basal segmental bronchus of left.tr: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of left lung (bix)
lateral basal segmental bronchus of left.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis lateralis (B IX) sinister

lateral basal segmental bronchus of righ.tr: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of right lung (bix)
lateral basal segmental bronchus of righ.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis lateralis (B IX) dexter

lateral border of humerus.d: Lateral border of the humerus; below it continues as the lateral supracondylar ridge.

lateral border of scapula.d: Lateral border facing the axilla; teres major and minor arise from it.

lateral circumflex femoral artery.d: Supplies the anterolateral muscles of the thigh.

lateral circumflex femoral veins.d: Accompanies the artery of the same name.

lateral condyle of femur.d: Lateral condyle of the femur; forms the knee joint with the tibia and meniscus, and its forward prominence prevents lateral slipping of the patella.

lateral condyle of tibia.d: Lateral condyle of the tibia; the lateral meniscus rests on it.

lateral corticospinal tract.d: Main pathway of voluntary motor fibres that have crossed in the medulla; damage causes upper motor neuron signs (Babinski) on the same side.

lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.d: Pulls the muscular process of the arytenoid forwards, bringing the vocal folds together (adduction); recurrent laryngeal nerve.

lateral cuneiform bone.d: Medium-sized cuneiform; it lies between the cuboid and the 3rd metatarsal.

lateral epicondyle of femur.d: Prominence on the lateral condyle; the lateral collateral ligament and the lateral head of gastrocnemius attach to it.

lateral epicondyle of humerus.d: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus; common origin of the forearm extensors (tennis elbow).

lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.d: Passes under the inguinal ligament just medial to the ASIS; its compression causes burning on the outer thigh (meralgia paraesthetica).

lateral femoral intermuscular septum.d: Fascial wall separating the anterior and posterior thigh compartments laterally.

lateral frontobasal artery.d: Supplies the inferolateral surface of the frontal lobe.

lateral geniculate body.d: Thalamic relay nucleus of the visual pathway; the optic radiation goes from here to the occipital cortex.

lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis.tr: Lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis
lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis.la: Caput laterale musculi flexoris hallucis brevis
lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis.d: Head attaching to the lateral sesamoid.

lateral head of gastrocnemius.d: Calf head arising from the lateral condyle of the femur.

lateral head of triceps brachii.d: Head arising above the radial groove; supplied by the radial nerve.

lateral intercondylar tubercle.d: Lateral tubercle of the intercondylar eminence.

lateral intermediate substance.d: Lateral part of the intermediate zone of the spinal cord.

lateral intermuscular septum of arm.d: The radial nerve pierces this septum to enter the anterior compartment.

lateral lip of linea aspera.d: Lateral lip of the linea aspera; vastus lateralis and the short head of biceps femoris attach to it.

lateral malleolar facet.d: Triangular surface that articulates with the lateral malleolus.

lateral malleolus.d: Lower end of the fibula; it reaches further down and further back than the medial malleolus.

lateral mass.d: Thick lateral part of the atlas on each side; transfers weight from the skull to the axis.

lateral meniscus.d: Nearly O-shaped lateral meniscus; it does not attach to the collateral ligament, is linked to popliteus and is more mobile.

lateral occipital artery.d: Supplies the inferior surface of the temporal lobe.

lateral occipital gyrus (middle occipita.d: Middle gyrus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe.

lateral occipitotemporal gyrus.d: Gyrus on the inferior surface of the temporal lobe; contains the face recognition area (damage causes prosopagnosia).

lateral part of longitudinal arch of foo.tr: Lateral part of longitudinal arch of foot

lateral part of occipital bone.d: Part beside the foramen magnum; carries the condyles.

lateral part of sacrum.d: Lateral parts of the sacrum; they carry the alae and the auricular surfaces.

lateral part of transverse process.d: Outer part of the transverse process.

lateral patellar retinaculum.d: Extension of the vastus lateralis aponeurosis from the edge of the patella to the tibia.

lateral pectoral nerve.d: Arises from the lateral cord and supplies pectoralis major.

lateral plantar artery.d: The large terminal branch; forms the deep plantar arch.

lateral plantar nerve.d: Sensation from the lateral sole and the lateral one and a half toes, and supplies most intrinsic foot muscles (the foot's counterpart of the ulnar nerve).

lateral plantar veins.d: Drain the lateral part of the sole.

lateral pontine branches of basilar arte.tr: Lateral pontine branches of basilar artery
lateral pontine branches of basilar arte.d: Supply the lateral parts of the pons.

lateral process of calcaneal tuberosity.d: Lateral process of the calcaneal tuberosity; abductor digiti minimi arises here.

lateral process of malleus.d: Small process of the malleus that makes a bulge on the eardrum.

lateral process of nasal septal cartilag.tr: Lateral process of septal cartilage (upper lateral cartilage)
lateral process of nasal septal cartilag.d: Cartilage plate extending sideways from the septal cartilage, supporting the middle of the nasal dorsum (upper lateral cartilage).

lateral process of talus.d: Lateral process of the talus; site of the snowboarder's fracture.

lateral pterygoid muscle.d: Its upper and lower heads attach to the mandibular condyle and the articular disc; the muscle of mastication that opens the mouth and protrudes the jaw.

lateral pterygoid plate.d: Lateral plate of the pterygoid process; both pterygoid muscles arise from it.

lateral rectus muscle.d: Muscle that turns the eye outwards (abduction); supplied by the abducens nerve (VI). Its paralysis causes a convergent squint and horizontal double vision.

lateral reticulospinal tract.d: Pathway from the medullary reticular formation that reduces extensor tone.

lateral sacral crest.d: Ridge formed by the fused transverse processes; the sacrotuberous ligament attaches to it.

lateral segmental artery of left lung.tr: Lateral segmental artery of left lung

lateral segmental artery of right lung.tr: Lateral segmental artery of right lung
lateral segmental artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

lateral segmental bronchus of right lung.tr: Lateral segmental bronchus of right lung (biv)

lateral spinothalamic tract.d: Carries pain and temperature from the opposite side; in Brown-Séquard syndrome these are lost on the opposite side.

lateral subtendinous bursa of gastrocnem.d: Between the lateral head and the capsule.

lateral supracondylar line.d: Continuation of the linea aspera down to the lateral condyle; plantaris and the lateral head of gastrocnemius arise from it.

lateral supracondylar ridge.d: Ridge above the lateral epicondyle; brachioradialis and ECRL arise from it.

lateral surface of fibula.d: Lateral surface of the fibula; fibularis longus and brevis arise from it.

lateral surface of radius.d: Lateral surface of the radius; pronator teres inserts at its middle.

lateral surface of tibia.d: Lateral surface of the tibia; tibialis anterior arises from it.

lateral talocalcaneal ligament.d: Short ligament joining the lateral surfaces of the talus and calcaneus.

lateral tarsal artery.d: Supplies the lateral part of the dorsum of the foot.

lateral temporomandibular ligament.d: Lateral thickening of the capsule; prevents backward displacement of the condyle.

lateral thoracic artery.d: Supplies serratus anterior and the lateral part of the breast.

lateral thyrohyoid ligament.d: Joins the superior horn of the thyroid cartilage to the greater horn of the hyoid; a small triticeous cartilage may lie within it.

lateral tubercle.d: Lateral tubercle of the posterior process of the talus; the posterior talofibular ligament attaches to it.

lateral vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

lateral ventricle.d: C-shaped cavity in each hemisphere with anterior, posterior and inferior horns and a body; its choroid plexus produces CSF.

lateral vestibulospinal tract.d: Pathway from the lateral vestibular nucleus stimulating the antigravity extensor muscles.

latissimus dorsi muscle.d: Broad flat muscle from the lower back to the floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus; adducts, extends and medially rotates the arm. Nerve: thoracodorsal nerve (C6–C8).

left anterior lateral segment of liver (.tr: Left anterior lateral segment of liver (iii)

left atrium.d: The most posterior chamber of the heart, receiving oxygenated blood from four pulmonary veins; lies against the oesophagus (its enlargement can cause dysphagia).

left brachiocephalic vein.d: Long vein crossing obliquely in front of the branches of the aortic arch.

left common carotid artery.d: Arises directly from the aortic arch; runs in the carotid sheath of the neck with the internal jugular vein and vagus nerve.

left coronary artery.d: Short trunk from the left aortic sinus; divides into the anterior interventricular and circumflex arteries. Its occlusion causes an extensive anterior infarction.

left coronary leaflet.d: The left coronary artery arises from the sinus behind it.

left gastric artery.d: The smallest branch of the coeliac trunk; supplies the lesser curvature of the stomach and the lower oesophagus and may be the source of bleeding ulcers.

left gastro-omental vein.d: Drains the left part of the greater curvature of the stomach.

left inferior pulmonary vein.d: Carries blood from the left lower lobe to the left atrium; isolated in atrial fibrillation ablation.

left posterior lateral segment of liver.tr: Left posterior lateral segment of liver (ii)

left pulmonary artery.d: Short branch that passes over the left main bronchus to the left lung.

left renal artery.d: Short artery to the left kidney; renal artery stenosis causes renovascular hypertension.

left renal vein.d: Passes between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery to reach the IVC (compression: nutcracker syndrome); receives the left gonadal and adrenal veins.

left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary valv.tr: Left semilunar cusp of pulmonary valve
left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary valv.la: Valvula semilunaris sinistra valvae trunci pulmonalis
left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary valv.d: The left semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve.

left subclavian artery.d: Arises directly from the aortic arch; if blocked before the origin of the vertebral artery, subclavian steal syndrome develops.

left subclavian vein.d: The thoracic duct opens into the left venous angle (its junction with the internal jugular).

left subcostal vein.d: Helps to form the hemiazygos vein.

left superior intercostal vein.d: Carries the left 2nd–4th intercostal veins to the left brachiocephalic vein.

left superior pulmonary vein.d: Carries blood from the left upper lobe and lingula to the left atrium.

left testicular artery.d: Long thin artery supplying the left testis.

left testicular vein.d: Opens into the left renal vein at a right angle; this is why varicocele is mostly left-sided.

left ventricle.d: The chamber with the thickest wall, forming the apex of the heart; pumps blood into the aorta.

lens.d: Transparent lens behind the iris; its shape is changed by the ciliary muscle for accommodation, and its clouding is cataract.

lenticular process of incus.d: Lens-shaped process at the tip of the long limb; articulates with the stapes.

lentiform nucleus.d: Lens-shaped nucleus formed by the putamen and globus pallidus; lateral to the internal capsule.

lesser horn of hyoid bone.d: Lesser horn; the stylohyoid ligament attaches to it.

lesser sciatic foramen.d: Lesser sciatic foramen; the obturator internus tendon, the pudendal nerve and the internal pudendal vessels pass through it.

lesser sciatic notch.d: Notch below the ischial spine; ligaments convert it into the lesser sciatic foramen.

lesser trochanter.d: Projection on the posteromedial side of the femoral neck; iliopsoas inserts here.

lesser tubercle.d: Small prominence on the front of the humerus; subscapularis inserts here.

lesser wing.d: Small wing surrounding the optic canal; forms the posterior border of the anterior cranial fossa.

levator anguli oris.d: Runs from the canine fossa to the corner of the mouth; raises the corner of the mouth.

levator ani.d: Pelvic floor muscle made up of pubococcygeus, puboanalis and iliococcygeus; it supports the pelvic organs and contributes to continence. S4 and branches of the pudendal nerve.

levator labii superioris.d: Runs from below the orbital margin to the upper lip; raises the upper lip.

levator nasolabialis.la: Musculus levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
levator nasolabialis.d: Runs from the frontal process of the maxilla to the ala of the nose and the upper lip.

levator palpebrae superioris.d: Muscle that raises the upper eyelid; supplied by the oculomotor nerve, while its smooth-muscle fibres (superior tarsal muscle) are sympathetic. Its paralysis causes ptosis.

levator scapulae.d: Runs from the transverse processes of C1–C4 to the superior angle of the scapula; elevates the scapula. Nerves: dorsal scapular nerve and C3–C4.

levatores breves costarum.d: Small muscles from the transverse processes to the rib immediately below.

levatores longi costarum.d: Small muscles from the transverse processes that skip one rib to reach the second rib below.

ligament of head of femur.d: Ligament running from the fovea of the femoral head to the acetabular notch; the artery within it is important for supplying the femoral head in children.

ligamenta flava.d: Ligaments joining adjacent laminae, yellow because of their elastic fibres; in lumbar puncture resistance is felt as the needle passes through them.

limbus of sphenoid.d: Posterior edge of the jugum of the sphenoid.

linea alba.d: Fibrous band from the xiphoid to the symphysis where the aponeuroses of the three flat abdominal muscles fuse in the midline; wider above the umbilicus, it gives a bloodless route for surgical incisions.

linea aspera.d: Rough line on the back of the femoral shaft; the adductors and the vasti attach to it.

lingual gyrus.d: Gyrus below the calcarine sulcus; it represents the upper visual field.

lingual nerve.d: Carries general sensation from the anterior two thirds of the tongue and receives taste and parasympathetic fibres from the chorda tympani. It can be injured when extracting lower wisdom teeth.

lingual surface of tooth.d: Surface of a tooth facing the tongue.

lingula of cerebellum.d: Most anterior lobule of the vermis; it lies on the superior medullary velum.

lingular vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

long head of biceps brachii.d: Head arising from the supraglenoid tubercle and passing through the shoulder joint; its tendon runs in the intertubercular sulcus, and rupture produces the 'Popeye' sign.

long head of biceps femoris.d: Hamstring head arising from the ischial tuberosity; extends the hip and flexes the knee. Tibial nerve.

long head of triceps brachii.d: Arises from the infraglenoid tubercle; it separates the triangular and quadrangular spaces. It also extends the shoulder.

long limb of incus.d: Long limb of the incus extending downwards; it runs parallel to the handle of the malleus.

long plantar ligament.d: The longest tarsal ligament, from the lower surface of the calcaneus to the cuboid and metatarsal bases; it roofs the canal of the fibularis longus tendon and supports the lateral arch.

long posterior ciliary arteries.d: Supply the iris and ciliary body.

long thoracic nerve.d: Arises from the C5–C7 roots, runs on the lateral chest wall and supplies serratus anterior; injury during mastectomy causes a winged scapula.

longissimus capitis muscle.d: Part of longissimus inserting into the mastoid process; extends the head and turns it to the same side.

longissimus colli muscle.d: Cervical part of the longissimus column.

longissimus thoracis muscle.d: Trunk part of the middle and longest column of erector spinae.

longus capitis muscle.d: Prevertebral muscle from the transverse processes of C3–C6 to the basilar part of the occipital bone; flexes the head forwards.

longus colli muscle.d: Prevertebral muscle in front of the vertebral bodies from the anterior tubercle of the atlas to T3; flexes the neck forwards.

lower canine.d: Tooth at the corner of the mouth with the longest root; tears food.

lower first molar tooth.d: The first permanent tooth to erupt (age 6); it has a broad chewing surface and two roots.

lower first premolar.d: Premolar with two cusps; begins crushing food.

lower lateral incisor.d: Single-rooted incisor next to the central incisor.

lower medial incisor.d: Sharp-edged, single-rooted middle front tooth; cuts food by biting. It erupts at 6–8 years in the permanent dentition.

lower second molar tooth.d: Second molar erupting around age 12; it grinds food.

lower second premolar.d: Second premolar; usually single-rooted, with no counterpart in the milk teeth (it replaces the milk molars).

lumbar arteries.d: Four pairs of segmental branches from the back of the aorta; supply the posterior abdominal wall and spine.

lumbrical muscles of foot.d: Four small muscles arising from the flexor digitorum longus tendons; they flex the MTP joints.

lumbrical muscles of hand.d: Four small muscles from the deep flexor tendons to the extensor hood; they flex the MCP and extend the IP joints. The 1st–2nd are supplied by the median nerve, the 3rd–4th by the ulnar nerve.

lunate bone.d: Half-moon-shaped bone in the middle of the proximal row; the most commonly dislocated carpal bone, and its anterior dislocation can compress the median nerve in the carpal tunnel. Its avascular necrosis is Kienböck's disease.

lunate sulcus.d: Crescent-shaped sulcus sometimes present on the lateral surface of the occipital pole.

lunate surface.d: Crescent-shaped articular surface of the acetabulum; the cartilage-covered part in contact with the femoral head.

lunotriquetral interosseous ligament.d: Joins the lunate and triquetrum; a VISI deformity develops when it tears.

major alar cartilage.d: U-shaped cartilage shaping the tip of the nose and the rims of the nostrils; made up of medial and lateral crura.

malleolar fossa.d: Fossa on the posteromedial surface of the lateral malleolus; the posterior talofibular ligament attaches to it.

malleolar groove of fibula.d: Groove behind the lateral malleolus; the tendons of the fibular muscles pass through it.

malleolar groove of tibia.d: Groove behind the medial malleolus; the tibialis posterior and FDL tendons pass through it.

malleus.d: The outermost ossicle, attached to the eardrum; its handle (manubrium) is embedded in the inner surface of the drum, and tensor tympani attaches to it.

mamillary body.d: Paired swelling on the posterior floor of the hypothalamus; part of the Papez circuit, damaged in Wernicke encephalopathy.

mandible.d: The only movable bone of the face; its condyles form the temporomandibular joint with the temporal bone. The inferior alveolar nerve runs in the mandibular canal.

mandibular symphysis.d: Site where the two halves of the mandible fuse in the midline after birth.

manubrium of sternum.d: Upper part of the sternum; articulates with the clavicles and the 1st costal cartilages, and bears the jugular notch on its upper border.

marginal artery.d: Chain of anastomoses along the edge of the colon joining the mesenteric arteries; weak at the splenic flexure (Griffiths' point, ischaemic colitis).

masseter.d: Runs from the zygomatic arch to the angle of the mandible; one of the strongest muscles for its weight, it closes the jaw. Masseteric nerve (V3).

masseteric fascia.d: Fascia covering masseter, continuous with the parotid fascia.

mastoid angle of parietal bone.d: Posteroinferior angle facing the mastoid region.

mastoid border of occipital bone.d: Border that articulates with the mastoid part of the temporal bone.

mastoid notch.d: Notch on the medial side of the mastoid process; the posterior belly of digastric arises here.

mastoid process.d: Projection felt behind the ear; it is filled with air cells and SCM attaches to it.

maxilla.d: Paired bone forming the upper jaw, the front of the hard palate, the floor of the orbit and the lateral wall of the nasal cavity; it contains the maxillary sinus, the largest paranasal sinus.

maxillary artery.d: Large terminal branch of the external carotid; in the infratemporal and pterygopalatine fossae it gives branches to the teeth, muscles of mastication, nose and dura.

maxillary dental arch.d: Upper dental arch; it carries 16 permanent teeth.

maxillary nerve.d: Sensory division leaving through the foramen rotundum; supplies the midface, upper teeth, palate and maxillary sinus.

maxillary surface of greater wing.d: Surface of the greater wing facing the pterygopalatine fossa; the foramen rotundum opens here.

maxillary veins.d: Veins coming from the pterygoid plexus.

medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.d: Carries sensation from the skin of the inner forearm.

medial basal segment of left lung (svii).tr: Medial basal segment of left lung (svii)

medial basal segment of right lung (svii.tr: Medial basal segment of right lung (svii)

medial basal segmental artery of left lu.tr: Medial basal segmental artery of left lung
medial basal segmental artery of left lu.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis medialis pulmonis sinistri
medial basal segmental artery of left lu.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

medial basal segmental artery of right l.tr: Medial basal segmental artery of right lung
medial basal segmental artery of right l.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis medialis pulmonis dextri
medial basal segmental artery of right l.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

medial basal segmental bronchus of left.tr: Medial basal segmental bronchus of left lung (bvii)
medial basal segmental bronchus of left.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis medialis (B VII) sinister

medial basal segmental bronchus of right.tr: Medial basal segmental bronchus of right lung (bvii)
medial basal segmental bronchus of right.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis medialis (B VII) dexter

medial border of scapula.d: Medial border facing the spine; the rhomboids and serratus anterior attach to it.

medial brachial cutaneous nerve.d: Nerve from the medial cord carrying sensation from the skin of the inner arm.

medial circumflex femoral artery.d: Winds round the back of the femoral neck and is the main supply of the femoral head; its injury in neck fractures causes avascular necrosis.

medial circumflex femoral veins.d: Accompanies the artery of the same name.

medial condyle of femur.d: Medial condyle of the femur; it is longer and reaches lower than the lateral condyle, producing the carrying angle.

medial condyle of tibia.d: Medial condyle of the tibia; semimembranosus attaches to its back.

medial crural cutaneous branches of saph.tr: Medial crural cutaneous branches of saphenous nerve
medial crural cutaneous branches of saph.la: Rami cutanei cruris mediales nervi sapheni
medial crural cutaneous branches of saph.d: Sensation from the inner side of the leg.

medial cuneiform bone.d: The largest of the three cuneiforms; articulates with the 1st metatarsal and gives attachment to tibialis anterior and fibularis longus.

medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot.tr: Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot
medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot.d: Branch of the superficial fibular nerve to the medial part of the dorsum of the foot.

medial epicondyle of femur.d: Prominence on the medial condyle; the medial collateral ligament attaches to it.

medial epicondyle of humerus.d: Medial epicondyle of the humerus; common origin of the forearm flexors, with the ulnar nerve passing behind it.

medial femoral intermuscular septum.d: Fascial wall separating the anterior and medial thigh compartments.

medial geniculate body.d: Thalamic relay nucleus of the auditory pathway; the auditory radiation goes from here to Heschl's gyrus.

medial head of flexor hallucis brevis.tr: Medial head of flexor hallucis brevis
medial head of flexor hallucis brevis.la: Caput mediale musculi flexoris hallucis brevis
medial head of flexor hallucis brevis.d: Head attaching to the medial sesamoid.

medial head of gastrocnemius.d: The larger calf head, arising from the medial condyle of the femur; it tears in 'tennis leg'. The muscle raises the heel and flexes the knee. Tibial nerve.

medial head of triceps brachii.d: Deep head arising below the radial groove; all three heads insert into the olecranon and extend the elbow.

medial intercondylar tubercle.d: Medial tubercle of the intercondylar eminence.

medial intermuscular septum of arm.d: The ulnar nerve pierces this septum to enter the posterior compartment.

medial lip of linea aspera.d: Medial lip of the linea aspera; vastus medialis and the adductors attach to it.

medial malleolar facet.d: Comma-shaped surface that articulates with the medial malleolus.

medial malleolus.d: Lower end of the tibia felt under the skin; the great saphenous vein passes in front of it (emergency venous access).

medial meniscus.d: C-shaped medial meniscus; attached to the tibial collateral ligament, it is less mobile and tears more often ('unhappy triad').

medial occipital artery.d: Gives the calcarine and parieto-occipital branches.

medial occipitotemporal gyrus (parahippo.d: Gyrus beside the hippocampus; its anterior end curls into the uncus, the part that herniates in tentorial herniation.

medial part of longitudinal arch of foot.tr: Medial part of longitudinal arch of foot

medial patellar retinaculum.d: Extension of the vastus medialis aponeurosis; the medial patellofemoral ligament within it prevents lateral dislocation of the patella.

medial pectoral nerve.d: Arises from the medial cord and supplies pectoralis minor and major.

medial plantar artery.d: Small terminal branch supplying the medial part of the sole.

medial plantar nerve.d: Sensation from the medial sole and the medial three and a half toes; supplies abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis (the foot's counterpart of the median nerve).

medial plantar veins.d: Drain the medial part of the sole.

medial pontine branches of basilar arter.tr: Medial pontine branches of basilar artery
medial pontine branches of basilar arter.d: Perforating branches supplying the middle of the pons.

medial process of calcaneal tuberosity.d: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity; abductor hallucis and the plantar aponeurosis arise here.

medial pterygoid muscle.d: Runs from the pterygoid fossa to the inner surface of the angle of the mandible; with masseter it forms a sling for the mandible and closes the jaw.

medial pterygoid plate.d: Medial plate of the pterygoid process; the pterygoid hamulus lies at its tip.

medial rectus muscle.d: The strongest eye muscle, turning the eye inwards (adduction); oculomotor nerve.

medial reticulospinal tract.d: Pathway from the pontine reticular formation that increases extensor tone.

medial segmental artery of left lung.tr: Medial segmental artery of left lung

medial segmental artery of right lung.tr: Medial segmental artery of right lung
medial segmental artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

medial segmental bronchus of right lung.tr: Medial segmental bronchus of right lung (bv)

medial subtendinous bursa of gastrocnemi.d: Between the medial head and the capsule; joined with the semimembranosus bursa it can form a Baker's cyst.

medial supracondylar line.d: Continuation of the linea aspera down to the medial condyle; it ends at the adductor tubercle.

medial sural cutaneous nerve.d: Branch of the tibial nerve that joins to form the sural nerve.

medial surface of arytenoid cartilage.d: Surface facing the opposite arytenoid; covered by mucosa, it bounds the posterior part of the rima glottidis.

medial surface of fibula.d: Medial surface of the fibula; the extensor muscles of the anterior compartment arise from it.

medial surface of tibia.d: Broad anteromedial surface just under the skin; bone grafts and intraosseous access can be taken here.

medial surface of ulna.d: Medial surface of the ulna; FDP arises from it.

medial talocalcaneal ligament.d: Binds the medial tubercle of the talus to the sustentaculum tali.

medial tubercle.d: Medial tubercle of the posterior process; the deltoid ligament attaches to it.

medial vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

medial vestibulospinal tract.d: Descending pathway stabilising head and neck posture.

median antebrachial vein.d: Drains the front of the forearm.

median cricothyroid ligament.d: Ligament between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages; cricothyrotomy is performed here to open an emergency airway.

median cubital vein.d: Links the cephalic and basilic veins in the cubital fossa; the vein most used for taking blood.

median nerve.d: Formed by the union of the lateral and medial cords; supplies most forearm flexors, the thenar muscles and the palmar skin of the lateral three and a half fingers. Compression in the carpal tunnel is the commonest entrapment neuropathy ('ape hand', 'hand of benediction').

median sacral artery.d: Thin artery arising behind the bifurcation and descending in front of the sacrum.

median sacral crest.d: Midline ridge formed by the fused spinous processes.

median thyrohyoid ligament.d: Thick middle part of the thyrohyoid membrane.

medulla oblongata.d: Lowest part of the brainstem, continuous with the spinal cord at the foramen magnum. It contains the respiratory and circulatory centres, the nuclei of IX–XII and the pyramidal decussation.

meningeal branch of maxillary nerve.d: Small branch carrying sensation from the dura of the middle cranial fossa.

meniscopatellar ligament.d: Capsular thickening joining the edge of the patella to the menisci.

mental branch of inferior alveolar arter.tr: Mental branch of inferior alveolar artery
mental branch of inferior alveolar arter.d: Emerges at the mental foramen and supplies the chin.

mental foramen.d: Foramen below the second premolar; the mental nerve and artery emerge from it.

mental nerve.d: Branch leaving through the mental foramen and supplying the skin of the lower lip and chin.

mental tubercle.d: Prominence on each side of the mental protuberance.

mentalis muscle.d: Raises and wrinkles the skin of the chin and pushes the lower lip forwards (pouting).

mesial surface of tooth.d: Surface of a tooth facing the front (midline) of the dental arch.

metacarpal bones.d: Five long bones forming the skeleton of the palm; they articulate with the proximal phalanges of the fingers.

metatarsal interosseous ligaments.d: Interosseous ligaments between adjacent metatarsal bases.

midbrain.d: Part of the brainstem between the pons and diencephalon; formed by the tectum (colliculi), tegmentum (red nucleus, nuclei of III and IV) and the peduncles.

middle cardiac vein.d: Runs in the posterior interventricular groove and opens into the coronary sinus.

middle cells of ethmoid bone.d: Air cells forming the ethmoidal bulla; they open into the middle meatus.

middle cerebral artery (m1-segment).d: Continuation of the internal carotid; runs in the lateral fissure. Its lenticulostriate branches supply the internal capsule; occlusion causes marked paralysis of the opposite face and arm and (on the dominant side) aphasia.

middle cerebral artery (m3 segment).d: Segment on the inner surface of the opercula.

middle cerebral artery (m3-segment).d: The opercular segment, from which the cortical branches arise.

middle clinoid process.d: Small process at the anterolateral corner of the sella turcica; sometimes fused with the anterior clinoid.

middle colic artery.d: Supplies the transverse colon in the transverse mesocolon.

middle collateral artery.d: Joins the anastomosis around the elbow.

middle facet for calcaneus.d: Middle surface that articulates with the sustentaculum tali.

middle frontal gyrus.d: Its posterior part contains the frontal eye field (Brodmann 8); with damage the eyes look towards the side of the lesion.

middle glenohumeral ligament.d: Limits anterior translation in moderate abduction.

middle layer of thoracolumbar fascia.d: Layer between erector spinae and quadratus lumborum.

middle lobar artery of left lung.tr: Middle lobar artery of left lung

middle lobar artery of right lung.tr: Middle lobar artery of right lung
middle lobar artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to the middle lobe of the right lung.

middle meningeal artery.d: Enters the skull through the foramen spinosum; torn in pterion fractures, causing an epidural haematoma (lucid interval).

middle phalanx of fifth finger of foot.d: Middle bone of the little toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

middle phalanx of fifth finger of hand.d: Middle bone of the little finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.

middle phalanx of fourth finger of foot.d: Middle bone of the 4th toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

middle phalanx of fourth finger of hand.d: Middle bone of the ring finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.

middle phalanx of second finger of foot.d: Middle bone of the 2nd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

middle phalanx of second finger of hand.d: Middle bone of the index finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.

middle phalanx of third finger of foot.d: Middle bone of the 3rd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

middle phalanx of third finger of hand.d: Middle bone of the middle finger; it lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.

middle pharyngeal constrictor.d: Fan-shaped constrictor arising from the horns of the hyoid bone.

middle temporal gyrus.d: Middle gyrus of the lateral surface of the temporal lobe.

motor nucleus of facial nerve.d: Nucleus supplying the muscles of facial expression; the part for the forehead muscles receives bilateral cortical control.

motor root of trigeminal nerve.d: Root passing below the ganglion to join the mandibular nerve and supply the muscles of mastication.

multifidus lumborum muscle.d: Deep muscle, thickest in the lumbar region, spanning 2–4 segments; it provides segmental stability and wastes in low back pain.

muscular branches of axillary nerve.d: Branches to deltoid and teres minor.

muscular branches of deep fibular nerve.tr: Muscular branches of deep fibular nerve
muscular branches of deep fibular nerve.d: Branches to the muscles of the anterior compartment.

muscular branches of median nerve.d: Branches to the muscles of the anterior compartment of the forearm.

muscular branches of radial nerve.d: Branches to triceps, brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus.

muscular branches of ulnar nerve.d: Branches to FCU and the ulnar half of FDP.

muscular process.d: Laterally projecting process of the arytenoid; the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles attach here to open or close the vocal folds.

musculocutaneous nerve.d: Arises from the lateral cord and pierces coracobrachialis; supplies the anterior arm muscles and carries sensation from the lateral forearm.

musculophrenic artery.d: Supplies the diaphragm and the lower intercostal spaces.

musculophrenic veins.d: Drain the margin of the diaphragm.

mylohyoid branch of inferior alveolar ar.tr: Mylohyoid branch of inferior alveolar artery

mylohyoid line.d: Oblique line on the inner surface of the mandible; mylohyoid, which forms the floor of the mouth, attaches to it.

mylohyoid muscle.d: Flat muscle forming the floor of the mouth (oral diaphragm); supplied by the nerve to mylohyoid (V3), it raises the floor of the mouth and the tongue during swallowing.

nasal bone.d: Small, paired, rectangular bone forming the bridge of the nose; the most commonly fractured facial bone.

nasal margin of frontal bone.d: Margin that articulates with the nasal bones.

nasal part of frontal bone.d: Part of the frontal bone extending to the root of the nose.

nasal septal cartilage.d: Quadrilateral hyaline cartilage forming the front of the nasal septum; its deviation causes nasal obstruction.

nasal spine of frontal bone.d: Small spine supporting the nasal septum.

nasalis muscle.d: Its transverse part narrows the nostril and its alar part widens it.

nasolacrimal duct.d: Duct from the lacrimal sac opening into the inferior meatus; it may be blocked in newborns.

navicular articular surface.d: Surface of the head of the talus that articulates with the navicular.

navicular bone.d: Boat-shaped tarsal bone between the head of the talus and the cuneiforms; tibialis posterior attaches to its medial tuberosity, and it is the keystone of the medial longitudinal arch.

neck of femur.d: Neck joining the head to the shaft; it often fractures in the elderly and can lead to avascular necrosis of the head.
