neck of fibula.d: Neck below the head; the common fibular nerve lies against the bone here, and a fracture can cause foot drop.

neck of malleus.d: Constriction between the head and handle of the malleus.

neck of radius.d: Constriction between the head and the tuberosity.

neck of rib.d: Part between the head and the tubercle.

neck of scapula.d: Constriction just medial to the glenoid.

neck of talus.d: Constriction between the head and the body; after a fracture here avascular necrosis of the body is common.

neck of tooth.d: Constriction where the crown meets the root; the gum ends here.

nerve to mylohyoid muscle.d: Branch supplying mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric.

nerve to quadratus femoris muscle.d: Branch supplying quadratus femoris and the inferior gemellus.

ninth rib.d: 9th rib: a false (vertebrochondral) rib; its cartilage joins the costal cartilage above.

node of arch of azygos vein.tr: Node of arch of azygos vein

nodule of vermis.d: Vermian part of the flocculonodular lobe; the vestibulocerebellum.

non-coronary leaflet.d: The aortic cusp behind which no coronary artery arises.

nuchal ligament.d: Triangular fibroelastic ligament from the occipital bone to the C7 spine; it helps support the weight of the head and gives attachment to trapezius and splenius.

nucleus ambiguus.d: Motor nucleus supplying the pharynx, larynx and soft palate (IX, X, XI); its lesion causes dysphagia and hoarseness (Wallenberg syndrome).

nucleus of abducens nerve.d: Beneath the facial colliculus in the floor of the fourth ventricle; it contains the lateral gaze centre.

nucleus of accessory nerve.d: Nucleus in the anterior horn of C1–C5 supplying sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.

nucleus of hypoglossal nerve.d: Motor nucleus in the floor of the fourth ventricle supplying the tongue muscles.

nucleus of oculomotor nerve.d: At the level of the superior colliculus; supplies most eye muscles and levator palpebrae.

nucleus of solitary tract.d: Sensory nucleus receiving taste (VII, IX, X) and visceral sensation (baroreceptors, chemoreceptors).

nucleus of trochlear nerve.d: At the level of the inferior colliculus; its fibres cross and leave the back of the brainstem.

nucleus proprius.d: Main sensory nucleus of the dorsal horn.

nucleus pulposus c2-c3.d: Gel-like centre of the C2-C3 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus c3-c4.d: Gel-like centre of the C3-C4 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus c4-c5.d: Gel-like centre of the C4-C5 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus c5-c6.d: Gel-like centre of the C5-C6 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus c6-c7.d: Gel-like centre of the C6-C7 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus c7-t1.d: Gel-like centre of the C7-T1 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus l1-l2.d: Gel-like centre of the L1-L2 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus l2-l3.d: Gel-like centre of the L2-L3 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus l3-l4.d: Gel-like centre of the L3-L4 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus l4-l5.d: Gel-like centre of the L4-L5 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus l5-s1.d: Gel-like centre of the L5-S1 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t1-t2.d: Gel-like centre of the T1-T2 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t10-t11.d: Gel-like centre of the T10-T11 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t11-t12.d: Gel-like centre of the T11-T12 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t12-l1.d: Gel-like centre of the T12-L1 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t2-t3.d: Gel-like centre of the T2-T3 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t3-t4.d: Gel-like centre of the T3-T4 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t4-t5.d: Gel-like centre of the T4-T5 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t5-t6.d: Gel-like centre of the T5-T6 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t6-t7.d: Gel-like centre of the T6-T7 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t7-t8.d: Gel-like centre of the T7-T8 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t8-t9.d: Gel-like centre of the T8-T9 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

nucleus pulposus t9-t10.d: Gel-like centre of the T9-T10 disc; a remnant of the notochord. When the annulus fibrosus tears it can herniate posterolaterally and compress a nerve root.

oblique cord.d: Small fibrous band running from the ulnar tuberosity to the radius.

oblique head of adductor hallucis.d: Head arising from the bases of the 2nd–4th metatarsals.

oblique head of adductor pollicis.d: Arises from the capitate and the bases of the 2nd–3rd metacarpals.

oblique line of mandible.d: Oblique line on the outer surface; muscles of the corner of the mouth attach to it.

oblique line of thyroid cartilage.d: Oblique line on the outer surface of the lamina; sternothyroid, thyrohyoid and the inferior constrictor attach to it.

oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.d: Posterior fibres of cricothyroid, which tenses the vocal folds; it is the only laryngeal muscle supplied by the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

oblique popliteal ligament.d: Extension of the semimembranosus tendon that reinforces the back of the capsule obliquely.

obliquus inferior capitis muscle.d: Runs from the spine of the axis to the transverse process of the atlas; the only 'capitis' muscle that does not attach to the skull, it rotates the atlas on the axis.

obliquus superior capitis muscle.d: Runs from the transverse process of the atlas to the occiput; extends the head and tilts it sideways.

oblong fovea.d: Lower pit on the anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; vocalis attaches here.

obturator artery.d: Passes through the obturator canal to the thigh; sometimes arises from the external iliac artery ('corona mortis', dangerous in hernia surgery).

obturator crest.d: Ridge on the superior pubic ramus; the pubofemoral ligament attaches to it.

obturator externus.d: Runs from the outer surface of the obturator membrane to the trochanteric fossa; a lateral rotator supplied by the obturator nerve.

obturator foramen.d: Large opening surrounded by the pubis and ischium; closed by the obturator membrane, with the obturator vessels and nerve passing through the canal at its top.

obturator groove.d: Groove on the lower surface of the superior pubic ramus; forms the roof of the obturator canal.

obturator internus.d: Arises from the inner surface of the obturator foramen and leaves through the lesser sciatic foramen; rotates the hip laterally.

obturator membrane.d: Fibrous membrane closing the obturator foramen; the obturator vessels and nerve pass through the obturator canal at its upper edge.

obturator nerve.d: Arises from L2–L4 and passes through the obturator canal into the thigh; supplies the adductors. Its pain may be referred to the knee.

occipital artery.d: Supplies the back of the neck and the posterior scalp.

occipital bone.d: Bone forming the back and base of the skull; the spinal cord and vertebral arteries pass through its foramen magnum, and its condyles articulate with the atlas.

occipital border of parietal bone.d: Border forming the lambdoid suture with the occipital bone.

occipital condyle.d: Articular projection on each side of the foramen magnum; forms with the atlas the joint that produces the 'yes' movement.

occipital margin of temporal bone.d: Margin that articulates with the occipital bone.

occipital plane.d: Smooth area above the superior nuchal line.

occipital pole.d: Most posterior tip of the hemisphere; macular vision is represented here.

occipital sinus.d: Small sinus in the falx cerebelli.

occipital vein.d: Drains the scalp of the back of the head.

occipitalis muscle.d: Pulls the galea backwards; posterior auricular nerve (VII).

occipitotemporal sulcus (lateral part*).d: Separates the inferior temporal and fusiform gyri.

occlusal surface of tooth.d: Chewing surface that meets the opposing tooth.

oculomotor nerve (iii).d: Carries fibres to four eye muscles, levator palpebrae and the parasympathetic pupil fibres. In its palsy the eye turns down and out with ptosis and mydriasis; a posterior communicating aneurysm is a common cause.

olecranon.d: Projection forming the point of the elbow; triceps inserts into it.

olecranon fossa.d: Deep fossa on the lower posterior surface of the humerus; the olecranon enters it when the elbow is extended.

olfactory nerve (i).d: Fibres from the olfactory epithelium passing through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb; anterior skull base fractures cause anosmia.

olfactory sulcus.d: Groove in which the olfactory bulb and tract lie.

olive.d: Oval swelling on the side of the medulla; the inferior olivary nucleus inside sends climbing fibres to the cerebellum.

omohyoid muscle.d: Two-bellied infrahyoid muscle joined by an intermediate tendon, running from the upper border of the scapula to the hyoid; supplied by the ansa cervicalis, it depresses the hyoid.

opening of frontal sinus.d: Opening of the frontal sinus; it drains through the frontonasal duct into the middle meatus.

opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.tr: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus
opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus.d: With the triangular part it forms Broca's speech area (Brodmann 44); damage in the dominant hemisphere causes motor aphasia.

ophthalmic artery.d: First branch of the internal carotid; enters the orbit through the optic canal and supplies the eye, retina, forehead and part of the nose.

ophthalmic nerve.d: First, sensory division of the trigeminal; supplies the forehead, bridge of the nose and cornea and is the afferent limb of the corneal reflex. In herpes zoster ophthalmicus, involvement of the nose tip (Hutchinson sign) suggests eye involvement.

opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand.d: Turns the 5th metacarpal forwards and medially, deepening the hollow of the palm.

opponens pollicis muscle.d: Inserts along the whole radial border of the 1st metacarpal and brings the thumb against the other fingers (opposition). Median nerve.

optic canal.d: Canal in the lesser wing; the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery pass through it.

optic chiasm.d: Where the optic nerves meet; the fibres from the nasal retina cross. Compression by a pituitary tumour causes bitemporal hemianopia.

optic nerve (ii).d: Axons of retinal ganglion cells; it passes through the optic canal and, being wrapped in meninges, shows papilloedema when intracranial pressure rises.

optic tract.d: Visual pathway from the chiasm to the lateral geniculate body; its damage causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

orbicularis oris muscle.d: Sphincter muscle around the lips; closes and purses the lips (whistling).

orbital gyri.d: Inferior surface of the frontal lobe above the orbit; involved in decision making and impulse control.

orbital gyri (frontomarginal gyrus and s.d: Gyrus on the lower margin of the frontal pole.

orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus.tr: Orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus
orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus.d: Part of the inferior frontal gyrus above the orbit.

orbital part of orbicularis oculi.d: Outer fibres that close the eye tightly (screwing up the eyes); facial nerve.

orbital plate of frontal bone.d: Thin bony plate forming the roof of the orbit; it is the floor of the anterior cranial fossa.

orbital sulci (h-shaped orbital sulci*).d: Sulci on the orbital surface arranged like the letter H.

orbital sulci (lateral orbital sulcus*).d: Lateral sulcus of the orbital surface.

orbital surface of frontal bone.d: Surface of the orbital roof facing the eye.

orbital surface of greater wing.d: Surface forming the lateral wall of the orbit.

orbitofrontal branches of anterior cereb.tr: Orbitofrontal branches of anterior cerebral artery
orbitofrontal branches of anterior cereb.d: Supply the orbital surface of the frontal lobe.

outer lip of iliac crest.d: Outer lip of the iliac crest; external oblique, TFL and the fascia lata attach to it.

palatine bone.d: Paired L-shaped bone forming the back of the hard palate and the back of the lateral wall of the nasal cavity; the vessels and nerve of the same name pass through the greater palatine foramen.

palatopharyngeus muscle.d: Muscle running in the palatopharyngeal arch; during swallowing it shortens the pharynx and helps close off the nasopharynx.

palmar aponeurosis.d: Thick triangular fascia in the palm; thickening and shortening of its bands to the bases of the fingers is Dupuytren's contracture.

palmar branch of median nerve.d: Cutaneous branch passing above the carpal tunnel; this is why thenar skin sensation is preserved in carpal tunnel syndrome.

palmar branch of ulnar nerve.d: Cutaneous branch to the hypothenar skin.

palmar capitohamate ligament.d: Binds the capitate and hamate in front.

palmar carpal branch of radial artery.tr: Palmar carpal branch of radial artery

palmar carpometacarpal ligaments.d: Bind the distal carpal row to the metacarpal bases in front.

palmar digital veins.d: Drain the palmar surface of the fingers.

palmar interossei muscles.d: Three muscles that bring the fingers towards the middle finger ('PAD'). Ulnar nerve (deep branch).

palmar interphalangeal ligaments.tr: Palmar ligaments of interphalangeal joints (volar plates)
palmar interphalangeal ligaments.d: Thick plates on the front of the finger joints; prevent hyperextension.

palmar lunotriquetral ligament.d: Binds the lunate and triquetrum in front.

palmar metacarpal arteries.d: Branches arising from the deep arch.

palmar metacarpal ligaments.d: Bind the metacarpal bases to each other in front.

palmar radio-ulnar ligament.d: Ligament holding the distal radio-ulnar joint in front; part of the TFCC.

palmar scaphotriquetral ligament.d: Ligament running from the scaphoid to the triquetrum in front.

palmar surfaces of digits of hand.tr: Palmar surfaces of digits of hand

palmar trapezoideocapitate ligament.d: Binds the trapezoid and capitate in front.

palmaris longus muscle.d: Muscle with a long thin tendon inserting into the palmar aponeurosis; absent in about 14% of people, it is used for tendon grafts.

palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.d: Thin fibres within the eyelids; produce involuntary blinking. In facial palsy the eye cannot close (lagophthalmos).

paracentral gyrus and sulcus*.d: Continuation of the pre- and postcentral gyri on the medial surface; the motor and sensory area of the leg and foot (affected in anterior cerebral artery occlusion).

paracentral sulcus.d: Sulcus bounding the paracentral lobule in front.

parietal bone.d: Paired bone forming the roof and side walls of the skull; branches of the middle meningeal artery run in the grooves on its inner surface.

parietal branches of middle cerebral art.tr: Parietal branches of middle cerebral artery
parietal branches of middle cerebral art.d: Supply the lateral surface of the parietal lobe.

parietal eminence.d: The most prominent point of the parietal bone; the ossification centre.

parietal foramen.d: Small hole near the sagittal border; an emissary vein passes through it.

parietal margin of frontal bone.d: Margin forming the coronal suture with the parietal bones.

parietal margin of greater wing.d: Tip that articulates with the parietal bone; it contributes to the pterion.

parieto-occipital sulcus.d: Deep sulcus on the medial surface separating the parietal and occipital lobes.

pars interarticularis of vertebral arch.d: Part between the superior and inferior articular processes; spondylolysis occurs here.

patella.d: The largest sesamoid bone in the body; it develops within the quadriceps femoris tendon and strengthens knee extension by lengthening the muscle's lever arm.

patellar anastomosis.d: Network of genicular arteries around the patella.

patellar ligament.d: Continuation of the quadriceps tendon from the patella to the tibial tuberosity; the knee reflex (L3–L4) is elicited by tapping it.

patellar surface of femur.d: Articular surface in front of the condyles; forms the patellofemoral joint with the patella.

pecten pubis.d: Sharp edge on the superior pubic ramus; pectineus and the pectineal ligament attach to it.

pectineal line of femur.d: Line running from the lesser trochanter to the linea aspera; pectineus inserts here.

pectineus muscle.d: Quadrilateral muscle from the pecten pubis to the femur; forms part of the floor of the femoral triangle. Femoral nerve (sometimes obturator).

pectoral fascia.d: Fascia covering pectoralis major; the breast lies on it, separated by the retromammary space.

pectoralis major muscle.d: Fan-shaped muscle whose clavicular, sternocostal and abdominal parts insert into the crest of the greater tubercle; adducts and medially rotates the arm. Medial and lateral pectoral nerves.

pectoralis minor muscle.d: Runs from the 3rd–5th ribs to the coracoid process; an important landmark dividing the axillary artery into three parts. It pulls the scapula forwards and down. Medial pectoral nerve.

pedicle of vertebral arch.d: Short thick bone joining the body to the arch; pedicle screws are placed here.

peduncle of flocculus.d: White matter band connecting the flocculus to the nodule.

pelvic surface of sacrum.d: Concave anterior surface of the sacrum facing the pelvis; piriformis arises here.

perforating branches of plantar metatars.tr: Perforating branches of plantar metatarsal arteries
perforating branches of plantar metatars.d: Branches joining the arteries of the sole with those of the dorsum of the foot.

perforating femoral arteries.d: Branches that pierce adductor magnus to supply the posterior thigh muscles.

perforating veins.d: Valved veins connecting the superficial and deep veins; their incompetence contributes to varicose veins.

pericallosal artery.d: Branch of the anterior cerebral artery running over the corpus callosum.

pericardium.d: Two-layered sac around the heart and the roots of the great vessels: the fibrous pericardium outside and the serous pericardium, with parietal and visceral layers, inside. Attached below to the central tendon of the diaphragm and in front to the sternum; a rapid rise of fluid between the layers causes cardiac tamponade.

petrous part of temporal bone.d: Hard pyramidal part housing the inner and middle ear.

phalanges of hand.d: Bones of the fingers: 14 phalanges, two in the thumb and three in each of the other fingers.

pharyngeal tubercle.d: Prominence on the lower surface of the basilar part; the fibrous raphe of the pharynx attaches to it.

phrenic nerve.d: The only motor nerve to the diaphragm, from the cervical plexus (C3–C5, mainly C4). It descends on the front of scalenus anterior, enters the chest between the subclavian artery and vein and runs on the side of the pericardium in front of the lung root to the diaphragm; the right passes beside the superior vena cava, the left beside the aortic arch. Subdiaphragmatic irritation causes pain referred to the shoulder.

piriformis muscle.d: Runs from the front of the sacrum to the greater trochanter; a key structure dividing the greater sciatic foramen into upper and lower parts. The sciatic nerve sometimes passes through the muscle (piriformis syndrome).

pisiform bone.d: Sesamoid carpal bone developed within the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon; forms the medial wall of Guyon's canal.

pisohamate ligament.d: Ligament from the pisiform to the hook of the hamate, continuing flexor carpi ulnaris; forms the floor of Guyon's canal.

pisometacarpal ligament.d: Ligament from the pisiform to the base of the 5th metacarpal, transmitting the pull of flexor carpi ulnaris.

pisotriquetral ligament.d: Capsular ligament of the pisotriquetral joint.

plantar aponeurosis.d: Thick fibrous sheet from the calcaneus to the toes; it tightens the arch (windlass mechanism), and its inflammation is plantar fasciitis.

plantar arch.d: Arch formed by the lateral plantar artery and the deep plantar artery.

plantar calcaneocuboid ligament.d: Short, strong ligament from the lower surface of the calcaneus to the cuboid; supports the lateral arch.

plantar calcaneonavicular ligament.d: The 'spring' ligament running from the sustentaculum tali to the navicular and supporting the head of the talus from below; it supports the medial longitudinal arch.

plantar cuboideonavicular ligament.d: Binds the cuboid and navicular from below.

plantar cuneocuboid ligament.d: Binds the lateral cuneiform to the cuboid from below.

plantar cuneonavicular ligaments.d: Ligaments binding the navicular to the cuneiforms from below.

plantar digital veins.d: Drain the plantar surface of the toes.

plantar intercuneiform ligaments.d: Bind the cuneiforms to each other from below; support the transverse arch.

plantar interossei muscles.d: Three muscles that bring the 3rd–5th toes towards the 2nd toe.

plantar interphalangeal ligaments.tr: Plantar ligaments of interphalangeal joints of foot
plantar interphalangeal ligaments.d: Ligaments on the lower surface of the toe joints.

plantar metatarsal arteries.d: Branches running from the plantar arch to the toes.

plantar metatarsal ligaments.d: Bind the metatarsal bases to each other from below.

plantar metatarsal veins.d: Open into the plantar venous arch.

plantar metatarsophalangeal ligaments.d: Thick fibrocartilaginous plates on the lower surface of the joints; the flexor tendons pass over them.

plantar surfaces of digits of foot.tr: Plantar surfaces of digits of foot

plantar tarsometatarsal ligaments.d: Ligaments reinforcing the Lisfranc joint from below.

plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longu.tr: Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longus
plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longu.la: Vagina plantaris tendinis musculi fibularis longi
plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longu.d: Sheath enclosing the tendon as it crosses the sole.

plantar venous arch.d: Deep venous arch of the sole.

plantaris muscle.d: Muscle with a short belly and a very long thin tendon; its tendon is used as a graft, and it is absent in some people.

platysma.d: Thin flat muscle of facial expression under the skin of the front of the neck; supplied by the cervical branch of the facial nerve, it tenses the skin of the neck and pulls the corner of the mouth down.

pons.d: Bulging part of the brainstem between the midbrain and medulla, connected to the cerebellum; contains the nuclei of cranial nerves V–VIII.

popliteal artery.d: Continuation of the femoral artery beyond the adductor hiatus; the deepest structure of the popliteal fossa, it can be injured in knee dislocation.

popliteal fascia.d: Fascia roofing the fossa behind the knee; the small saphenous vein pierces it to pass deep.

popliteal surface of femur.d: Flat lower posterior surface of the femur; it forms the floor of the popliteal fossa and lies next to the popliteal artery.

popliteal vein.d: Runs superficial to the artery in the popliteal fossa.

popliteofibular ligament.d: Binds the popliteus tendon to the fibular head; an important stabiliser of the posterolateral corner.

popliteus muscle.d: Runs from the lateral condyle of the femur to the back of the tibia; it rotates the femur laterally to unlock the locked knee ('the key of the knee'). Tibial nerve.

postcentral gyrus.d: Gyrus behind the central sulcus (Brodmann 3, 1, 2); perceives touch, pain and position sense from the opposite side.

postcentral sulcus.d: Sulcus bounding the postcentral gyrus behind.

posterior antebrachial cutaneous nerve.d: Sensation from the skin of the back of the forearm.

posterior arch of atlas.d: Long posterior arch of the atlas; it carries a posterior tubercle instead of a spinous process.

posterior articular facet of dens axis.d: Back of the dens; articulates with the transverse ligament of the atlas.

posterior auricular vein.d: Drains the area behind the ear.

posterior basal segment of left lung (sx.tr: Posterior basal segment of left lung (sx)

posterior basal segment of right lung (s.tr: Posterior basal segment of right lung (sx)

posterior basal segmental artery of left.tr: Posterior basal segmental artery of left lung
posterior basal segmental artery of left.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis sinistri
posterior basal segmental artery of left.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

posterior basal segmental artery of righ.tr: Posterior basal segmental artery of right lung
posterior basal segmental artery of righ.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis dextri
posterior basal segmental artery of righ.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

posterior basal segmental bronchus of le.tr: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (bx)
posterior basal segmental bronchus of le.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis posterior (B X) sinister

posterior basal segmental bronchus of ri.tr: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (bx)
posterior basal segmental bronchus of ri.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis posterior (B X) dexter

posterior belly of digastric muscle.d: Runs from the mastoid notch to the intermediate tendon; supplied by the facial nerve, it pulls the hyoid upwards and backwards.

posterior border of ulna.d: Posterior border felt under the skin.

posterior branch of medial antebrachial.tr: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
posterior branch of medial antebrachial.la: Ramus posterior nervi cutanei antebrachii medialis
posterior branch of medial antebrachial.d: Supplies the skin of the posteromedial forearm.

posterior branch of obturator nerve.d: Supplies obturator externus and adductor magnus.

posterior branch of renal artery.d: Branch supplying the posterior segment; Brödel's line marks the avascular plane.

posterior calcaneal articular facet.d: Large posterior surface forming the subtalar joint with the calcaneus.

posterior cells of ethmoid bone.d: Posterior air cells of the ethmoidal labyrinth; they open into the superior meatus and lie next to the optic nerve.

posterior cerebral artery.d: Supplies the occipital lobe and the inferior surface of the temporal lobe; its occlusion causes homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.

posterior circumflex humeral artery.d: Passes through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve and winds round the back of the surgical neck.

posterior circumflex humeral vein.d: Accompanies the artery of the same name.

posterior clinoid process.d: Upper corners of the dorsum sellae; the tentorium attaches to them.

posterior cochlear nucleus.d: One of the first brainstem relay nuclei of the auditory fibres.

posterior commissure.d: Crossing fibres below the pineal gland; they make the pupillary light reflex bilateral.

posterior communicating artery.d: Links the internal carotid to the posterior cerebral artery; an aneurysm here presses on the oculomotor nerve and causes a third nerve palsy with a dilated pupil.

posterior cord of brachial plexus.d: Formed by the posterior divisions of the three trunks; gives the nerves supplying the extensors, mainly the axillary and radial nerves.

posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.d: The only muscle that opens the vocal folds (abduction); supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve. With bilateral paralysis the glottis closes and respiratory failure develops.

posterior cruciate ligament.d: Runs from the posterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the medial condyle of the femur; prevents backward sliding of the tibia. It is stronger than the ACL (posterior drawer test).

posterior division of inferior trunk of.d: Division that joins the posterior cord.

posterior division of internal iliac art.tr: Posterior division of internal iliac artery
posterior division of internal iliac art.d: Gives the iliolumbar, lateral sacral and superior gluteal arteries.

posterior division of mandibular nerve.d: Mostly sensory division; gives the auriculotemporal, lingual and inferior alveolar nerves.

posterior division of middle trunk of br.d: Division that joins the posterior cord.

posterior division of retromandibular ve.d: Helps to form the external jugular vein.

posterior division of superior trunk of.d: Division that joins the posterior cord.

posterior femoral cutaneous nerve.d: Sensation from the skin of the back of the thigh and the gluteal fold.

posterior gluteal line.d: Posterior line on the outer surface of the ilium; bounds the origin of gluteus maximus.

posterior horn of spinal cord.d: Grey matter where sensory fibres synapse; the substantia gelatinosa takes part in pain modulation.

posterior inferior cerebellar artery.d: The largest branch of the vertebral artery; its occlusion causes the lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome.

posterior inferior iliac spine.d: Projection at the posteroinferior end of the auricular surface.

posterior intercavernous sinus.d: Joins the two cavernous sinuses behind the pituitary.

posterior intercondylar area.d: Posterior area between the condyles; the posterior cruciate ligament attaches here.

posterior intercostal arteries.d: Branches of the thoracic aorta to the 3rd–11th spaces; run in the groove on the lower border of the rib and, enlarged in coarctation of the aorta, cause rib notching.

posterior intermuscular septum of leg.d: Fascial wall separating the lateral and posterior compartments.

posterior interosseous artery.d: Supplies the posterior compartment of the forearm.

posterior interosseous nerve of forearm.d: Continuation of the deep branch; supplies the forearm extensors. Compression at the arcade of Frohse causes finger drop without sensory loss.

posterior lateral nasal branches of sphe.tr: Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
posterior lateral nasal branches of sphe.d: Supply the lateral wall of the nose; the source of posterior nosebleeds.

posterior layer of thoracolumbar fascia.d: Strong layer covering erector spinae from behind; latissimus dorsi arises from it.

posterior leaflet of left atrioventricul.d: The posterior cusp of the mitral valve; prolapse is most common in this cusp.

posterior ligament of fibular head.d: Ligament reinforcing the superior tibiofibular joint behind.

posterior longitudinal ligament.d: Ligament on the back of the vertebral bodies, in the anterior wall of the spinal canal; because it is thick in the midline, disc herniations are mostly posterolateral. It limits flexion.

posterior malleolus.d: Posterior margin of the lower end of the tibia; it breaks in trimalleolar fractures.

posterior median sulcus of medulla oblon.tr: Posterior median sulcus of medulla oblongata

posterior meniscotibial ligament (latera.d: Ligament attaching the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus to the tibia.

posterior meniscotibial ligament (medial.d: Ligament attaching the posterior horn of the medial meniscus to the tibia; it lies next to the part of the meniscus that tears most often.

posterior nucleus of vagus nerve.d: Nucleus of the parasympathetic preganglionic fibres to the heart, lungs and digestive tract.

posterior obturator tubercle.d: Small prominence on the posterior margin of the obturator foramen; the obturator membrane attaches to it.

posterior parietal artery.d: Supplies the posterior part of the parietal lobe.

posterior process of talus.d: Posterior process; the FHL tendon passes in the groove between its two tubercles.

posterior quadrangular lobule.d: Uppermost hemispheric lobule of the posterior lobe.

posterior root of posterior femoral cuta.tr: Posterior root of posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
posterior root of posterior femoral cuta.la: Radix posterior nervi cutanei femoris posterioris
posterior root of posterior femoral cuta.d: Root of the nerve coming from the posterior divisions.

posterior sacral foramina.d: Posterior sacral foramina; the posterior rami of the sacral nerves emerge through them.

posterior sacro-iliac ligament.d: Strong ligament of short and long fibres behind the sacroiliac joint.

posterior segment of eyeball.d: Structures behind the lens (vitreous, retina, choroid).

posterior segmental artery of left lung.tr: Posterior segmental artery of left lung
posterior segmental artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

posterior segmental artery of right lung.tr: Posterior segmental artery of right lung
posterior segmental artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

posterior segmental bronchus of right lu.tr: Posterior segmental bronchus of right lung (bii)

posterior septal branches of sphenopalat.tr: Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
posterior septal branches of sphenopalat.d: Supply the nasal septum; contribute to Kiesselbach's area.

posterior spinocerebellar tract.d: Starts in Clarke's nucleus and reaches the cerebellum of the same side through the inferior cerebellar peduncle.

posterior sternoclavicular ligament.d: Posterior capsular thickening of the joint; in posterior dislocation the great vessels behind it are at risk.

posterior superior alveolar artery.d: Supplies the upper molars and the maxillary sinus.

posterior superior iliac spine.d: Posterior end of the iliac crest; the dimple in the skin over it (dimple of Venus) marks the S2 level.

posterior surface of arytenoid cartilage.d: Posterior surface; covered by the transverse and oblique arytenoid muscles.

posterior surface of fibula.d: Posterior surface of the fibula; soleus and FHL arise from it.

posterior surface of humerus.d: Posterior surface of the humerus; it carries the triceps heads and the radial groove.

posterior surface of petrous part.d: Surface facing the posterior cranial fossa; the internal acoustic meatus opens on it.

posterior surface of radius.d: Posterior surface of the radius; APL and EPB arise from it.

posterior surface of scapula.d: Posterior surface divided in two by the spine of the scapula.

posterior surface of tibia.d: Posterior surface of the tibia; it carries the soleal line.

posterior surface of ulna.d: Posterior surface of the ulna; the deep extensors arise from it.

posterior talocalcaneal ligament.d: Short ligament closing the subtalar joint behind.

posterior talofibular ligament.d: Strong ligament from the lateral malleolus to the posterior process of the talus; rarely torn.

posterior temporal branch.d: Supplies the back of the temporal lobe.

posterior tibial artery.d: Descends deep in the calf; its pulse is felt behind the medial malleolus and it passes through the tarsal tunnel to the sole.

posterior tibial veins.d: Accompany the posterior tibial artery; often involved in calf DVT.

posterior tibiofibular ligament.d: Strong ligament holding the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis from behind.

posterior tibiotalar ligament.d: The strongest, deep part of the deltoid ligament.

posterior tubercle of atlas.d: Prominence in the middle of the posterior arch; rectus capitis posterior minor and the nuchal ligament attach to it.

posterior tubercle of transverse process.d: Posterior prominence of a cervical transverse process; the scalene muscles attach to it.

posterior vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

posterolateral tract.d: Pathway in which pain and temperature fibres run up or down one or two segments before entering the dorsal horn.

posteromedial surface of fibula.d: Posteromedial surface of the fibula; tibialis posterior arises from it.

precentral gyrus.d: Gyrus in front of the central sulcus (Brodmann 4); initiates voluntary movements of the opposite half of the body; the motor homunculus lies here.

precentral sulcus (inferior part)*.d: Lower part of the sulcus in front of the precentral gyrus.

precentral sulcus (superior part)*.d: Upper part of the sulcus in front of the precentral gyrus.

precuneus.d: Part of the parietal lobe on the medial surface in front of the cuneus; linked to visuospatial imagery and self-awareness.

prefrontal artery.d: Supplies the lateral surface of the frontal lobe.

procerus muscle.d: At the root of the nose it pulls down the medial ends of the eyebrows, making horizontal wrinkles at the bridge of the nose.

promontory.d: Anterosuperior edge of the sacrum; the posterior boundary of the pelvic inlet and a reference point in obstetric measurement.

pronator quadratus.d: Deep muscle joining the radius and ulna in the distal quarter of the forearm; the main muscle of pronation. Anterior interosseous nerve.

pronator teres.d: Two-headed forearm muscle; it inserts into the middle of the radial shaft and pronates. Median nerve.

pronator tuberosity.d: Rough area on the lateral surface of the radius; pronator teres inserts here.

proper hepatic artery.d: Rises in the hepatoduodenal ligament to the left of the bile duct and in front of the portal vein; supplies the liver and, through its right branch, the gallbladder (cystic artery).

proper palmar digital arteries.d: End arteries running along both sides of the fingers; this is why adrenaline in digital blocks is debated.

proper palmar digital branches of median.tr: Proper palmar digital nerves of median nerve
proper palmar digital branches of median.la: Nervi digitales palmares proprii nervi mediani
proper palmar digital branches of median.d: Sensory branches running along the sides of the fingers from the thumb to half of the ring finger.

proper palmar digital branches of ulnar.tr: Proper palmar digital nerves of ulnar nerve
proper palmar digital branches of ulnar.la: Nervi digitales palmares proprii nervi ulnaris
proper palmar digital branches of ulnar.d: Sensory branches to the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger.

proper plantar digital arteries.d: Terminal branches running along the sides of the toes.

proper plantar digital branches of later.tr: Proper plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve
proper plantar digital branches of later.la: Nervi digitales plantares proprii nervi plantaris lateralis
proper plantar digital branches of later.d: Sensation from the plantar surface of the lateral toes.

proper plantar digital branches of media.tr: Proper plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve
proper plantar digital branches of media.la: Nervi digitales plantares proprii nervi plantaris medialis
proper plantar digital branches of media.d: Sensation from the plantar surface of the medial toes.

proximal lateral striate branches.d: Thin perforating branches supplying the basal ganglia and internal capsule; the source of hypertensive haemorrhages.

proximal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.d: Proximal bone of the little toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

proximal phalanx of fifth finger of hand.d: Proximal bone of the little finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.

proximal phalanx of first finger of foot.d: Proximal bone of the big toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

proximal phalanx of first finger of hand.d: Proximal bone of the thumb; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.

proximal phalanx of fourth finger of foo.d: Proximal bone of the 4th toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

proximal phalanx of fourth finger of han.d: Proximal bone of the ring finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.

proximal phalanx of second finger of foo.d: Proximal bone of the 2nd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

proximal phalanx of second finger of han.d: Proximal bone of the index finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.

proximal phalanx of third finger of foot.d: Proximal bone of the 3rd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.

proximal phalanx of third finger of hand.d: Proximal bone of the middle finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.

psoas major.d: Long muscle from the T12–L5 vertebrae to the lesser trochanter; the most powerful flexor of the thigh. The lumbar plexus forms within the muscle. Branches of the lumbar plexus.

pterygoid canal.d: Canal at the root of the pterygoid process; the nerve of the pterygoid canal (Vidian nerve) passes through it.

pterygoid fossa.d: Fossa between the two pterygoid plates; medial pterygoid arises here.

pterygoid hamulus.d: Hook at the tip of the medial plate; the tensor veli palatini tendon turns around it.

pterygoid notch.d: Notch at the lower end of the two plates; a process of the palatine bone fits into it.

pterygoid process.d: Process extending downwards from the sphenoid; it consists of two plates.

pterygospinous ligament.d: Ligament between the lateral pterygoid plate and the spine of the sphenoid; if it ossifies it can compress branches of the mandibular nerve.

pterygospinous process.d: Process on the posterior border of the lateral plate; a ligament joins it to the spine of the sphenoid.

pubic crest.d: Upper border of the body of the pubis; rectus abdominis and pyramidalis attach to it.

pubic symphysis.d: Fibrocartilaginous joint uniting the two pubic bones in front; it loosens in pregnancy under the influence of relaxin.

pubic tubercle.d: Prominence at the lateral end of the pubic crest; the inguinal ligament attaches to it, and it is a landmark in hernia examination.

pubis.d: Anteroinferior part of the hip bone.

pubo-analis muscle.d: Fibres of levator ani forming a U-shaped sling behind the rectum that creates the anorectal angle; essential for continence.

pubococcygeus muscle.d: Main part of levator ani, running from the pubis to the coccyx; it supports the pelvic organs and can be damaged in childbirth.

pubofemoral ligament.d: Ligament from the superior pubic ramus to the capsule; limits excessive abduction.

pudendal nerve.d: Arises from S2–S4, passes through the sciatic foramina into Alcock's canal; supplies the perineal muscles, external sphincters and skin of the external genitalia. It is blocked during childbirth.

pulmonary trunk.d: Trunk leaving the right ventricle that carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs; divides under the aortic arch into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

putamen.d: Outer part of the lentiform nucleus; with the caudate it forms the striatum and is the commonest site of hypertensive haemorrhage.

pyramid of medulla oblongata.d: Anterior swelling formed by the corticospinal fibres; about 85% of them cross at its lower end (pyramidal decussation).

pyramidalis muscle.d: Small triangular muscle at the very bottom of the rectus sheath, from the pubis to the linea alba; tenses the linea alba. Absent in some people.

pyramis of vermis.d: Pyramid-shaped lobule of the inferior vermis.

quadrangular membrane.d: Fibroelastic membrane between the epiglottis and the arytenoid cartilage; its free lower edge forms the false vocal fold (vestibular ligament).

quadrate ligament.d: Binds the neck of the radius to the lower border of the radial notch of the ulna; limits supination.

quadrate tubercle.d: Prominence on the intertrochanteric crest; quadratus femoris inserts here.

quadratus femoris muscle.d: Powerful lateral rotator running from the ischial tuberosity to the intertrochanteric crest.

quadratus lumborum muscle.d: Posterior abdominal wall muscle between the iliac crest, the 12th rib and the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae. Nerves: T12–L4. It bends the trunk sideways and fixes the 12th rib during inspiration.

quadratus plantae muscle.d: Attaches from the calcaneus to the flexor digitorum longus tendon and corrects its line of pull.

quadriceps femoris muscle.d: Powerful knee extensor made up of rectus femoris and the three vasti; inserts into the patella and, through the patellar ligament, into the tibia. Femoral nerve (L2–L4).

radial artery.d: The artery used for the pulse at the wrist; passes through the snuffbox to form the deep palmar arch. Used for arterial blood gases and coronary angiography (Allen test).

radial collateral artery.d: Joins the anastomosis around the elbow.

radial collateral ligament.d: Fan-shaped ligament from the lateral epicondyle to the annular ligament; resists varus stress.

radial collateral ligament of wrist join.d: Ligament from the radial styloid process to the scaphoid.

radial fossa.d: Small anterior fossa above the capitulum; the radial head enters it when the elbow is flexed.

radial groove.d: Spiral groove on the back of the humeral shaft; the radial nerve and profunda brachii artery run in it.

radial head of flexor digitorum superfic.tr: Radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis
radial head of flexor digitorum superfic.la: Caput radiale musculi flexoris digitorum superficialis
radial head of flexor digitorum superfic.d: Arises from the front of the radius; the muscle's tendons insert into the middle phalanges and flex the PIP joints. Median nerve.

radial nerve.d: Continuation of the posterior cord; runs in the spiral groove of the humerus and supplies all the extensors. A humeral shaft fracture or 'Saturday night palsy' causes wrist drop.

radial notch.d: Notch on the lateral side of the coronoid process; forms the proximal radio-ulnar joint with the radial head.

radial styloid process.d: Process at the lower lateral end of the radius; brachioradialis inserts into it, and it lies lower than the ulnar styloid.

radial tuberosity.d: Prominence below the neck; the biceps brachii tendon inserts here.

radiate carpal ligament.d: Palmar ligament radiating like a star from the head of the capitate to the surrounding carpal bones.

radiate ligament of head of rib.tr: Radiate ligament of head of rib
radiate ligament of head of rib.d: Ligament fanning out from the rib head to two vertebral bodies and the disc.

radiocapitate ligament.d: Part of the palmar radiocarpal ligaments running from the radius to the capitate.

radioscaphocapitate ligament.d: Ligament passing across the waist of the scaphoid to the capitate; it provides the axis of rotation of the scaphoid.

radius.d: Forearm bone on the thumb (lateral) side; by rotating around the ulna it produces pronation and supination. A fracture of its distal end (Colles') is the commonest wrist fracture.

rectus abdominis muscle.d: Muscle running from the pubis to the 5th–7th costal cartilages and the xiphoid, divided by 3–4 tendinous intersections (the 'six-pack'). It lies within the rectus sheath. Nerves: T7–T12. It flexes the trunk.

rectus anterior capitis muscle.d: Short prevertebral muscle from the atlas to the occipital bone; flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

rectus femoris muscle.d: The only head of quadriceps that also crosses the hip; arises from the AIIS, flexes the hip and extends the knee. Femoral nerve.

rectus lateralis capitis muscle.d: Runs from the transverse process of the atlas to the jugular process of the occipital bone; tilts the head sideways.

rectus posterior major capitis muscle.d: Suboccipital muscle from the spine of the axis to the occipital bone; extends and rotates the head. Suboccipital nerve (C1).

rectus posterior minor capitis muscle.d: Runs from the posterior tubercle of the atlas to the occiput; its connection to the dura has been linked to tension-type headache.

recurrent interosseous artery.d: Branch that runs back to the back of the elbow.

red nucleus.d: Iron-containing nucleus in the midbrain tegmentum; the origin of the rubrospinal tract, it receives cerebellar output.

retina.d: Inner layer containing the visual cells; the fovea at the centre of the macula is the site of sharpest vision.

retromandibular vein.d: Runs within the parotid, deep to the facial nerve.

rhomboid major muscle.d: Runs from the T2–T5 spines to the medial border of the scapula; retracts the scapula. Nerve: dorsal scapular nerve.

rhomboid minor muscle.d: Small muscle from the C7–T1 spines to the level of the root of the spine of the scapula.

rib.d: Curved bone of the thoracic cage; it continues in front as the costal cartilage.

right ascending lumbar vein.d: Joins the lumbar veins and continues as the azygos vein.

right atrium.d: Chamber receiving blood from the superior and inferior venae cavae and the coronary sinus; the sinoatrial node lies at the entry of the superior vena cava and the fossa ovalis in the interatrial septum.

right brachiocephalic vein.d: Short vertical vein formed by the right internal jugular and subclavian veins.

right common carotid artery.d: Arises from the brachiocephalic trunk; divides at the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C4) into the internal and external carotids.

right coronary artery.d: Arises from the right aortic sinus and runs in the right AV groove; in most people it supplies the SA and AV nodes and the posterior interventricular artery (right dominance). Its occlusion causes inferior MI and bradycardia.

right coronary leaflet.d: The right coronary artery arises from the sinus behind it.

right gastro-omental vein.d: Drains the right part of the greater curvature of the stomach.

right inferior pulmonary vein.d: Carries blood from the right lower lobe to the left atrium.

right inferolateral branch of right coro.tr: Right posterolateral branch of right coronary artery
right inferolateral branch of right coro.d: Branch of the right coronary artery to the posterolateral wall of the left ventricle.

right pulmonary artery.d: Branch passing behind the aorta and superior vena cava to the right lung.

right renal artery.d: Arises at L1–L2 and passes behind the inferior vena cava; longer than the left renal artery.

right renal vein.d: Short vein opening directly into the inferior vena cava.

right semilunar leaflet of pulmonary val.tr: Right semilunar cusp of pulmonary valve
right semilunar leaflet of pulmonary val.la: Valvula semilunaris dextra valvae trunci pulmonalis
right semilunar leaflet of pulmonary val.d: The right semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve.

right subclavian artery.d: Arises from the brachiocephalic trunk; passes behind scalenus anterior and becomes the axillary artery at the outer border of the 1st rib.

right subclavian vein.d: Continuation of the axillary vein; passes in front of scalenus anterior and is used for central catheters.

right subcostal vein.d: Helps to form the azygos vein.

right superior intercostal vein.d: Carries the right 2nd–4th intercostal veins to the azygos vein.

right superior phrenic vein.d: Drains the upper surface of the diaphragm.

right superior pulmonary vein.d: Carries oxygenated blood from the right upper and middle lobes to the left atrium.

right testicular artery.d: Arises from the aorta at L2 and descends in the spermatic cord to the testis.

right ventricle.d: Chamber forming most of the front of the heart; it has a trabeculated inner surface and a moderator band and pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk.

risorius muscle.d: Pulls the corner of the mouth sideways; contributes to dimples.

root apex.d: Tip of the root; nerves and vessels enter the tooth through the apical foramen.

root of tooth.d: Part of the tooth embedded in the alveolus; covered with cementum.

roots of brachial plexus.d: Anterior rami of C5–T1; they emerge between the scalene muscles.

rotatores.d: The deepest small muscles, running from a transverse process to the base of the lamina one or two levels above; they contribute to proprioception during spinal movement.

rubrospinal tract.d: Descending pathway from the red nucleus that increases flexor muscle tone.

sacral canal.d: Continuation of the vertebral canal in the sacrum; it contains the lower roots of the cauda equina and the filum terminale.

sacral hiatus.d: Opening at the lower posterior end of the sacrum; caudal epidural anaesthesia is given here.

sacral horn.d: Horns on each side of the hiatus; they guide caudal block.

sacral tuberosity.d: Rough area behind the auricular surface; the interosseous sacroiliac ligaments attach to it.

sacrococcygeal symphysis.d: Fibrocartilaginous joint between the tip of the sacrum and the coccyx; it lets the coccyx bend backwards during childbirth.

sacropelvic surface of ilium.d: Inner posterior surface of the ilium facing the sacrum and pelvis.

sacrospinous ligament.d: Triangular ligament from the edge of the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine; it separates the greater and lesser sciatic foramina.

sacrotuberous ligament.d: Strong ligament from the sacrum to the ischial tuberosity; prevents the sacrum tipping forwards and bounds the lesser sciatic foramen.

sacrum.d: Triangular bone formed by the fusion of five sacral vertebrae; it forms the back wall of the pelvis between the two hip bones. Branches of the sacral nerves emerge through the anterior and posterior sacral foramina.

sagittal border of parietal bone.d: Border forming the sagittal suture with the opposite parietal.

saphenous nerve.d: Longest sensory branch of the femoral nerve; passes through the adductor canal and supplies the inner side of the leg and foot. It can be injured when the saphenous vein is harvested.

sartorius muscle.d: The longest muscle in the body; runs from the ASIS to the medial surface of the tibia (pes anserinus). It flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip and flexes the knee. Femoral nerve.

scalenus anterior muscle.d: Runs from the C3–C6 transverse processes to the 1st rib; the phrenic nerve and subclavian vein pass in front of it, the subclavian artery and brachial plexus behind (scalene gap). It raises the 1st rib.

scalenus medius muscle.d: The largest scalene; runs from the cervical vertebrae to the 1st rib, and the roots of the long thoracic nerve pass through it.

scalenus posterior muscle.d: The smallest scalene, from the lower cervical vertebrae to the 2nd rib; raises the rib in deep inspiration.

scaphoid bone.d: The most lateral and largest bone of the proximal carpal row; it is felt in the anatomical snuffbox. Because its blood supply comes from distally, avascular necrosis of the proximal fragment can follow waist fractures.

scaphoid fossa.d: Fossa above the medial plate; tensor veli palatini arises here.

scapholunate interosseous ligament.d: The most important carpal ligament, joining the scaphoid and lunate; when it tears a gap opens (Terry-Thomas sign) and a DISI deformity develops.

scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal ligament.d: Binds the distal end of the scaphoid to the trapezium and trapezoid.

scapula.d: Triangular flat bone on the upper back of the thoracic cage; it carries the spine, acromion, coracoid process and glenoid cavity, and gives attachment to 17 muscles.

scapular notch.d: Notch on the upper border; the suprascapular nerve passes beneath it and the suprascapular artery above.

scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle.d: Posterior fibres; move the arm backwards and rotate it laterally.

sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus muscle.d: Over the ischial tuberosity; it becomes inflamed in people who sit for long periods.

sciatic bursa of obturator internus.d: Bursa beneath the tendon as it turns over the lesser sciatic notch.

sciatic nerve.d: Thickest nerve in the body, formed from L4–S3; emerges below piriformis into the gluteal region and divides in the back of the thigh into the tibial and common fibular nerves.

sclera.d: White, tough outer layer of the eyeball; it gives attachment to the eye muscles.

second metacarpal bone.d: The 2nd of the five long bones of the metacarpus; its base articulates with the carpal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.

second metatarsal bone.d: The 2nd of the five long bones of the metatarsus; its base articulates with the tarsal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.

second posterior intercostal artery.d: Arises from the supreme intercostal artery.

second rib.d: 2nd rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly. Serratus anterior attaches to the tuberosity on its upper surface.

sella turcica.d: Saddle-shaped structure on the upper surface of the body; contains the hypophysial fossa.

semimembranosus bursa.d: Between the semimembranosus tendon and the tibia; the commonest source of a Baker's (popliteal) cyst.

semimembranosus muscle.d: Deep hamstring inserting into the back of the medial condyle of the tibia; its tendon forms the oblique popliteal ligament.

semispinalis colli muscle.d: Cervical part of the superficial layer of the transversospinal group.

semispinalis thoracis muscle.d: Thoracic part of the superficial layer of the transversospinal group.

semitendinosus muscle.d: Hamstring inserting into the pes anserinus by its long tendon; used as a graft in ACL reconstruction. Tibial nerve.

sensory root of trigeminal nerve.d: Large root running from the trigeminal ganglion to the pons.

septal branches of anterior interventric.d: Branches supplying the anterior 2/3 of the septum and the bundle of His.

septal branches of posterior ethmoidal a.tr: Septal branches of posterior ethmoidal artery
septal branches of posterior ethmoidal a.d: Supply the upper part of the nasal septum.

septal leaflet of right atrioventricular.d: The cusp of the tricuspid valve facing the septum.

septal nuclei.d: Limbic nuclei below the septum pellucidum; they take part in the reward and pleasure circuit.

septal papillary muscle of right ventric.tr: Septal papillary muscle of right ventricle
septal papillary muscle of right ventric.d: Small papillary muscle arising from the septum.

septum of frontal sinuses.d: Thin bony septum separating the two frontal sinuses; it usually deviates from the midline.

septum of sphenoidal sinuses.d: Septum separating the two sphenoidal sinuses; a guide in transsphenoidal surgery.

septum pellucidum.d: Thin membrane separating the anterior horns of the two lateral ventricles.

serratus anterior muscle.d: Runs from the upper 8–9 ribs to the medial border of the scapula; protracts the scapula, holds it against the chest wall and allows the arm to rise above 90°. Long thoracic nerve damage causes a 'winged scapula'.

serratus posterior inferior muscle.d: Thin muscle from the T11–L2 spines to the lower four ribs.

serratus posterior superior muscle.d: Thin muscle from the upper thoracic spines to the 2nd–5th ribs; an accessory muscle of inspiration.

sesamoid bones of foot.d: Two small bones within the flexor hallucis brevis tendons beneath the 1st metatarsal head; they share in load transfer and can suffer sesamoiditis and fractures.

seventh rib.d: 7th rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.

short head of biceps brachii.d: Head arising from the coracoid process; both heads insert into the radial tuberosity, flexing and supinating the forearm. Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6).

short head of biceps femoris.d: Head arising from the linea aspera that flexes only the knee; supplied by the common fibular nerve. Both heads insert into the fibular head.

short posterior ciliary arteries.d: Supply the choroid and the optic nerve head.

sigmoid arteries.d: Two to four branches supplying the sigmoid colon.

sigmoid sinus.d: Curves in an S behind the mastoid and opens at the jugular foramen into the internal jugular vein; mastoiditis can cause its thrombosis.

sinus of frontal bone.d: Paired air space within the frontal bone; it opens into the middle meatus through the frontonasal duct.

sinus of sphenoid bone.d: Air space in the body of the sphenoid; it opens into the sphenoethmoidal recess and is used as the transsphenoidal route in pituitary surgery.

sixth rib.d: 6th rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.

small saphenous vein.d: Begins behind the lateral malleolus and opens into the popliteal vein; runs with the sural nerve.

soleal line.d: Oblique line on the posterior surface; soleus arises from it.

soleus muscle.d: Flat muscle beneath gastrocnemius; it maintains posture when standing and, as a 'peripheral heart', aids venous return. Tibial nerve.

sphenoid bone.d: Butterfly-shaped bone in the middle of the skull base; the pituitary lies in its sella turcica. Nerves and vessels pass through the openings in its greater and lesser wings (optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum).

sphenoidal angle of parietal bone.d: Anteroinferior angle contributing to the pterion; the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery runs on its inner surface.

sphenoidal crest.d: Midline ridge on the front of the body; it contributes to the nasal septum.

sphenoidal lingula.d: Tongue-shaped projection on the lateral edge of the carotid sulcus.

sphenoidal margin of frontal bone.d: Margin that articulates with the sphenoid.

sphenoidal yoke.d: Flat bony area joining the two lesser wings (jugum).

sphenomandibular ligament.d: Ligament from the spine of the sphenoid to the lingula of the mandible; a remnant of Meckel's cartilage.

spinal dura.d: Tough membrane surrounding the spinal cord; it ends at S2 and is separated from the vertebral canal by the epidural space (epidural anaesthesia).

spinal ganglion.d: Ganglion on the dorsal root containing the cell bodies of sensory neurons; the herpes zoster virus lies latent here.

spinal reticular process.d: Network beside the dorsal horn where grey and white matter mix.

spinalis capitis muscle.d: Head part of the spinalis column, fused with semispinalis capitis.

spinalis colli muscle.d: Cervical part of the spinalis column; often poorly developed.

spinalis thoracis muscle.d: The most medial column of erector spinae; runs between the spinous processes.

spine of scapula.d: Bony ridge dividing the posterior surface in two; trapezius and deltoid attach to it.

spine of sphenoid bone.d: Spine at the posterior end of the greater wing; the sphenomandibular ligament attaches to it.

spinoglenoid notch.d: Notch between the spine and the glenoid; the suprascapular nerve passes through it to the infraspinous fossa.

spinotectal tract.d: Carries sensory information to the superior colliculus, orienting the head and eyes.

spinous process.d: Backward-projecting process of the arch; ligaments and back muscles attach to it.

splenic artery.d: The largest coeliac branch, running a tortuous course along the upper border of the pancreas; gives the short gastric and left gastro-omental branches. A posterior gastric ulcer can erode it.

splenic vein.d: Runs behind the pancreas; can thrombose in pancreatitis.

splenius capitis muscle.d: Bandage-like muscle from the nuchal ligament and upper thoracic spines to the mastoid; extends the head and turns it to the same side.

splenius colli muscle.d: Part of splenius extending to the transverse processes of the upper cervical vertebrae.

squamosal border of parietal bone.d: Border that articulates with the squamous part of the temporal bone.

squamosal margin of greater wing.d: Margin that articulates with the squamous part of the temporal bone.

squamous part of frontal bone.d: Broad squamous part forming the forehead.

squamous part of occipital bone.d: Broad posterior squamous part of the occipital bone.

squamous part of temporal bone.d: Thin squamous part forming the temple; a fracture here can cause an extradural haematoma.

stapes.d: The smallest bone in the body; its footplate closes the oval window and transmits vibration to the inner ear. Stapedius attaches to it; in otosclerosis the footplate becomes fixed.

sternal angle.d: Angle where the manubrium meets the body; at the level of the 2nd rib, it is used for counting ribs.

sternal articular surface.d: Articular surface at the medial end; forms the sternoclavicular joint with the sternum and the articular disc.

sternal end.d: Thick medial end of the clavicle; forms the only joint attaching the upper limb to the trunk.

sternocleidomastoid muscle.d: Muscle from the sternum and clavicle to the mastoid process, dividing the neck into anterior and posterior triangles. Nerves: accessory nerve (XI) and C2–C3. Acting alone it tilts the head to the same side and turns the face to the opposite side; it is shortened in torticollis.

sternocostal head of pectoralis major mu.d: Broad fibres arising from the sternum and costal cartilages; adduct and medially rotate the arm. Pectoral nerves.

sternohyoid muscle.d: Superficial infrahyoid muscle from the manubrium to the hyoid; supplied by the ansa cervicalis, it depresses the hyoid after swallowing.

sternothyroid muscle.d: Deep infrahyoid muscle from the manubrium to the thyroid cartilage; pulls the larynx down.

straight gyrus (gyrus rectus).d: Gyrus on the inferior surface of the frontal lobe at the midline, medial to the olfactory sulcus.

straight part of cricothyroid muscle.d: Vertical fibres of cricothyroid; they tilt the thyroid cartilage forwards and raise the pitch of the voice.

straight sinus.d: Formed by the union of the inferior sagittal sinus and the great cerebral vein (of Galen).

stria medullaris thalami.d: Fibre bundle running along the upper medial border of the thalamus to the habenula.

stria terminalis.d: Fibre pathway from the amygdala to the hypothalamus along the edge of the caudate nucleus.

stylohyoid ligament.d: Ligament from the styloid process to the lesser horn of the hyoid; its ossification causes Eagle syndrome.

stylohyoid muscle.d: Runs from the styloid process to the hyoid, embracing the digastric tendon; supplied by the facial nerve.

styloid process of temporal bone.d: Thin process projecting downwards below the ear; three 'stylo-' muscles and two ligaments attach to it.

styloid process of third metacarpal bone.d: Small process on the base of the 3rd metacarpal; the ECRB tendon attaches near it.

stylomandibular ligament.d: Ligament from the styloid process to the angle of the mandible; separates the parotid and submandibular glands.

stylopharyngeus muscle.d: The only muscle supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX); it raises the pharynx and larynx during swallowing.

subacromial bursa.d: Between the acromion and the supraspinatus tendon; it becomes inflamed in impingement syndrome and is used for injections.

subclavian nerve.d: Arises from the upper trunk and supplies subclavius.

subclavius muscle.d: Runs from the 1st rib to the lower surface of the clavicle; protects the neurovascular structures beneath in clavicle fractures. Nerve to subclavius.

subcostal artery.d: The last segmental branch, running below the 12th rib.

subcutaneous acromial bursa.d: Under the skin over the acromion.

subcutaneous bursa of lateral malleolus.d: Bursa under the skin over the lateral ankle prominence.

subcutaneous bursa of medial malleolus.d: Bursa under the skin over the medial ankle prominence.

subcutaneous bursa of tuberosity of tibi.d: Subcutaneous bursa in front of the tibial tuberosity.

subcutaneous calcaneal bursa.d: Between the Achilles tendon and the skin; it becomes inflamed from shoe friction.

subcutaneous infrapatellar bursa.d: Under the skin in front of the patellar ligament; it becomes inflamed in people who work kneeling.

subcutaneous prepatellar bursa.d: Subcutaneous bursa in front of the patella; its inflammation is known as 'housemaid's knee'.

subcutaneous trochanteric bursa.d: Under the skin over the greater trochanter.

subdeltoid bursa.d: Between deltoid and the humeral head; usually continuous with the subacromial bursa.

subfacial prepatellar bursa.d: Bursa in front of the patella beneath the fascia.

sublime tubercle.d: Prominence on the medial side of the coronoid process; the anterior band of the ulnar collateral ligament attaches to it.

sublingual fossa.d: Fossa on the inner surface above the mylohyoid line; the sublingual gland lies in it.

submental artery.d: Supplies the floor of the mouth and the area under the chin.

submental vein.d: Drains the area under the chin.

subparietal sulcus.d: Sulcus on the medial surface separating the precuneus from the cingulate gyrus.

subscapular artery.d: The largest branch of the axillary artery; gives the thoracodorsal and circumflex scapular branches.

subscapular fossa.d: Anterior surface facing the chest wall; subscapularis arises here.

subscapularis muscle.d: Rotator cuff muscle filling the front of the scapula; inserts into the lesser tubercle and rotates the arm medially. Subscapular nerves.

subtendinous bursa of iliacus muscle.d: Between the iliopsoas tendon and the lesser trochanter.

subtendinous bursa of infraspinatus musc.d: Between the infraspinatus tendon and the capsule.

subtendinous bursa of obturator internus.d: Between the tendon and the hip capsule.

subtendinous bursa of sartorius muscle.d: Between the sartorius tendon and the other pes anserinus tendons.

subtendinous bursa of teres major muscle.d: Between the teres major tendon and the humerus.

subtendinous bursa of tibialis anterior.d: Between the tibialis anterior tendon and the medial cuneiform.

subtendinous bursa of trapezius muscle.d: Between the ascending part of trapezius and the spine of the scapula.

subtendinous bursa of triceps brachii mu.d: Between the triceps tendon and the olecranon.

subtendinous calcaneal bursa.d: Between the Achilles tendon and the back of the calcaneus (retrocalcaneal bursa); it becomes inflamed in Haglund's deformity.

subtendinous prepatellar bursa.d: Between the quadriceps tendon and the patella.

sulcus interm_prim-jensen.d: Small sulcus separating the supramarginal and angular gyri.

sulcus of auditory tube.d: Groove in which the cartilaginous part of the auditory (Eustachian) tube lies.

superficial branch of medial plantar art.tr: Superficial branch of medial plantar artery
superficial branch of medial plantar art.d: Superficial branch supplying the big-toe side.

superficial branch of radial nerve.d: Sensory branch to the lateral back of the hand; it can be compressed by a tight watch strap (Wartenberg).

superficial branch of ulnar nerve.d: Carries palmar sensation from the medial one and a half fingers and supplies palmaris brevis.

superficial dorsal veins of penis.d: Open into the external pudendal veins.

superficial epigastric artery.d: Superficial branch supplying the skin of the lower abdomen.

superficial epigastric vein.d: Can dilate in portal hypertension and contribute to 'caput medusae'.

superficial external pudendal artery.d: Superficial branch supplying the skin of the external genitalia.

superficial fibular nerve.d: Supplies the lateral compartment muscles and most of the skin of the dorsum of the foot.

superficial head of flexor pollicis brev.tr: Superficial head of flexor pollicis brevis
superficial head of flexor pollicis brev.la: Caput superficiale musculi flexoris pollicis brevis
superficial head of flexor pollicis brev.d: Arises from the flexor retinaculum; supplied by the median nerve.

superficial head of pronator teres.d: Arises from the medial epicondyle; the median nerve passes between the two heads and can be compressed here (pronator syndrome).

superficial investing cervical fascia.tr: Investing layer of deep cervical fascia
superficial investing cervical fascia.d: Fascial layer surrounding the neck and enclosing sternocleidomastoid and trapezius like a sheath.

superficial layer of temporal fascia.d: Layer of the strong fascia covering temporalis that attaches to the outer lip of the zygomatic arch.

superficial palmar arch.d: Arch formed by the ulnar artery, lying distal to the deep arch (Kaplan's line); at risk in palm injuries.

superficial part of anterior compartment.tr: Superficial layer of anterior forearm compartment

superficial part of masseter.d: Powerful masticatory fibres from the zygomatic arch to the angle of the mandible; masseteric nerve (V3). It closes the jaw.

superficial part of posterior compartmen.tr: Superficial layer of posterior forearm compartment
Superficial layer of posterior leg compartment

superficial part of tibial collateral li.tr: Superficial part of medial collateral ligament
superficial part of tibial collateral li.d: Flat band from the medial epicondyle to the shaft of the tibia; resists valgus stress.

superficial temporal artery.d: Its pulse is felt in front of the ear; biopsied in giant cell arteritis.

superficial transverse metacarpal ligame.d: Transverse fibres at the bases of the fingers in the palm.

superficial transverse metatarsal ligame.d: Transverse fibres of the plantar aponeurosis at the bases of the toes.

superficial venous palmar arch.d: Accompanies the superficial palmar arterial arch.

superior angle of scapula.d: Superomedial angle of the scapula; levator scapulae attaches to it.

superior anorectal artery.d: Continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery; supplies the upper rectum.

superior articular facet of vertebra.d: Surface of the superior articular process that forms a facet joint.

superior articular process of sacrum.d: Process forming a facet joint with L5.

superior articular process of vertebra.d: Process that articulates with the vertebra above.

superior articular surface of atlas.d: Concavity on the upper surface of the lateral mass; with the occipital condyles it forms the joint for the 'yes' movement.

superior articular surface of lateral co.tr: Superior articular surface of lateral condyle
superior articular surface of lateral co.d: Surface of the lateral condyle that articulates with the femur.

superior articular surfaces of tibia.d: Surfaces of the tibial plateau that articulate with the femoral condyles.

superior basal vein of left lung.tr: Superior basal vein of left lung
superior basal vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

superior basal vein of right lung.tr: Superior basal vein of right lung
superior basal vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

superior border of scapula.d: Short upper border of the scapula; the inferior belly of omohyoid arises here.

superior bursa of biceps femoris muscle.d: At the origin of the long head of biceps femoris.

superior cerebellar artery.d: Branch of the basilar artery near its top; supplies the upper surface of the cerebellum and can cause neuralgia by touching the trigeminal nerve.

superior cerebellar peduncle.d: Main output pathway of the cerebellum; carries fibres from the dentate nucleus to the thalamus and red nucleus.

superior colliculus.d: Visual reflex centre; it turns the eyes and head towards visual stimuli.

superior costal facet.d: Half facet on the upper border of the body; articulates with the head of the rib of the same number.

superior deep lateral nodes.la: Nodi lymphoidei cervicales laterales profundi superiores

superior epigastric artery.d: Anastomoses in the rectus sheath with the inferior epigastric artery (a collateral path in coarctation of the aorta).

superior extensor retinaculum of ankle.d: Transverse band in front of the ankle holding the extensor tendons.

superior facet of talus.tr: Superior facet of trochlea of talus
superior facet of talus.d: Upper articular surface of the trochlea facing the tibia.

superior fibular retinaculum.d: Band holding the fibular tendons behind the lateral malleolus; when it tears the tendons dislocate.

superior frontal gyrus.d: Upper gyrus of the frontal lobe; its medial part contains the supplementary motor area.

superior frontal sulcus.d: Separates the superior and middle frontal gyri.

superior gemellus muscle.d: Runs from the ischial spine to join the obturator internus tendon; a lateral rotator.

superior glenohumeral ligament.d: Thin ligament on the inner surface of the capsule; limits inferior translation with the arm at the side.

superior gluteal artery.d: The largest branch of the internal iliac artery, emerging above piriformis; supplies gluteus medius and minimus.

superior gluteal nerve.d: Emerges above piriformis; supplies gluteus medius and minimus and TFL. Its injury causes a Trendelenburg gait.

superior head of lateral pterygoid muscl.d: Runs from the greater wing of the sphenoid to the articular disc and condyle; steadies the disc as the jaw closes.

superior horn of thyroid cartilage.d: Upward extension of the thyroid cartilage; joined to the hyoid by the lateral thyrohyoid ligament.

superior labial artery.d: Supplies the upper lip and the front of the nasal septum (contributes to Kiesselbach's area).

superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv.tr: Superior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm
superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv.d: Carries sensation from the skin over deltoid (the 'badge' area).

superior lateral genicular artery.d: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.

superior lingular artery of left lung.tr: Superior lingular segmental artery of left lung
superior lingular artery of left lung.la: Arteria segmentalis lingularis superior pulmonis sinistri
superior lingular artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

superior lingular artery of right lung.tr: Superior lingular artery of right lung
superior lingular artery of right lung.la: Arteria segmentalis lingularis superior pulmonis dextri

superior lingular segment of left lung (.tr: Superior lingular segment of left lung (siv)
