superior lingular segmental bronchus of.tr: Superior lingular segmental bronchus of left lung (biv)

superior lingular vein of left lung.tr: Superior lingular vein of left lung
superior lingular vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

superior lingular vein of right lung.tr: Superior lingular vein of right lung

superior lobar artery of left lung.tr: Superior lobar artery of left lung
superior lobar artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to the superior lobe of the left lung.

superior lobar artery of right lung.tr: Superior lobar artery of right lung
superior lobar artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to the superior lobe of the right lung.

superior medial genicular artery.d: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.

superior mental spine.d: Upper spine on the inner surface; genioglossus attaches to it.

superior mesenteric artery.d: Arises from the aorta at L1 and passes in front of the 3rd part of the duodenum to supply the midgut (small intestine, ascending colon and 2/3 of the transverse colon). Its acute occlusion causes mesenteric ischaemia.

superior mesenteric vein.d: Drains the small intestine and right colon.

superior nuchal line.d: Superior nuchal line; trapezius, SCM and splenius capitis attach to it.

superior oblique muscle.d: Its tendon passes through the trochlea to attach to the eye; it turns the eye down and out and rotates it inwards. Supplied by the trochlear nerve (IV); when paralysed, double vision appears when going down stairs.

superior occipital gyri.d: Upper gyrus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe.

superior ophthalmic vein.d: Drains the orbit and opens into the cavernous sinus.

superior parietal lobule.d: Lobule above the intraparietal sulcus; linked to body schema and spatial perception.

superior petrosal sinus.d: Connects the cavernous sinus with the transverse sinus.

superior pharyngeal constrictor.d: Constrictor in the wall of the nasopharynx and oropharynx; arises from the pterygomandibular raphe. Pharyngeal plexus (X).

superior phrenic arteries.d: Small branches from the thoracic aorta to the upper surface of the diaphragm.

superior pubic ligament.d: Ligament reinforcing the upper border of the symphysis, extending to the pubic tubercles.

superior pubic ramus.d: Upper ramus of the pubis; the femoral vessels pass in front of it into the thigh.

superior rectus muscle.d: Turns the eye up (elevation) and in, and rotates it inwards; supplied by the superior branch of the oculomotor nerve (III).

superior sagittal sinus.d: In the upper border of the falx cerebri; the arachnoid granulations empty CSF into it.

superior salivatory nucleus.d: Nucleus of the parasympathetic fibres (VII) to the lacrimal, submandibular and sublingual glands.

superior segmental artery of left lung.tr: Superior segmental artery of left lung
superior segmental artery of left lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

superior segmental artery of right lung.tr: Superior segmental artery of right lung
superior segmental artery of right lung.d: Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.

superior segmental bronchus of left lung.tr: Superior segmental bronchus of left lung (bvi)

superior segmental bronchus of right lun.tr: Superior segmental bronchus of right lung (bvi)

superior subscapular nerve.d: Supplies the upper part of subscapularis.

superior tarsus.d: Dense connective tissue plate forming the skeleton of the upper eyelid; it contains the meibomian glands.

superior temporal gyrus (lateral part).d: Its posterior part contains Wernicke's area (Brodmann 22); damage on the dominant side causes fluent (sensory) aphasia.

superior temporal line.d: Upper line to which the temporal fascia attaches.

superior temporal sulcus.d: Separates the superior and middle temporal gyri.

superior thyroid notch.d: V-shaped notch on the upper border of the thyroid cartilage; easily felt in the neck.

superior thyroid tubercle.d: Prominence at the upper end of the oblique line.

superior thyroid vein.d: Drains the upper pole of the thyroid.

superior transverse scapular ligament.d: Ligament converting the scapular notch into a foramen; the suprascapular nerve passes beneath it and the suprascapular artery above.

superior trunk of brachial plexus.d: Formed by the union of the C5–C6 roots; its stretching at birth causes Erb–Duchenne palsy ('waiter's tip').

superior ulnar collateral artery.d: Accompanies the ulnar nerve and joins the anastomosis around the elbow.

superior vein of left lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

superior vein of right lung.d: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.

superior vena cava.d: Formed by the two brachiocephalic veins and opens into the right atrium; compression by lung tumours causes superior vena cava syndrome.

supinator.d: Muscle wrapping the upper third of the radius; supinates the forearm. The posterior interosseous nerve can be compressed at the arcade of Frohse as it pierces this muscle.

supinator crest.d: Ridge below the radial notch; supinator arises from it.

supra-acetabular groove.d: Groove on the upper rim of the acetabulum; the reflected head of rectus femoris attaches to it.

supra-orbital artery.d: Supplies the forehead and the front of the scalp.

supra-orbital notch.d: Notch on the upper margin of the orbit; the supraorbital nerve and artery pass through it.

supraglenoid tubercle.d: Prominence above the glenoid; the long head of biceps arises here.

supramarginal gyrus.d: Gyrus capping the posterior end of the lateral fissure (Brodmann 40); on the dominant side it takes part in language processing.

suprapatellar bursa.d: Large bursa between the quadriceps tendon and the femur, continuous with the knee joint cavity; it swells in a knee effusion.

suprascapular artery.d: Passes above the superior transverse scapular ligament; joins the scapular anastomosis.

suprascapular nerve.d: Arises from the upper trunk, passes through the scapular notch and supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus.

supraspinatus muscle.d: Rotator cuff muscle from the supraspinous fossa to the greater tubercle; initiates the first 15° of abduction. Suprascapular nerve. Its tendon is the one most often torn and impinged.

supraspinous fossa.d: Fossa above the spine; supraspinatus arises here.

supraspinous ligament.d: Strong ligament joining the tips of the spinous processes; in the neck it continues as the nuchal ligament.

supratrochlear artery.d: Supplies the middle of the forehead; the pedicle of the forehead flap.

supreme intercostal artery.d: Supplies the first two intercostal spaces.

supreme nuchal line.d: Highest nuchal line; the galea aponeurotica attaches to it.

sural nerve.d: Carries sensation from the posterolateral leg and the lateral border of the foot; used for nerve biopsy and grafts.

surgical neck of humerus.d: Constriction below the tubercles; it fractures often and the axillary nerve can be injured.

suspensory ligament of eyeball.d: Hammock-like thickening of fascia supporting the eyeball from below.

sustentaculum tali.d: Shelf projecting from the medial surface of the calcaneus; supports the head of the talus, with the FHL tendon passing beneath it.

sympathetic nerves.d: Branches from the sympathetic trunk to the organs and vessels; they include the splanchnic nerves.

sympathetic trunk.d: Chain of ganglia on either side of the vertebral column from the skull base to the coccyx; damage to the cervical ganglia causes Horner syndrome.

symphysial surface of pubis.d: Midline articular surface of the pubis; forms the pubic symphysis with the opposite side.

synovial joints of free lower limb.tr: Synovial joints of free lower limb

synovial joints of free upper limb.tr: Synovial joints of free upper limb

synovial sheaths of digits of hand.d: Synovial sheaths enclosing the flexor tendons in the fingers; infection (tenosynovitis) requires urgent surgery.

talar sulcus.d: Groove on the lower surface of the talus; with the calcaneal sulcus it forms the sinus tarsi.

talocalcaneal interosseous ligament.d: Strong ligament binding the talus and calcaneus within the sinus tarsi; the main stabiliser of the subtalar joint.

talonavicular ligament.d: Binds the neck of the talus to the upper surface of the navicular.

talus.d: Tarsal bone transferring weight between leg and foot, with no muscles attached; its trochlea forms the ankle joint. Neck fractures carry a risk of avascular necrosis.

tarsal sinus.d: Laterally open canal between the talus and calcaneus; contains the interosseous talocalcaneal ligament.

tectospinal tract.d: From the superior colliculus to the neck muscles; a reflex pathway turning the head towards visual stimuli.

tegmen tympani.d: Thin bone forming the roof of the middle ear; middle ear infections can spread through it into the skull.

tegmentum of pons.d: Dorsal part of the pons containing cranial nerve nuclei, sensory pathways and the reticular formation.

temporal bone.d: Complex bone housing the middle and inner ear, made up of the petrous, squamous and tympanic parts and the mastoid process; it forms the temporomandibular joint with the mandible.

temporal branches of middle cerebral art.tr: Temporal branches of middle cerebral artery
temporal branches of middle cerebral art.d: Supply the lateral surface of the temporal lobe.

temporal line.d: Line on the outer surface of the frontal bone to which the temporal fascia attaches.

temporal plane.d: Flat area behind Heschl's gyrus; larger in the dominant hemisphere and involved in language processing.

temporal pole.d: Anterior tip of the temporal lobe.

temporal surface of frontal bone.d: Surface forming the front wall of the temporal fossa; temporalis arises here.

temporal surface of greater wing.d: Surface facing the temporal fossa; temporalis arises here.

temporalis muscle.d: Fan-shaped muscle from the temporal fossa to the coronoid process; deep temporal nerves (V3). It closes the jaw, and its posterior fibres retract it.

temporo-occipital branch.d: Supplies the border between the temporal and occipital lobes.

temporoparietalis muscle.d: Thin, variable muscle of facial expression at the side of the galea.

tendinous arch of levator ani.d: Thickening of the obturator internus fascia; the line of origin of levator ani.

tendon of extensor digitorum longus.d: Tendon that splits into four slips on the dorsum of the foot to reach the 2nd–5th toes.

tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longus - e.la: Vagina tendinum musculorum abductoris longi et extensoris brevis pollicis
tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longus - e.d: Sheath around abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis; its narrowing is De Quervain's tenosynovitis (Finkelstein test).

tendon sheath of extensor carpi ulnaris.tr: Tendon sheath of extensor carpi ulnaris
tendon sheath of extensor carpi ulnaris.la: Vagina tendinis musculi extensoris carpi ulnaris

tendon sheath of extensor digiti minimi.tr: Tendon sheath of extensor digiti minimi
tendon sheath of extensor digiti minimi.la: Vagina tendinis musculi extensoris digiti minimi

tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.tr: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and.la: Vagina tendinum musculorum extensoris digitorum et extensoris indicis

tendon sheath of extensor digitorum long.tr: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum longus
tendon sheath of extensor digitorum long.la: Vagina tendinum musculi extensoris digitorum longi pedis
tendon sheath of extensor digitorum long.d: Synovial sheath enclosing the extensor digitorum longus tendons in front of the ankle.

tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longu.tr: Tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longus
tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longu.la: Vagina tendinis musculi extensoris hallucis longi
tendon sheath of extensor hallucis longu.d: Sheath of the big toe extensor tendon in front of the ankle.

tendon sheath of extensor pollicis longu.tr: Tendon sheath of extensor pollicis longus
tendon sheath of extensor pollicis longu.la: Vagina tendinis musculi extensoris pollicis longi
tendon sheath of extensor pollicis longu.d: Sheath of the 3rd extensor compartment, turning around Lister's tubercle.

tendon sheath of extensors carpi radiali.tr: Tendon sheath of extensores carpi radiales
tendon sheath of extensors carpi radiali.la: Vagina tendinum musculorum extensorum carpi radialium

tendon sheath of flexor carpi radialis.tr: Tendon sheath of flexor carpi radialis
tendon sheath of flexor carpi radialis.la: Vagina tendinis musculi flexoris carpi radialis
tendon sheath of flexor carpi radialis.d: Sheath enclosing the tendon in the groove of the trapezium.

tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus.tr: Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus
tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus.la: Vagina tendinum musculi flexoris digitorum longi
tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus.d: Sheath enclosing the tendon in the tarsal tunnel.

tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus.tr: Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus
tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus.la: Vagina tendinis musculi flexoris hallucis longi
tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus.d: Sheath enclosing the tendon in the tarsal tunnel.

tendon sheath of flexor pollicis longus.tr: Tendon sheath of flexor pollicis longus (radial bursa)
tendon sheath of flexor pollicis longus.la: Vagina tendinis musculi flexoris pollicis longi
tendon sheath of flexor pollicis longus.d: Sheath enclosing the thumb flexor tendon from the carpal tunnel to the distal phalanx.

tendon sheath of tibialis anterior.d: The most medial tendon sheath in front of the ankle.

tendon sheath of tibialis posterior musc.d: Tendon sheath just behind the medial malleolus.

tensor fasciae latae.d: Runs from the ASIS to the iliotibial band; flexes and abducts the hip and stabilises knee extension. Superior gluteal nerve.

tenth rib.d: 10th rib: a false (vertebrochondral) rib; its cartilage joins the costal cartilage above.

tentorium cerebelli.d: Tent of dura separating the cerebellum from the occipital lobes; the brainstem passes through its notch, and uncal herniation occurs at this edge.

teres major muscle.d: Runs from the inferior angle of the scapula to the crest of the lesser tubercle; adducts and medially rotates the arm. Lower subscapular nerve.

teres minor muscle.d: Rotator cuff muscle from the lateral border of the scapula to the greater tubercle; rotates the arm laterally. Axillary nerve.

thalamus.d: Large mass of grey matter forming the side walls of the third ventricle; the relay station to the cortex for all senses except smell.

third metacarpal bone.d: The 3rd of the five long bones of the metacarpus; its base articulates with the carpal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.

third metatarsal bone.d: The 3rd of the five long bones of the metatarsus; its base articulates with the tarsal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.

third rib.d: 3rd rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.

third trochanter.d: Extra projection seen in some people at the upper end of the gluteal tuberosity; an attachment area for gluteus maximus.

third ventricle.d: Narrow cavity between the two thalami; connected to the lateral ventricles by the foramina of Monro and to the fourth ventricle by the aqueduct of Sylvius.

thoracic aorta.d: Runs in the posterior mediastinum from T4 to the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm (T12); gives intercostal, bronchial and oesophageal branches.

thoracic vertebra.d: Thoracic vertebra; it carries facets that articulate with the ribs.

thoraco-acromial artery.d: Pierces the clavipectoral fascia and gives pectoral, deltoid, acromial and clavicular branches.

thoracodorsal artery.d: Supplies latissimus dorsi; a free-flap pedicle.

thoracodorsal nerve.d: Arises from the posterior cord and supplies latissimus dorsi; preserved for the flap in breast reconstruction.

thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-arytenoid.d: Fibres extending to the edge of the epiglottis; they widen the laryngeal inlet.

thyrocervical trunk.d: Short trunk giving the inferior thyroid, suprascapular and transverse cervical arteries.

thyrohyoid muscle.d: Short muscle from the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid; supplied by C1 fibres (via the hypoglossal nerve), it raises the larynx or depresses the hyoid.

thyroid articular surface.d: Articular surface on the side of the cricoid; forms the cricothyroid joint with the inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage.

thyroid cartilage.d: The largest cartilage of the larynx; its two laminae join in front to form the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).

tibia.d: Medial, weight-bearing bone of the leg; its anterior border and medial surface are felt under the skin. Its distal end forms the medial malleolus; it is the long bone most often involved in open fractures.

tibial nerve.d: Medial branch of the sciatic nerve; descends from the popliteal fossa into the calf, supplies the posterior compartment muscles and passes through the tarsal tunnel to the sole.

tibial plateau.d: Flat upper surface of the tibia; plateau fractures involve the knee joint.

tibial tuberosity.d: Prominence on the front of the tibia; the patellar ligament inserts here, and Osgood–Schlatter disease occurs here.

tibialis anterior muscle.d: Runs from the lateral surface of the tibia to the medial cuneiform and 1st metatarsal; lifts the foot (dorsiflexion) and inverts it. Deep fibular nerve; its paralysis causes 'foot drop'.

tibialis posterior muscle.d: The deepest muscle of the leg; it inserts into the navicular and tarsal bones, inverts the foot and supports the medial arch. Its dysfunction is the commonest cause of acquired flatfoot.

tibiocalcaneal ligament.d: Part of the deltoid ligament from the medial malleolus to the sustentaculum tali.

tibionavicular ligament.d: Part of the deltoid ligament from the medial malleolus to the navicular.

tonsil of cerebellum.d: Rounded lobule beside the inferior vermis; with raised intracranial pressure it can herniate through the foramen magnum and compress the medulla (displaced downwards in Chiari malformation).

transversalis fascia.d: Fascia lining the inner surface of transversus abdominis; the deep inguinal ring opens in it.

transverse acetabular ligament.d: Ligament bridging the acetabular notch and completing the labrum; vessels supplying the joint enter beneath it.

transverse arytenoid muscle.d: The only unpaired muscle, drawing the two arytenoid cartilages together; it closes the posterior part of the glottis.

transverse cervical artery.d: Crosses the posterior triangle of the neck.

transverse costal facet.d: Facet of the transverse process that articulates with the tubercle of the rib.

transverse facial artery.d: Supplies the parotid gland and the skin of the cheek.

transverse frontopolar gyrus and sulcus*.d: Transverse gyri and sulci at the frontal pole.

transverse head of adductor hallucis.d: Arises from the capsules of the lateral metatarsophalangeal joints; supports the transverse arch.

transverse head of adductor pollicis.d: Arises from the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal; the muscle adducts the thumb. Ulnar nerve; when weak, Froment's sign is positive.

transverse humeral ligament.d: Bridges the intertubercular sulcus, holding the tendon of the long head of biceps in place.

transverse intermuscular septum of leg.d: Fascia dividing the posterior compartment into superficial and deep parts.

transverse ligament of knee.d: Ligament joining the anterior horns of the two menisci.

transverse ligament tubercle.tr: Tubercle for transverse ligament of atlas
transverse ligament tubercle.d: Prominence on the inner surface of the lateral mass; the transverse ligament of the atlas, which holds the dens, attaches here.

transverse occipital sulcus.d: Continuation of the intraparietal sulcus in the occipital lobe.

transverse part of iliofemoral ligament.d: Lateral limb of the inverted-Y ligament; limits lateral rotation and extension.

transverse part of trapezius muscle.d: Middle fibres from the C7–T3 spines to the acromion; retract the scapula.

transverse process.d: Laterally projecting process of the arch; muscles and ligaments attach to it.

transverse ridges.d: Transverse lines on the pelvic surface; they mark the boundaries of the fused vertebral bodies.

transverse sinus.d: Sinus running from the confluence to the sigmoid sinus.

transverse temporal gyri.d: Primary auditory cortex (Brodmann 41, 42) on the surface of the superior temporal gyrus inside the lateral fissure.

transverse tibiofibular ligament.d: Deep part of the posterior tibiofibular ligament; deepens the ankle socket from behind.

transversus abdominis muscle.d: The deepest flat muscle of the abdominal wall; its fibres are horizontal and, by raising intra-abdominal pressure, it works like a corset. Nerves: T7–L1.

transversus thoracis muscle.d: Thin muscle from the inner surface of the sternum to the 2nd–6th costal cartilages.

trapeziotrapezoidal interosseous ligamen.d: Interosseous ligament between the trapezium and trapezoid.

trapezium bone.d: Lateral bone of the distal row; with the 1st metacarpal it forms the saddle joint that allows opposition of the thumb.

trapezoid bone.d: The smallest bone of the distal row; articulates with the base of the 2nd metacarpal.

trapezoid ligament.d: Lateral, quadrilateral part of the coracoclavicular ligament; prevents the scapula sliding medially under the clavicle.

trapezoid line.d: Line on the lower surface of the lateral end; the trapezoid part of the coracoclavicular ligament attaches to it.

trapezoideocapitate interosseous ligamen.d: Interosseous ligament between the trapezoid and capitate.

triangular fovea.d: Upper pit on the anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; it contains glandular tissue.

triangular part of inferior frontal gyru.tr: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus

triceps brachii muscle.d: The only elbow extensor, whose long, lateral and medial heads insert into the olecranon. Radial nerve; triceps reflex C7.

triceps surae muscle.d: Muscle group made up of the two heads of gastrocnemius and soleus; inserting into the calcaneus via the Achilles tendon, it plantarflexes the foot. Tibial nerve (S1–S2).

trigeminal nerve (v).d: Largest cranial nerve; carries sensation from the face (V1, V2, V3) and supplies the muscles of mastication (V3). Trigeminal neuralgia most often affects the V2–V3 territory.

triquetrocapitate ligament.d: Binds the triquetrum to the capitate.

triquetrohamate ligament.d: Binds the triquetrum to the hamate; contributes to midcarpal stability.

triquetrum bone.d: Pyramid-shaped medial bone of the proximal row; articulates with the pisiform on its palmar surface.

triradiate cartilage.d: Y-shaped growth cartilage joining the ilium, ischium and pubis in the acetabulum in childhood; it ossifies at puberty.

trochanteric bursa of gluteus maximus mu.d: Between the iliotibial band and the greater trochanter; trochanteric bursitis most often occurs here.

trochanteric bursa of gluteus medius mus.d: Bursae beneath the gluteus medius tendon.

trochanteric bursa of gluteus minimus mu.d: Bursa beneath the gluteus minimus tendon.

trochanteric fossa.d: Fossa on the medial surface of the greater trochanter; obturator externus inserts here.

trochanteric insertion.d: Common insertion area of the deep hip rotators around the greater trochanter.

trochlea of humerus.d: Pulley-shaped articular surface at the lower medial end of the humerus; forms the hinge joint with the ulna.

trochlea of phalanx of foot.d: Pulley-shaped distal head of a toe phalanx; forms a hinge joint with the next phalanx.

trochlea of phalanx of hand.d: Pulley-shaped head of a finger phalanx; forms the interphalangeal hinge joint.

trochlea of superior oblique muscle.d: Fibrocartilaginous pulley at the superomedial corner of the orbit; the superior oblique tendon turns through it.

trochlea of talus.d: Pulley that sits in the mortise between the tibia and fibula; being wider in front, the joint is stable in dorsiflexion.

trochlear fovea.d: Pit at the superomedial corner of the orbit; the trochlea of superior oblique attaches here.

trochlear nerve (iv).d: Supplies superior oblique; the only and thinnest cranial nerve leaving the back of the brainstem, with the longest intracranial course.

trochlear notch.d: Large notch that grips the trochlea of the humerus.

trochlear spine.d: Small spine in the trochlear fovea; holds the pulley of superior oblique.

tuber of vermis.d: Lobule in the posterior inferior vermis.

tubercle of iliotibial tract.d: Prominence on the lateral condyle (Gerdy's tubercle); the iliotibial band inserts here.

tubercle of rib.d: Prominence behind the junction of the neck and shaft; articulates with the transverse process.

tubercle of scaphoid bone.d: Prominence on the palmar side of the scaphoid; the flexor retinaculum attaches to it, and it is felt at the front of the wrist.

tubercle of trapezium bone.d: Prominence on the palmar side of the trapezium; the FCR tendon passes in the groove beside it.

tuberculum sellae.d: Elevation in front of the hypophysial fossa.

tuberosity for coracoclavicular ligament.d: Lower lateral surface of the clavicle; both parts of the coracoclavicular ligament attach here.

tuberosity of cuboid bone.d: Ridge on the plantar surface of the cuboid; the fibularis longus tendon passes in the groove in front of it.

tuberosity of distal phalanx of foot.tr: Tuberosity of distal phalanx of foot
tuberosity of distal phalanx of foot.d: Rough expansion at the tip of a distal toe phalanx; supports the soft tissue of the toe tip.

tuberosity of distal phalanx of hand.tr: Tuberosity of distal phalanx of hand
tuberosity of distal phalanx of hand.d: Expansion at the tip of a distal finger phalanx; supports the finger pulp and nail bed.

tuberosity of navicular bone.d: Projection on the medial surface of the navicular; the main insertion of tibialis posterior.

tuberosity of ulna.d: Rough area below the coronoid process; brachialis inserts here.

twelfth rib.d: 12th rib: a floating rib; its front end is free and ends among the muscles of the abdominal wall.

tympanic membrane.d: Thin membrane separating the external and middle ear; the umbo and cone of light are seen on otoscopy, and paracentesis is done in the posteroinferior quadrant.

tympanic part of temporal bone.d: Part forming the bony wall of the external acoustic meatus.

ulna.d: Forearm bone on the little finger (medial) side; with the olecranon and coronoid process it grips the trochlea of the humerus to form the elbow joint.

ulnar artery.d: Descends on the medial side of the forearm; passes through Guyon's canal to form the superficial palmar arch.

ulnar collateral ligament.d: Spreads like a triangular fan from the medial epicondyle to the ulna; resists valgus stress and tears in baseball pitchers.

ulnar collateral ligament of wrist joint.d: Ligament from the ulnar styloid process to the triquetrum and pisiform.

ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.tr: Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris
ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.la: Caput ulnare musculi extensoris carpi ulnaris
ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.d: Arises from the posterior border of the ulna; the muscle inserts into the base of the 5th metacarpal, extending and ulnarly deviating the hand.

ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.tr: Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris
ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.la: Caput ulnare musculi flexoris carpi ulnaris
ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.d: Arises from the olecranon and the posterior border of the ulna; the muscle inserts into the pisiform, flexing and ulnarly deviating the hand. Ulnar nerve.

ulnar nerve.d: Arises from the medial cord and passes behind the medial epicondyle (the 'funny bone'); supplies most intrinsic hand muscles and sensation of the medial one and a half fingers. Injury causes a claw hand.

ulnar notch.d: Notch at the lower end of the radius; forms the distal radio-ulnar joint with the ulnar head.

ulnar styloid process.d: Process at the posteromedial end of the ulnar head; the articular disc attaches to it.

ulnocapitate ligament.d: Palmar ligament running from the ulnar side to the capitate.

ulnolunate ligament.d: Palmar ligament running from the TFCC to the lunate.

ulnopisiform ligament.d: Small ligament between the ulna and pisiform.

ulnotriquetral ligament.d: Palmar ligament running from the TFCC to the triquetrum.

uncinate process of first thoracic verte.d: Small process on the body of T1 resembling those of the cervical vertebrae.

uncinate process of vertebra.d: Process on the upper lateral edge of a cervical vertebral body; it forms the uncovertebral (Luschka) joint, and osteophytes here can compress nerve roots.

upper canine.d: Tooth at the corner of the mouth with the longest root; tears food. The root of the upper canine can reach up to the corner of the eye.

upper first molar tooth.d: The first permanent tooth to erupt (age 6); it has a broad chewing surface and three roots.

upper first premolar.d: Premolar with two cusps; begins crushing food. In the upper jaw it usually has two roots.

upper lateral incisor.d: Single-rooted incisor next to the central incisor.

upper medial incisor.d: Sharp-edged, single-rooted middle front tooth; cuts food by biting. It erupts at 6–8 years in the permanent dentition.

upper second molar tooth.d: Second molar erupting around age 12; it grinds food.

upper second premolar.d: Second premolar; usually single-rooted, with no counterpart in the milk teeth (it replaces the milk molars).

uvula of vermis.d: Lobule of the inferior vermis between the two tonsils.

vaginal process of sphenoid bone.d: Thin process on the lower surface of the body; articulates with the vomer.

vagus nerve (x).d: Cranial nerve with the widest distribution, carrying parasympathetic fibres to the neck, chest and abdominal organs and motor fibres to the pharynx and larynx; the efferent limb of the gag reflex.

vastus intermedius muscle.d: Deep head of quadriceps beneath rectus femoris, arising from the front of the femur.

vastus lateralis muscle.d: The largest head of quadriceps; forms the lateral part of the thigh and is used for intramuscular injections.

vastus medialis muscle.d: Medial head of quadriceps; its lower oblique fibres (VMO) pull the patella medially and prevent lateral dislocation.

ventral parts of lateral intertransversa.tr: Ventral parts of lateral lumbar intertransversarii
ventral parts of lateral intertransversa.la: Partes ventrales musculorum intertransversariorum lateralium lumborum
ventral parts of lateral intertransversa.d: Anterior fibres of the small muscles between the lumbar transverse processes.

vermian fossa.d: Fossa seen in some people at the lower end of the internal occipital crest; the vermis of the cerebellum lies in it.

vertebra.d: Bone of the spine; made up of a body and an arch.

vertebra c3.d: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process.

vertebra c4.d: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process.

vertebra c5.d: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process.

vertebra c6.d: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process. Its anterior tubercle (carotid tubercle) is the point against which the common carotid artery can be compressed.

vertebra c7.d: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process. Its spinous process (vertebra prominens) is the first prominent bump felt at the base of the neck; the vertebral artery usually does not pass through its foramen transversarium.

vertebra l1.d: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes. The spinal cord usually ends at the conus medullaris at the L1–L2 level.

vertebra l2.d: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes.

vertebra l3.d: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes.

vertebra l4.d: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes. The line joining the highest points of the iliac crests (Tuffier's line) usually crosses the L4 spine; the reference for lumbar puncture.

vertebra l5.d: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes. The largest vertebra; its body is taller in front (wedge-shaped) and forms the lumbosacral angle with the sacrum. Spondylolisthesis is most common at L5–S1.

vertebra t1.d: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. Its body has a whole facet for the 1st rib and a half facet for the 2nd rib.

vertebra t10.d: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. It usually carries only a single facet for the 10th rib.

vertebra t11.d: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. It has a single rib facet; there is no facet on its transverse process.

vertebra t12.d: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. Its body resembles a lumbar vertebra; one of the vertebrae most often fractured at the thoracolumbar junction.

vertebral arch.d: Arch surrounding the vertebral foramen from behind; made up of the pedicles and laminae.

vertebral artery.d: First branch of the subclavian artery; rises through the transverse foramina of C6–C1, enters through the foramen magnum and joins its partner to form the basilar artery.

vertebral foramen.d: Opening surrounded by the body and arch; it contains the spinal cord and its membranes.

vertebral vein.d: Descends with the vertebral artery through the transverse foramina.

vestibular nerve.d: Part carrying balance information from the semicircular canals, utricle and saccule; its inflammation is vestibular neuritis.

vestibular nuclei.d: Four nuclei receiving balance information; they regulate eye movements and posture through the vestibulospinal tracts and the MLF.

vestibular surface of tooth.d: Surface of a tooth facing the cheek or lip.

vestibule.d: Middle part of the inner ear; with the utricle and saccule it senses linear acceleration.

vestibulocochlear nerve (viii).d: Carries hearing and balance; a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) at the cerebellopontine angle causes one-sided hearing loss.

vitreous body.d: Transparent gel filling the space between the lens and the retina.

vocal process.d: Forward-projecting process of the arytenoid; the vocal ligament attaches to it.

vomer.d: Thin single bone forming the posteroinferior part of the nasal septum.

white matter of spinal cord.d: Anterior, lateral and posterior funiculi containing the ascending and descending tracts.

white matter of telencephalon.d: Myelinated fibres beneath the cortex: association, commissural and projection fibres.

wing of central lobule.d: Wings of the central lobule extending into the hemisphere.

xiphoid process.d: Lowest, cartilaginous-to-bony tip of the sternum; it gives attachment to the diaphragm and the rectus sheath, and lies below the compression area during CPR.

zona orbicularis.d: Circular capsular fibres encircling the femoral neck like a ring.

zonular fibres.d: Fibres suspending the lens from the ciliary body; they weaken in Marfan syndrome, causing lens dislocation.

zygomatic bone.d: Bone forming the prominence of the cheek and the lateral wall of the orbit; with the temporal bone it forms the zygomatic arch.

zygomatic margin of greater wing.d: Margin that articulates with the zygomatic bone.

zygomatic process of frontal bone.d: Lateral process that articulates with the zygomatic bone; it forms the upper lateral margin of the orbit.

zygomaticus major muscle.d: The 'smiling muscle', running from the zygomatic bone to the corner of the mouth; pulls the corner of the mouth up and out.

zygomaticus minor muscle.d: Raises the upper lip and deepens the nasolabial fold.
